body:
Colony, the buffet restaurant at The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore, has turned its seven kitchens over to a Japan Week menu until Sunday 25 October, with prices from S$108++ for weekday lunch to S$998++ for a Sunday brunch poured with Cristal. The Japan Week started on 16 October and covers every lunch, dinner and brunch session in the 10 days.
Japan Week runs at Colony from 16 to 25 October 2026. Photo: The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore
The menus mix izakaya-style Japanese dishes into Colony’s usual international and local spread rather than replacing it. The Ice Bar, The Grill and Rotisserie, The Steam Basket, The Wok, The Tandoor, The Fruit Stall and The Patisserie all stay open, and the local roast meats and wok dishes are still on the line.
Four price points, four menus
Each session has its own Japan Week menu, and the price climbs with the seafood.
• Lunch, Monday to Saturday, 12pm to 2.30pm: S$108++ an adult, S$54++ for children aged six to 12. Sashimi, nigiri, a truffle tuna roll and chilled buckwheat noodles, plus kimchi pork fried rice and pork belly yaki udon from The Wok.
• Dinner, Sunday to Thursday, 6pm to 10.30pm: S$130++ an adult, S$65++ a child. Adds freshly shucked oysters, snow crab, a negitoro avocado bruschetta, chashu omurice, menchi katsu and tori karaage with nanban sauce.
• Seafood dinner, Friday and Saturday, 6pm to 10.30pm: S$152++ an adult, or S$250++ with free-flow Barons de Rothschild Ritz Réserve Brut NV Champagne; S$76++ a child. Adds langoustine, kaki furai fried oysters, unagi omurice, a truffle seafood okonomiyaki and Singapore chilli crab with golden mantou.
• Sunday Champagne Brunch, 12pm to 3.30pm, on 18 and 25 October: S$258++ with Barons de Rothschild Champagne, S$698++ with Dom Pérignon 2015, or S$998++ with Cristal 2015 and 30g of Oscietra caviar. Children aged six to 12 pay S$129++, and those aged three to five pay S$64.50++.
The Ice Bar adds snow crab and oysters at Japan Week dinners from S$130++. Photo: The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore
The Sunday brunch is the headline
The brunch has the longest Japan Week menu. A whole hon maguro, or bluefin tuna, is carved live, and The Ice Bar has king crab, lobster claw, langoustine and yabby next to the oysters, with amaebi and tsubugai among the sashimi. Ankimo and soft shell crab rolls, unagi don with ikura and chirashi don sit next to the sushi.
The hot line has Boston lobster with uni sauce, misoyaki black cod and Hokkaido scallop with sake beurre blanc. An à la minute chef’s table cooks foie gras with smoked eel and a crystal fin chawanmushi topped with Oscietra caviar and uni foam.
At S$258++, the cheapest brunch tier is S$128 more than a Sunday-to-Thursday Japan Week dinner. The difference buys the live tuna carving, the luxury seafood and free-flow Champagne, wine, cocktails and beer.
The Japan Week Sunday brunches on 18 and 25 October start at S$258++. Photo: The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore
Booking and details
Seats for the two brunches are limited. All prices are before service charge and GST, and the menus are subject to change. The Japan Week menus include pork dishes.
Colony is at 7 Raffles Avenue, inside The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore, a short walk from Promenade MRT station. Reservations are by phone on 6434 5288 or by email to rc.sinrz.restaurantreservations@ritzcarlton.com. Japan Week ends after dinner on 25 October.
summary: Colony at The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore has a Japan Week menu at every buffet session from 16 to 25 October, from S$108++ for lunch to S$998++ for the Cristal brunch.
title: Colony at The Ritz-Carlton runs a Japan Week buffet to 25 October, from S$108++

A long-standing hidden gem at First Centre in Serangoon North is set to close its doors at the end of this month. Bid farewell to London Grill Japanese & Western , which will have its last day of operation on 31 Oct 2026 after 10 years in business.
Credit – Joanne Lim via FB
The impending closure comes as a result of higher rental costs alongside other issues the owners face. Owned and operated by a very friendly and kind elderly couple, the stall has gained a loyal following over the years for its highly affordable Japanese and Western fare, with prices starting from just S$2.50 .
Credit – Joanne Lim via FB
The friendly auntie taking orders shared that the closure marks a permanent retirement for the couple, with no plans to relocate elsewhere. Here are some comforting dishes they serve up.
Credit – Joanne Lim via FB
The Black Pepper Chicken Chop (S$6) features a generously-sized piece of chicken, smothered in a thick black pepper sauce. The chicken chop is accompanied by a combination of 3 different sides. Pictured is a bed of shredded lettuce, with coleslaw and a pile of crispy, golden-brown fries. Their menu pictures the chicken chop being served with baked beans instead, much like other old-school Western joints.
Credit – Joanne Lim via FB
They also offer an old-school style Chicken Burger (S$2.50) , which comes with a deep-fried chicken patty dressed in sweet chilli sauce on a bed of lettuce and mayo. For just S$2.50 , it’s a classic snack for all ages that’s bound to put a smile on your face.
Look out for some of their Japanese dishes as well, including the Chicken Teriyaki Set (S$5) and the Chicken Katsu Don (S$4.30) .
Beyond serving food, the couple has been an anchor for the workers at First Centre. Through their warmth and consistent service, they have forged good relationships with most of the people working in the building, making their upcoming departure a significant loss for the community. Head down to support auntie and uncle and wish them a happy retirement before their last day!
Hougang Oyster Omelette & Fried Kway Teow — Owners retiring, successor wanted
summary: London Grill Japanese & Western at First Centre in Serangoon North will cease operations on 31 Oct 2026 after 10 years of business due to rising rental costs and retirement. Serving affordable Japanese and Western fare starting from S$2.50, the stall has long acted as a community anchor for building workers. This overview is ideal for local diners and regulars looking to support the owners before their final service.
title: London Grill Japanese & Western closing permanently after 10 years as elderly owners retire

Chef Johanne Siy’s debut restaurant, Árō, prices its Chef’s Tasting Menu at S$268++ a head at 15 Mohamed Sultan Road, while over at The Singapore EDITION on Cuscaden Road, Tanica charges S$48++ for a three-course weekday lunch. Árō ‘s cooking is Creator’s Cuisine, built on lesser-known ingredients from across Asia-Pacific. Tanica cooks Southeast Asian food over a Josper grill and in the wok, meant for sharing.
Photo: Árō
The two sit at opposite ends of a night out near Orchard and River Valley, one a counter-led tasting room and the other a hotel dining room open from breakfast. Further out on Dempsey Hill, Petra opens its Mediterranean dining room on 24 October .
Árō on Mohamed Sultan Road
The name joins two words: arō, Latin for “to plough”, and áro, “love” in the dialect of the chef’s hometown. The room is small, with a counter for 10, two tables of four and a private dining room holding four tables of two. Keiji Ashizawa Design worked it in walnut, rattan, stone and bronze, and the art on the walls comes from Siy’s own collection.
Photo: Árō
For now there is one menu, the Chef’s Tasting Menu at S$268++. A shorter tasting menu is marked as coming soon, without a price yet.
Árō opens Thursday to Monday, with lunch from 12pm to 3pm and dinner from 6pm to 10pm, and closes on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Bookings go through SevenRooms, and the restaurant also takes enquiries at info@arosingapore.com.
Tanica at The Singapore EDITION
Tanica is the EDITION’s all-day restaurant at 38 Cuscaden Road, organised around herbs, spices and fire. Breakfast runs from 6.30am to 10.30am and lunch from 12pm to 2.30pm. Dinner is 6pm to 10pm from Monday to Thursday, and to 10.30pm from Friday to Sunday.
Photo: Tanica
The weekday set lunch, Monday to Friday, is three courses for S$48++ with coffee or tea, served within 60 minutes. Booking through SevenRooms comes with three hours of complimentary parking. A wagyu hanger steak main adds S$10, a glass of wine S$15 and a Saicho osmanthus sparkling tea S$12.
On Sundays the restaurant runs Sunday Table at S$98 a person, S$168 with wines, or S$198 with Louis Roederer Collection 246 champagne.
What the Tanica menu costs
The à la carte menu leans on hawker classics reworked for the grill and wok. Hokkaido sea urchin pie tee is S$30. Char kway teow, Singapore laksa noodles and Hainanese chicken rice are S$28 each. The char kway teow contains pork, and other dishes on the menu do too.
Photo: Tanica
The larger plates climb quickly. An asam pedas seafood risotto and Iga Bakar Kicap, a 72-hour wagyu short rib, are S$58 each. A one-kilogram grilled grouper is S$138, the XO mapo tofu with lobster S$128, and a 500g rib eye S$178.
Prices at both restaurants carry a 10 per cent service charge and GST.
Tanica takes reservations on +65 6329 5000 as well as SevenRooms.

body:
Apam balik filled with Biscoff, Milo Dinosaur or even pistachio kunafa ? Singapore’s Munchi Pancakes is giving the familiar snack a rather interesting spin, and it’s opening first outlet in Malaysia this October . The halal-certified brand will make its way to AEON Mall Tebrau City , JB, bringing over 20 flavours to Malaysia after growing to more than 42 outlets across Singapore.
Credit – Munchi Pancakes
The story began in 2016, when childhood friends Calvyn and Au decided to turn their shared love for Min Jiang Kueh , also known as apam balik , into a business. Starting with a hawker stall in Yishun, the pair began experimenting with different fillings and pancake skins, giving the traditional snack a fresh spin.
Credit – Munchi Pancakes
Of course, the classics haven’t gone anywhere. Peanut , Coconut , Red Bean , Kaya and Black Sesame are still on the menu, alongside sweeter picks such as Belgian Chocolate , Milo Dinosaur , Biscoff and Oreo Cheese . For tea lovers, there’s also Matcha , Thai Milk Tea and Earl Grey to try.
Feeling a little more adventurous? Pistachio Kunafa , Kopi Gao and Pineapple Cheese offer unexpected twists on the usual fillings. Even the pancake skins get a change-up, making this more than just your standard apam balik run.
Credit – Munchi Pancakes
If you prefer your snacks in smaller portions, Mini Munchi comes in boxes of 6 , perfect for sharing or sampling a few flavours. Traditional Min Jiang Kueh is also available for those who prefer to keep things classic.
They offer vegan options, too. With old-school favourites sitting alongside more unconventional combinations, Munchi Pancakes’ JB debut gives apam balik fans in Malaysia plenty to explore. The big question is, what flavours are you looking forward to the most?
JB’s famous Red House reopens with a century-old biscuit shop from Ipoh & Nanyang cafe
summary: Munchi Pancakes, the halal-certified Singapore brand known for reinventing traditional apam balik, is opening its first Malaysian outlet at AEON Mall Tebrau City, Johor Bahru, in October 2026. With over 20 flavours ranging from peanut and kaya to Biscoff and pistachio kunafa, plus Mini Munchi, vegan options and traditional Min Jiang Kueh, it offers a useful option for snack lovers keen to sample both familiar fillings and newer combinations.
title: SG’s Munchi Pancakes to open 1st Malaysian outlet in JB with 20+ apam balik flavours

Briyani is one of the most satisfying dishes around, so why not have as much as you like? Indian Saaga on Race Course Road is offering unlimited briyani for S$38++ for two, which works out to S$19++ per person. Now that’s a steal! This deal is only available from 12pm – 6pm (Mon to Sat).
Credit – Google
Located at 38 Race Course Road, Indian Saaga is a halal-certified North Indian restaurant serving tried-and-true classics. It prides itself on affordable prices, so this deal comes as no surprise.
Some of you might recognise Indian Saaga, as it shares founders with The Song of India. That restaurant became Singapore’s first Indian restaurant to receive a Michelin star in 2016. Indian Saaga focuses on a family vibe, with big tables and plenty of seats for larger groups.
This deal, however, breaks that convention, as it is intended for pairs. So if you have a special someone, or just a buddy you want to hang out with, this deal is perfect for you.
Credit – Indian Saaga via Instagram
The deal includes 90 minutes of unlimited briyani , with a choice of chicken or mutton. Diners also get unlimited mutton curry, papad and raita , plus a 1-time serving of plain, butter or garlic naan .
Credit – Indian Saaga via Instagram
Briyani aside, the menu also has kebabs , curries and fresh naans .
Some of their popular dishes are the Mutton dum biryani (S$18++) , Chicken tikka masala (S$16++) and Goan fish curry (S$16++) . So, if you happen to feel peckish for something else, peruse the menu and maybe try something new.
Indian Saaga is open daily from 12pm – 11pm, and reservations can be made online at indiansaaga.com or via WhatsApp
at +65 9789 9004.
This deal is available for a limited time only, from 12pm – 6pm (Mon to Sat) . Head down to Indian Saaga for a hearty briyani meal.
Singapore’s highest-rated biryani has 4.9 stars — is it really that good?

The Starbucks Winnie the Pooh collection arrives in Singapore on 20 October 2026, just as the chain rolls out a Halloween line-up built around a Black Cat Frappuccino and a trio of cat-themed collectibles. It is a busy week for Starbucks collectors.
Image: Starbucks Singapore
Starbucks Winnie the Pooh collection: what is in it
Starbucks has teamed up with Disney for a limited-edition range marking 100 years of Winnie the Pooh. The collection draws on the Hundred Acre Wood, with drinkware and lifestyle pieces that nod to friendship, kindness and everyday connections.
Image: Starbucks Singapore
The drinkware line-up includes 12oz ceramic mugs, 16oz stainless steel tumblers (one themed around Tigger), cold cups and a 20oz stainless steel cold cup. There is also a beehive-shaped ceramic mug that looks made for desk duty.
Image: Starbucks Singapore
Collectors can also look out for Starbucks Bearista keychains and phone straps dressed as Winnie the Pooh, Piglet, Eeyore and Tigger, plus a Winnie the Pooh-themed reusable bag that folds into a matching pouch.
When and where: the collection goes on sale from 20 October 2026 in stores, and on LazMall at 12pm, while stocks last.
Image: Starbucks Singapore
Black Cat Frappuccino and Halloween collectibles
For Halloween, Starbucks is serving the Black Cat Frappuccino Blended Beverage. It combines raspberry blackcurrant with dark mocha, topped with whipped cream, dark mocha sauce and cat ear and tail-shaped chocolate pieces. It is available from 20 to 31 October at all stores and via Mobile Order & Pay, and can also be ordered through Starbucks Delivers, GrabFood and Foodpanda, while stocks last.
Image: Starbucks Singapore
The Halloween Spooky Meowchestra collection is inspired by retro cartoon illustrations, with a cast of tuxedo and black cats playing in a whimsical orchestra. It spans tumblers, mugs and everyday essentials.
Image: Starbucks Singapore
The Black Cat Starlit Party collection pays tribute to the Starbucks Black Cat, joined by owl and Bearista companions in Halloween outfits. Beyond drinkware, it includes a phone stand and a reusable cup bag with plush. Both Halloween collections are available in stores, on the Starbucks Online Store and on LazMall, while stocks last.
Image: Starbucks Singapore
Catching up on recent Starbucks news? Read about the Protein Cold Foam launch , the autumn drop with Roasted Macadamia drinks and the 30 Years of Shared Moments campaign . Release details and images courtesy of Starbucks Singapore.
summary: Starbucks Singapore launches its Disney Winnie the Pooh collection and a Black Cat Frappuccino on 20 October 2026.

Vincenzo Capuano’s Robertson Quay pizzeria is running a Monday to Friday bottomless lunch of starters, pasta, pizza and gelato for S$28 a person, built around the Caputo Nuvola dough the 2022 World Pizza Champion ferments for up to 30 hours.
The weekday lunch is built around Caputo Nuvola dough fermented for up to 30 hours. Photo: Vincenzo Capuano
The set sits at #01-12 The Pier at Robertson, 80 Mohamed Sultan Road, a short walk from Fort Canning MRT. Lunch is noon to 3pm with last order at 2.30pm. Dinner runs 6pm to 11pm every day, with food last order at 10pm and drinks at 10.30pm. Thirty per cent of seats stay open for walk-ins; the rest take reservations on the restaurant’s site or by phone on +65 6485 9153.
What the S$28 lunch puts on the table
Guests move through four courses. Starters are a Caesar salad with grilled chicken breast, taralli, vine tomatoes and parmigiano, or Cotoletta di Pollo, a baked chicken thigh cutlet finished with fior di latte, basil and olive oil. Pasta options are mezze maniche with Vincenzo’s tomato salsa, aubergine and ricotta, or house-made porcini ravioli in a truffle cream sauce.
Pizzas are cut with scissors so the cornicione stays airy. Photo: Vincenzo Capuano
The pizza course offers Diavola alla Nonno Enzo with spicy Napoli salami, an Aglio e Olio cartwheel with sliced garlic and bird’s eye chilli, or Pesto Basilico with fior di latte, vine tomatoes, pine nuts and parmigiano. Dessert is gelato al cioccolato fondente or gelato al pistacchio. Pizzas are cut with scissors rather than a wheel so the airy cornicione stays open rather than crushed.
Bottomless drinks are a Monday to Friday add-on at S$28.
The dough and the ranking
Vincenzo Capuano is a third-generation Neapolitan pizzaiolo. His Singapore flagship sits at number 13 on the 2025 50 Top World Artisan Pizza Chains list, held the Best Marketing Award in 2024, and carries two Spicchi from Gambero Rosso. The dough uses Caputo Nuvola Super flour and rests for up to 30 hours, which the kitchen pitches as soft, airy and light on the stomach.
Capuano is the 2022 World Pizza Champion with a Singapore flagship at Robertson Quay. Photo: Vincenzo Capuano
Friday to Sunday evenings add a separate free-flow tipples ticket at S$48 for 90 minutes of Hugo and Aperol spritzes, Tropical Spritz, Mimosa, prosecco, Negroni and Sbagliato, with a Moët and Chandon upgrade at S$40 a person. That offer is nights only and sits beside the weekday lunch, not inside it.
Where it is and how to book
The Pier at Robertson is at 80 Mohamed Sultan Road in Robertson Quay. Fort Canning MRT Exit B is a seven-minute walk along Mohamed Sultan Road. Bookings run through vincenzocapuano.sg. The Monday to Friday S$28 bottomless lunch is the weekday ticket; evenings and weekends follow the a la carte pizza list and the free-flow tipples menu instead.
summary: Vincenzo Capuano at The Pier at Robertson runs a Monday to Friday bottomless lunch of starters, pasta, pizza and gelato for S$28, noon to 3pm.
title: Vincenzo Capuano’s weekday bottomless lunch costs S$28 at Robertson Quay

The cheapest mains are the Pomodoro , Aglio Olio , and Cheesy Crumble , which go for $7.90 before the discount. With the 1-for-1 deal, you’re only paying $3.95 for each portion—a steal in this economy!

body:
Osteria Da Su opens at 163 Telok Ayer Street on Friday 23 October 2026, with 25 sharing plates from S$14++ that fold Korean accents into classic Italian cooking. The casual osteria is the newest restaurant from NAE:UM Group , next door to its one-Michelin-starred Korean fine-dining sibling NAE:UM, and is run by Korea-born Chef Suji Park.
Photo: Osteria Da Su
Opening week is dinner only. From 16 November the kitchen plans Monday to Saturday lunch and dinner. Bookings go through the restaurant’s reservation link at bit.ly/dasu.
Who is cooking
Park has cooked Italian food for close to 20 years, including stints in Bergamo, Milan and Sicily, three years at three-Michelin-starred Da Vittorio in Bergamo, two years at Claudio Sadler’s Milan trattoria, and time on the opening team of Massimo Bottura’s Gucci Osteria in Seoul. She and NAE:UM chef founder Louis Han met as students at Korea Tourism College and have been friends for 16 years. The Telok Ayer unit next to NAE:UM came up for lease in June 2026, and they opened the Italian room together.
The name works in two languages. In Italian, “da Su” reads as an osteria from Su. In Korean, “da su” means many people, which is how the kitchen frames a neighbourhood table rather than a tasting counter.
What is on the menu
Handmade pasta sits at the centre of the list. Spaghetti alle vongole is S$28++, built on asari clam stock with Korean water parsley (minari) in place of Italian parsley, and the shells removed before service. Tortelli di galbi jjim is S$30++, with Korean braised pork inside handmade tortelli and sage butter. Farfalle all’amatriciana is S$24++, finished with guanciale chips brushed in gochujang bulgogi sauce.
Photo: Osteria Da Su
Smaller plates start lower. Korean pepper fritto, a fried gochu chilli stuffed with prawn and ricotta and served with doenjang mayonnaise and balsamic soy, is S$14++. Zucchini bruschetta is S$12++, and insalata condiglione with a Korean soy-marinated egg is S$18++. For dessert, dalgona tiramisu is S$14++, a classic mascarpone and savoiardi tiramisu topped with housemade dalgona honeycomb, and salame di cioccolato is S$10++.
Photo: Osteria Da Su
The room
The restaurant seats 34: eight at the kitchen counter, 16 on banquettes and ten in a raised lounge. The fit-out mixes arched openings, terracotta floors and warm wood with a cleaner Korean line, and framed photographs Park took in Italy hang on the walls. Diners walk past the open kitchen on the way in.
Telok Ayer Street is a short walk from Telok Ayer and Downtown MRT stations. The group’s other sibling restaurant is GU:UM, a modern Korean steakhouse, which makes the Italian room its first non-Korean concept in Singapore. Prices carry a 10 per cent service charge and GST. The restaurant is not halal-certified.
summary: NAE:UM Group's casual Italian osteria opens at 163 Telok Ayer Street on 23 October 2026, with 25 sharing plates from S$14++ led by Chef Suji Park.
title: Osteria Da Su opens on Telok Ayer on 23 October with Korean-accent Italian plates from S$14++

body:
Though it has reportedly been operating for decades, Restoran Ahmad Muzakin in Sri Petaling has found itself under the social media spotlight in recent years— most notably in 2023. The eatery, known for its “ Muslim-friendly ” claypot chicken rice, came under fire from segments of the Malaysian Muslim community following allegations that it used rice wine in its cooking, despite the Muslim-owned restaurant’s claim that the dish was halal .
The rumour was swiftly debunked, but not without consequence. The restaurant allegedly closed temporarily for internal improvements before reopening and continuing business as usual. According to the Malay Muslim couple behind Restoran Ahmad Muzakin, JAKIM had inspected the premises twice and found no trace of non-halal ingredients. The restaurant is also said to be in the process of applying for official halal certification from JAKIM.
Despite the controversy, Restoran Ahmad Muzakin appears to have weathered the storm. It continues to draw a steady crowd of loyal patrons from all races and walks of life, reflecting the diverse appetite of Malaysians.
What I tried at Restoran Ahmad Muzakin
Now, I usually walk you through each dish one at a time. This time, however, I simply can’t contain myself. Just look at the glorious spread that graced our table. Despite there being only 3 of us in the restaurant — my dining partner, a lone diner, and myself — the wait was surprisingly long. But patience, as it turns out, has its delicious rewards: all of our dishes arrived at once, piping hot and ready to impress.
First up, the undisputed bestseller: the Chicken Claypot Rice (RM10 for a small) . And I say “small” with a raised eyebrow. It was far more generous than expected, easily enough for two light eaters or one ravenous foodie.
The pot came to the table still sizzling , wisps of steam curling into the air like a prelude to something comforting and soul-warming. Just when we thought the theatrics were over, more steam emerged as we mixed the contents, releasing a clean, savoury aroma that made my mouth water in real time.
The rice was gently coated in soy sauce and sesame oil, accented by spring onions and juicy cuts of chicken drumstick. The colour was on the lighter side, but the first bite revealed a different story. I was immediately met with the sharp saltiness of salted fish. It caught me off guard, if I’m being honest.
Foong Foong Yong Tau Foo: Ampang’s iconic YTF since 1974 with crowd-favourite fried & steamed delights
I figured I hadn’t stirred the rice well enough, so I gave it another good mix and went in again. The flavours mellowed slightly, but the salted fish still took centre stage— and not in a good way. The rice itself was made of imperfect grains— tiny yet toothsome, not mushy in the least, which actually worked in its favour.
It paired beautifully with the tender chicken, which was remarkably soft and clean-tasting. Most of the flavour came from the sauces it was cooked in, but that didn’t take away from how enjoyable each bite was.
Next, we moved on to the Claypot Duck Rice (RM15) , which comes in small— it had the same generous portion as the chicken version.
As we stirred it up, I noticed the rice was visibly darker, promising a bolder flavour profile. I couldn’t resist diving right in. Unlike the chicken, this dish leaned into the warm, fragrant notes of ginger, which I instantly preferred. There was no overpowering salted fish here (thank God).
The duck itself was abundant and beautifully done, tender with just the right amount of fatty bits. In fact, some pieces were so soft, they could easily be mistaken for chicken at first bite. But the flavour was definitely richer and more robust. A spoonful of the raw onion– kicap –bird’s eye chilli mix on top elevated it even more.
To complete the feast, we added a side of Chicken Wings (RM10 for 2 pieces) . We saved them for last, but they held their crunch like champs. Even after cooling down, the skin remained delightfully crispy, encasing meat that was juicy and well-seasoned. A side of chilli sauce was provided, but honestly? These wings didn’t need it.
Final thoughts
While Restoran Ahmad Muzakin remains no stranger to controversy and continues to stir debate online, there’s no denying one thing— the food holds its own. Each dish we tried was thoughtfully prepared, well-seasoned, and satisfying.
For the price point, it was an above-average meal that is hearty, flavourful, and worth the wait. Whatever your stance on the chatter, there’s something to be said for a restaurant that lets its food speak louder than the noise.

It’s official: we’ve compiled the best Christmas dinners, brunches and other festive menus in Singapore so you don’t have to. We love the holiday season, but between sussing out the best Christmas gifts in Singapore to making space in our cals for all the festive parties we can’t wait to attend, choosing the right restaurant for Christmas in Singapore can feel like just another item on a lengthy to-do list. That’s why we’ve done the searching for you – from grand hotel buffets to intimate festive dinners, keep scrolling for the best Christmas feasts to book, complete with some of the best Christmas cocktails in Singapore for your yuletide toast.
Psst: we’re still in the midst of updating this roundup for 2026, so keep your eyes peeled!
Where to go for Christmas dinner in Singapore
1. Fire
Photography: Fire via Facebook
Fancy a sky-high festive date amid the clouds? Make your way to level 55 of Ion Orchard for Fire’s Deck The Flames Christmas dinner. Priced at $158 each, this flame-kissed five-course menu features unique dishes inspired by traditional asado flavours and modern techniques. In the spirit of giving, you’ll also get a complimentary festive postcard to send to someone special anywhere in the world.
Nibble on Argentine rustic potato and egg salad, and roasted Patagonian red prawn and octopus empanada for a start. Next, choose from show-stopping mains like stuffed turkey ballotine and curanto-style slow-cooked lamb shoulder. Desserts are non-negotiable, so save space for Argentinian bread pudding and chocolate-dipped alfajores.
Best for: A sky-high Argentinian feast
Dates: 24 & 25 Dec 2026
Prices: $158 per pax (minimum two pax)
Timings: Daily, 12pm to 3.30pm & 6pm to 10.30pm
Address: Level 55, 2 Orchard Turn, Singapore 238801
Visit Fire
2. Andaz
Photography: Andaz Singapore
You can count on Andaz Singapore to deliver a sumptuous feast this festive season. The hotel’s sophisticated steakhouse, 665°F, welcomes you to an intimate setting that overlooks the stunning Marina Bay. The feast begins from 1 December with the 665°F festive table set menu with the likes of Applewood-smoked sustainable Atlantic salmon, Black North Onyx tenderloin and more.
Alternatively, come by on Christmas Eve and Christmas Day for specially curated set menus available for both lunch and dinner. The multi-course menu is a treat for both the eyes and the palate, featuring premium ingredients across every course. Think pine-smoked Puglian burrata, Jerusalem artichoke cappuccino, Australian pure black crossbred F1 wagyu striploin and kombu-aged Mediterranean sea bream. Vegetarian options are available, too. For a decadent finale to the experience, indulge in a festive dessert and petit fours, featuring roasted Japanese persimmon, mascarpone mousse, Fewster’s honeycomb and vanilla bean ice cream.
Best for: A delectable multi-course feast
Dates : 24 and 25 Dec 2026
Prices : 665°F festive table set menu from $98 per adult; Christmas Eve and Christmas day lunch from $128 per adult and dinner from $148 per adult
Timings : 12-12.30pm for lunch; 6pm-10pm for dinner
Address : 5 Fraser Street, Singapore 189354
Visit Andaz Singapore

Photography: Violet Oon via Facebook
If you need motivation to trudge through deadlines during the holiday season, let Violet Oon’s Christmas set lunch be it. Call up your work besties for a date at its lush Dempsey location to enjoy a jolly lunch set with local and Peranakan flavours.
Warm up your palate with a comforting bowl of pong tahu soup, before tucking into sharing plates of kueh pie tee, beef rendang, babi pongteh, nasi kuning rice and more. Finish off with a classic fruit cake drizzled with Brandy butter sauce.
Best for: A mid-week festive booster

Holiday feasting and juicy steaks go hand-in-hand at Meadesmoore. This modern steakhouse in the CBD brings out a formidable centrepiece: the Westholme F1 wagyu bone-in striploin MS 4/5 (600g). Hailing from northern Australia, this cut is best known for its fine, even marbling and lingering beef flavour.
To amp up the earthy and smoky flavours, the steak is cooked over charcoal, and finished with sea salt flakes and black Kampot pepper. Enjoy it with sauce charcutiere, blistered vine tomatoes and confit garlic. With limited availability, we recommend placing a pre-order when making your reservation.

Matsuya is bringing affordable gyudon bowls to Singapore
Image credit: Japan Journeys
Joining the growing list of Japanese food chains making their way to Singapore is Matsuya , one of Japan’s most popular gyudon chains. The fast food chain has a whopping 1200 locations across Japan and has been expanding internationally since 2018. Currently, they have over 1,500 outlets globally!
Image credit: u/kccz123 via Reddit
With its first Singapore outlet opening at Suntec City in November 2026 , the brand is set to give established names such as Sukiya and Yoshinoya a run for their money.
Suntec City Food Guide: 25 Places For Cheap Kimbap, Matcha Parfait And More
While not much is known about the Singapore outlet, Matsuya is famous in Japan for its affordable gyudon bowls. A full meal there is reported to cost between ¥400 and ¥1000 , which converts to about S$3.25 to S$8.10 .
The current exchange rate is ¥ 1 = ~S$0.0081 as of 19 October 2026.
Image credit: Japan Journeys
Some popular dishes from the Japan outlets are, of course, the classic Beef Bowl (¥480) , stewed with onions in a sweet soy sauce, Beef Bowl with Tomato and Cheese (¥710), Beef Bowl topped with Grated Radish and Ponzu Citrus Soy Sauce (¥580) and more.
Image credit: Toru via Google Maps
Matsuya also offers curry bowls, including Beef Curry and Rice (¥680), Beef Curry with Cheese (¥880), and Beef Curry with Hamburg Steak (¥950) for something heartier.
Similar to many restaurants here, Matsuya uses a kiosk system that allows customers to order and pay easily.
For more delicious Japanese fare, check out these best Japanese cafes in Singapore . And we can’t mention Japan without bringing up matcha; here’s a list of the best matcha cafes according to us!
Address: 3 Temasek Boulevard, #B1-125 (Tower 2), Singapore 038983
Opening hours: TBD

Food prices are the highest they’ve ever been. Even a simple lunch in Singapore suffers from wildly high prices. Which is why I was surprised to see Mexican-inspired dishes , famous for their expensive price tag, only cost S$4.90 a piece at The Daily Fiesta in Bedok . And it’s Halal-certified as well.
But are they actually good? I went down to their second outlet to have a taste myself. I’d like to think I make pretty awesome tacos and quesadillas , so I think I’m qualified for the task ahead.
What to order at The Daily Fiesta
With the prices being so affordable, I decided to try a few of their staples. I ordered the Cajun Chicken Taco (S$4.90) , Crispy Fish Taco (S$4.90) , Chicken Quesadilla (S$13) and Beef Quesadilla (S$14) . All of them include a side of salsa and guacamole.
Let’s start with the Cajun chicken taco (S$4.90) . This one was quite a letdown compared to the other dishes. Firstly, the slaw. I found it too sweet, and it overpowered a lot of the other ingredients, namely the chicken. On top of that, they also added corn, which only made it sweeter. I would suggest replacing the slaw with regular iceberg lettuce for a more balanced flavour.
I also felt the quail egg on top was a little unnecessary, but that’s just me.
The Crispy Fish Taco (S$4.90) was much better. It had a beautifully crispy battered fish laid on top of their slaw. On top of that was a creamy sauce with a bit of spice, black ebiko and fried shallots. The flavours were a medley of sweet, salty and tart, all working in harmony. The black ebiko also added a nice popping texture when I bit into it. All in all, one of the better fish tacos I’ve had in recent memory.
Lavi Tacos: Hidden Mexican gem at Chinatown with rare birria tacos & delicious taco platters
Now, let’s move on to the quesadillas.
The Chicken Quesadilla (S$13) was pretty solid. They seared a cheese crust within the tortilla, giving an intense grilled cheese flavour. The Cajun chicken flavour was more prominent here, but I felt it still lacked intensity. As a whole, though, it was still very yummy, especially when dipped in their salsa . I would recommend increasing the spices for the Cajun chicken or marinating it for longer. Also, while the salsa was tangy with a refreshing tomato flavour, the guacamole was a bit on the sour side. It could use a bit of salt to bring out the avocado flavour.
Now this is a quesadilla! The Beef Quesadilla (S$14) was everything I wanted it to be and more. It still had the same formula: a cheese crust inside the tortilla, stringy and soft cheese, and a protein. However, the meat? Ay dios mio , it was perfectly seasoned. It had smoky, slightly spicy and rich flavours when melted together with the cheese. The meat had a bite to it, not too soft, which was my original worry.
It had to have a high fat content as well, as there was so much grease at the bottom. This is a telltale sign of a good quesadilla. Even the tortilla seems darker than the chicken version. I suspect the grease really absorbed into the tortilla, making the beef flavour very prominent in every bite.
Who is The Daily Fiesta best for?
Honestly, anyone who likes a decent Mexican lunch. I struggle to find someone who doesn’t fit in this category. Even vegetarians have options, as they have a mushroom quesadilla and taco. On top of that, they also have a variety of pastas, sides like corn ribs and much more. If you’re looking for a delicious lunch, you can’t go wrong with The Daily Fiesta.
How to get to The Daily Fiesta
Luckily for all of us, their Bedok outlet is near Bedok Mall. There is also a bus stop a few metres away called After Heartbeat @ Bedok , with several buses leading there. Alternatively, you can take the MRT to Bedok. The Daily Fiesta is only an 8-minute walk from the MRT station.
Do we recommend The Daily Fiesta?
Good food and better prices. It’s going to be hard for me not to recommend this spot. The amount of options alone makes this place worth a visit. But if I had to point to one specific dish, it has to be their Beef Quesadilla (S$14) . It really is a level above the rest, though I’m sure you will find your own favourites when you get there.
Do note that they sell out fast . I arrived an hour after opening, and their Beef Bolo Tacos were already sold out and I just managed to get their beef quesadilla , so clearly the beef is a fan favourite.

Where to get authentic Mexican food in Singapore?
summary: The Daily Fiesta’s second outlet in Bedok serves Mexican-inspired tacos from S$4.90 and quesadillas at S$13 to S$15, each with salsa and guacamole. The crispy fish taco and beef quesadilla stand out, while the Cajun chicken taco is let down by an overly sweet slaw. Popular items such as the beef bolo tacos can sell out within an hour of opening.

Doughnut lovers, good news! I’m donut? , the Japanese doughnut brand that has drawn long queues and a cult following, is coming to Singapore this December .
Credit: I’m donut?
This will be I’m donut?’s Singaporean debut, and it will open its first store at ION Orchard’s Basement 2 . For those who have been waiting for the popular doughnut brand’s arrival, they are probably looking forward to the signature nama doughnuts they have become so beloved for.
Credit: I’m donut?
These doughnuts, which have made waves across social media, are known for their “pillowy”, light, fluffy, and extra-soft texture. This is the result of founder Ryouta Hirako’s reimagination of what a doughnut could be.
Complementing the airy texture of the doughnuts are a variety of creamy fillings and delicate toppings, which bring satisfaction and surprise with every bite. You will experience a springy delight that melts in your mouth, no matter which flavour you go for.
Credit: CapitaLand
I’m donut? first opened its doors and built a fanbase in Japan in 2022. In just 4 years, it has brought its nama goodness to cities like New York, Taipei, and Seoul. Now, it’s finally coming to our Little Red Dot, ready to spread its sweet joy to more doughnut fans internationally.

Nervous about meeting your partner’s parents? Start with one great meal at a time. Try these 5 restaurants that’ll win their heart and bellies.
1. Maison Yoshoku
Meeting your other half’s parents for the first time? Start with a great restaurant, then amuse them with dessert. Maison Yoshoku ’s interior combines muted tones, soft lighting, and Japanese details, making conversations easy. Here are a few dinner picks worth trying – a selection of modern Yoshoku dishes and Izakaya-style plates.
Photo by Adoncia Ho (Confirm Good)
You’ve got to try the Trevally Crudo (S$24) , paired with house-made yuzu ponzu, wasabi oil for that nice kick, and heirloom tomatoes. Good for sharing, the Maison Yoshoku Bouillabaisse (S$34) is a Japanese take on French seafood stew paired with sourdough bread.
End off the meal at the dessert Omakase Bar . Choose from the 3-course (S$25) , 5-course (S$35) , or 7-course (S$45) – whichever you think suits your in-laws and will be in-law-approved.
The dessert Omakase Bar is available from 3pm to 10pm daily , with limited slots . Click here to make your reservations !
Maison Yoshoku

If your goal tonight is to be the favourite child-in-law, then Summer Pavilion is a Michelin-starred Cantonese restaurant that speaks for itself. It’s a polished fine-dining experience, which is a plus or minus depending on the occasion.
Photo by Adoncia Ho (Confirm Good)
Trust us on their Double-boiled Superior Bird’s Nest served in a whole coconut (S$108) , warm, hearty, and nourishing. With many proteins to choose from, the Barbecued Ibérico Pork with honey sauce (S$48) was a showstopper, and the must-try Poached Rice with Canadian Lobster Meat (S$32) . Good food, calm ambience , and servers who know what they’re doing. Dill is a warm, vibrant space to enjoy delicious, casual Scandinavian food . They turn up the elegance with a Set Menu and à la carte options , with dinner and drinks served from Wednesday to Saturday , 4pm to 11pm .

We’d suggest trying the Waffle with Löyrom (S$32) , Toast Skagen with Fermented Turnips (S$28) , Wagyu Onglet with Tarragon and Kailan (S$49) , and Wild-caught Fish with Potato and Leeks (S$49) .

Storage spaces in Singapore
We all dream of living in that TikTok house tour-worthy house, filled with pretty furniture and not a shred of clutter to ruin the aesthetic. But when you’re working with 1,300sqft or less and a lifetime’s worth of barang , even the best storage hacks and space-saving furniture can only do so much.
The answer to all your storage needs is to rent a self-storage unit in Singapore . Whether you just need a small locker for documents, a space to keep your furniture during a home reno, or a long-term storage solution while you’re out of the country being a digital nomad, there are plenty of affordable storage spaces in Singapore from as low as $4/month.
Here are 12 of the best storage spaces in Singapore to stash your stuff, so your home stays looking like a Pinterest board.
What is a storage space rental?
Storage space rental has become increasingly popular, especially in Singapore, since most of us have limited space in our homes. You can use these spaces to store almost anything you want – from excess household items to even large pieces of furniture.
Storage spaces can also be used by businesses to keep extra inventory. However, there are some things which aren’t allowed, such as chemicals, radioactive materials, hazardous substances – you get the picture.
The pricing of each storage unit is heavily dependent on various factors – the storage facility, the size that you’re renting, and the duration of your rental. Generally, for most of these facilities, the longer you store your items, the lower the rates. The size of these rental spaces ranges from a box’s worth of storage space to the equivalent of a bedroom.
Although you are paying money for the space, you aren’t allowed to do anything you want with it. This means that you aren’t allowed to live there or set up your office. The space should be used solely for storage purposes only.
1. Lock+Store
50% off air-con units at Ayer Rajah & flexible terms across 16 locations
Image credit: Lock+Store
Wherever you are on the island, there’s likely a Lock+Store nearby. With 16 outlets from Sembawang in the North to Tanjong Pagar in Central Singapore – just minutes from the new Cantonment MRT on the Circle Line – and Kaki Bukit in the East, it offers air-con and non-air-con units for homes and businesses alike.
Image credit: Lock+Store
The lobang to hop on right now is Lock+Store Ayer Rajah, where brand new air-con units are going at 50% off , while stocks last. It’s minutes from one-north MRT and convenient for those staying in or working from Dover, Clementi, and Bukit Timah. Units range from 11-200sqft, enough for a few boxes or a whole reno’s worth of furniture. The wide aisles, loading bays, and free parking also make moving in a much smoother and less dreaded process.
Come and go 24/7 with a PIN code or by using the handy mobile app, with CCTV watching round the clock. Trolleys, ladders, and pallet jacks are free to use, and you can rent a storage space from 1 month to 1 year, with the option to renew as you please. Online sellers can also use Ayer Rajah’s free drop-off and pickup point, so you won’t need to be there when a delivery arrives.

They’re Singapore’s largest valet storage operator, with in-house professional movers who can go to you, pick up your items and keep them safe with extra protective wrapping, then eventually send them right back to you.
Their valet storage facilities start from as small as 20sqft, all the way to 1,000sqft spaces; when it comes to self-storage options, there’s 24/7 secured CCTV surveillance, and options for both ambient and air-conditioned units. Dating events in Singapore happen more frequently than you think! With the rise of in-person social events , we’re clearly not the only ones craving some real-life socialising. And for the members of the lonely hearts club, you’ve likely exhausted your dating app matches. How about trying something new with a little in-person chit-chat? All you have to do is find one that catches your eye (the same way your new beau will).
Dating events in Singapore
1. SomeoneNew: Love edition
Photography: Culture Sg
Culture Sg never disappoints when it comes to social events in Singapore. Branching out from Above 30 Club comes SomeoneNew, a place for all 30-somethings and up to meet like-minded people. Because we all know as you get older, making friends gets ridiculously harder. The collective is hosting its first singles’ event, and you have two ways to meet your match – approach the cutie across the bar or leave it up to fate with a questionnaire. And there’ll be plenty of games to keep things interesting along the way.
When: 21 October 2026, 7.30pm to 10.30pm
How much: Tickets start from $30; includes one drink
Where: SomeoneNew: Love edition , Rasa Space, 9 Raffles Place, Singapore 048619
2. Type Mixers: Angels & Devils
Photography: Type Mixers via Instagram
Hey, Gen Zs. We haven’t forgotten about you, and neither has the team at Type Mixers. What started as a desire to ditch the dating apps and to “do it for the plot” soon turned into regular themed gatherings to put singles into a room to see what happens. And then, strangers became friends while sparks flew. Sounds like a pretty magical journey to us! You can also join the fun by keeping an eye out on the team’s social media pages for updates.
For the month of October, it’s no surprise that we’re getting another Halloween-themed mixer! This time, you’re getting a mystery match, secret identity, and a hidden mission. Come dressed as either a devil or an angel and enjoy tarot reading, snap photos at a photo booth, sip Halloween-themed drinks, and meet a special someone along the way.
When: 30 October 2026, 7.30pm to 11pm
How much: Tickets start from $48 for ladies and $55 for men; pre-registration required
Where: Type Mixers: Angels & Devils , location revealed only to confirmed attendees
3. Never Strangers
Photography: Never Strangers
After its launch in 2024, the demand for Never Strangers events skyrocketed and clearly has no signs of coming down! As one of the first offline social event collectives to come about, the team has hosted a number of social events, from dating mixers to platonic dinners. If you want to be part of this cool kids club, register your details on the website, and you’ll be added to the guest list! Events are curated based on age, vibe, and interest, so you’ll be hand-picked for an event that’s catered to you.
The next edition of Never Strangers will be hosted on a yacht. AKA, the perfect opportunity for you to break out a cute swimsuit that hasn’t seen water in a hot minute. Sailing out of Keppel Bay, you’ll get to enjoy free-flow cocktails by Garage, games, and the classic algorithm match reveal before returning to the dock.
When: Hosts events monthly; yacht event on 24 October 2026, 3pm to 7pm
How much: Varies with each event
Where: Never Strangers, register online
4. Thursday
Photography: Alfatah Bilal Afdam via Pexels
Let us introduce you to Thursday; the biggest IRL dating app in the world. It’s less about the dating app itself and more about the in-person events. Because they care about getting you out the door to meet someone rather than spend your time endlessly matching. All you have to do is pick your city and you can pick from a tidy list of events happening in your area.
We’ve already spotted a variety of singles’ mixers you can join depending on what your vibe is! Enter a game of mystery mini golf, head to a rooftop bar for conversations with stunning city views, or enter a Halloween-themed encounter.
When: Various dates
How much: Ticket costs vary with each event
Where: Thursday , locations vary
5. The Stupid Cupid’s Singles’ Mixer
Photography: The Stupid Cupid via Instagram
From the same crew who brought you the dating series Maybe It’s You is The Stupid Cupid. The team will be hosting its first singles mixer, taking the dating experience offline, putting the same thoughtfulness and love into it. There is a strict vetting process you’ll have to go through if you want to participate. But this means the crowd will be extra curated to ensure a good vibe.
When: 1 November 2026, 7pm till late
How much : Free admission; registration required, closes 18 October 2026

Winnie the Pooh x Starbucks collection
One of the most iconic cartoon characters we grew up with is Winnie the Pooh. With his golden-yellow fur and signature red shirt that barely contains his chubby belly, the lovable bear has remained a childhood favourite for generations.
Now, Starbucks is bringing a little of that nostalgia to coffee runs with a limited-edition Winnie the Pooh x Starbucks collection launching in Singapore on 20th October 2026 . Here’s everything you can find, including their prices.
What’s in the collection?
Image credit: Starbucks Singapore
Inspired by Hundred Acre Wood, the fictional setting of Winnie the Pooh, this collection features a range of drinkware and lifestyle accessories donning the beloved characters and motifs from the cartoon.
Stainless steel tumblers
I mage credit: Starbucks Singapore
Whether you’re looking to keep your cold beverages chilled in Singapore’s heat or bring your morning coffee along for the commute, these stainless steel tumblers do the job.
Each tumbler holds 473ml of liquid and comes in 3 designs. The Pooh 16oz Stainless Steel Tumbler​ ($49.90) keeps things simple with a clean design featuring the bear himself, while the Pooh 16oz Stainless Steel Tigger Tumbler ​($59.90) and Pooh 16oz Stainless Steel Eeyore Tumbler​ ($49.90) editions stand out with bolder designs inspired by his close companions.
Cold cups of different materials
Designed for cold beverages, these cold cups are both practical and stylish. Their lids are made to fit reusable straws, making them ideal for sipping on the go.
Image adapted from: Starbucks Singapore
Choose from 4 cold cup designs made from different materials. The Pooh 12oz Plastic Cold Cup ($36.90) stands out with its transparent dome lid, which houses a decorative yellow Pooh figure surrounded by colourful, confetti-like pieces.
Image credit: Starbucks Singapore
If you prefer a bigger cup, the Pooh 16oz Double Wall Piglet Glass Cold Cup ($42.90) is another option, especially if Piglet is your favourite character. The orange honey-drip pattern gives the cup a playful touch, along with the light wooden lid and matching straw. For a final cute detail, the straw is topped with a honey-dipper-inspired stopper.
Image adapted from: Starbucks Singapore
There’s also the Pooh 20oz Stainless Steel Cold Cup ($46.90) , which features a group shot of Pooh and all his forest buddies. For those who need more room for their drinks, the Pooh 24oz Cold Cup ($36.90) is the largest option in the collection.
Ceramic mug & water bottle
Image adapted from: Starbucks Singapore
For a mug with a little more character, the Pooh 12oz Ceramic Mug ($34.90) has a rounded, barrel-like shape and raised horizontal ridges, giving it a sculpted look. Its warm peach and creamy beige tones add a subtle pop of colour to your mug collection.
Rounding out the drinkware collection is the Pooh 24oz Plastic Water Bottle ($46.90) , a practical pick for everyday hydration, which also comes with a reusable straw.
Other merchandise such as phone straps & multi-use bag
Image credit: Starbucks Singapore
Beyond drinkware, the collection also includes a few cute accessories, especially for those who can’t resist the blind box craze. The Pooh Phone Strap Blind Box ($14.90) puts a Pooh-themed spin on the trend, with 4 possible designs featuring Pooh, Piglet, Eeyore, and Tigger in different colours.
But if you are not keen on leaving the odds of getting your favourite character to chance, the Pooh Phone Strap Gift Set ($59.60) comes with all 4 designs , allowing you to bring home the whole Hundred Acre Wood gang.
Image credit: Starbucks Singapore
Another set you can pick up is the Pooh Mini Bearista Bear Set ($75.90), which comes with a Bearista bear plushie and 4 interchangeable Pooh and Friends-inspired costumes . It also has its own “home” – a honey-pot-shaped pouch with a transparent front window to show off your adorable companion. Complete with a keychain ring, you can easily clip it onto your bag and bring your little Bearista along for your daily outings.
Image credit: Starbucks Singapore
Finally, the Pooh Pouch with Reusable Bag ($39.90) is a handy pick for days when you need extra space for your shopping. The Pooh-themed bag folds neatly into a matching pouch, making it easy to tuck into your handbag and whip out whenever you need more room.
How can I purchase the Winnie the Pooh x Starbucks collection?
This special Pooh collection will be available in Starbucks stores and on LazMall from 12pm on 20th October 2026 , while stocks last.
Get your hands on the Winnie the Pooh x Starbucks collection when it launches
With Pooh-inspired collectibles lining the shelves, your next Starbucks run might cost a little more than just your usual coffee, especially if you leave with a few cute additions in tow. But it’ll all be worth it when you get to bring home a little piece of the Hundred Acre Wood.

body:
Rawr Cafe is a new tiger-themed cafe in Jalan Besar
Wunderfolks , the mastermind behind Oh Wunder Cafe and Cafe Barco , is back with another concept. Its latest venture, Rawr Cafe , opened in Jalan Besar on 17 October 2027 . Unlike the other two concepts, this new cafe offers locally inspired brunch fare in a cute tiger-themed setup.
The cafe interior features adorable red-and-white tiger graphics.
You’ll also find a display of merchandise, from their house-made kaya to a tiger-inspired cap and stickers.
The menu features local flavours in the form of Western brunch classics. Some must-tries recommended by the cafe are the Singaporean Breakfast Latte ($8++) , Nasi Lemak Chicken Burger ($18++), Laksa Cream Halibut ($24++), Gula Melaka Pandan Cloud ($8++), Tiger Bomb ($12++), and Soft Shell Crab Chilli Pasta ($23++).
The Soft Shell Crab Chilli Pasta was served with a whole crab. The tomato-based sauce was sweet, tangy, and mildly spicy. Personally, it tasted more like regular red pasta sauce than chilli crab.
The soft-shell crab appeared to be lightly battered and deep-fried, giving it a crispy exterior. Beneath the shell was tender, fleshy crab meat with some creamy roe. The crab had some natural sweetness and brininess that came through nicely.
The Nasi Lemak Chicken Burger was extremely hearty, layered with fried chicken, fresh lettuce, and cucumber, then topped with ikan bilis and sambal for that bold umami flavour.
For sides, we got the Prawn Paste Chicken ($15++) . It tasted like regular har cheong gai—the exterior was fried till crisp, coating the greasy, tender chicken wing. I noticed that the chicken meat was a little pinker than what I was used to, so I thought it could’ve been cooked for longer.
We also got two of the signature drinks: the SG Breakfast Latte, a creamy pandan latte, and Tiger Bomb, espresso topped with orange foam.
Image credit: Rawr Cafe
You can also choose to top your drinks with an adorable Raw Tiger Cookie Topper for just $2++!
The SG Breakfast Latte caught our eye with its e foamy “fried egg” on top. It’s served with a crunchy slab of kaya toast, which was light, fragrant, and perfect for soaking up the latte. FYI: the “yolk” in the foam is kaya-flavoured!
The Tiger Bomb had an intense citrusy flavour, thanks to the addition of the orange-infused foam. Paired with espresso, it made for a unique flavour combination that’s worth trying.
Overall, Rawr Cafe is definitely worth a visit if you love cutesy cafes. The SG Breakfast Latte is my favourite in terms of taste and appearance, so give it a go!
Cafe-hoppers, here are some new restaurants and cafes that opened in October 2026 ! And for more authentic local eateries, here is the ultimate Singapore food guide .
Address: 134 Jalan Besar, Singapore 208852
Opening hours: Daily 9:30am to 9pm

Tampines 1 Halloween Scaretacular 2026
It’s a great time to be an East-dwelling horror buff, because Tampines 1 has major frights and thrills in store for shoppers this Halloween season. Gear up for a Halloween gamified maze on the mall’s rooftop, priced at $10/pax or free to redeem for those who shop and dine at Tampines 1.
Get spooked in a Halloween gamified maze
Combining the thrills and immersive challenge of a haunted house, maze, escape room, and horror movie, Tampines 1’s Halloween gamified maze thrusts you into a living, breathing horror scenario.
Headlining this year’s festivities is Toy Factory 444 , with signature scares that have made Tampines 1’s Halloween Scaretacular a must-visit annual event, now intensified with scarier encounters, darker twists, and more heart-pounding moments than ever before.
Building on these fan-favourite frights, this year’s edition reimagines the traditional haunted maze as an immersive gamified adventure, where visitors become part of the story as they navigate the eerie factory, uncover clues and complete missions to escape the nightmare that awaits within.
Location: Tampines 1 Rooftop
Date: 17th-18th Oct, 22nd-25th Oct, 29th Oct-1st Nov
Time: 7pm-11pm, last entry at 10.30pm
Admission: $10/pax. Alternatively, spend min. $100 to redeem 2 tickets or min. $150 to redeem 4 tickets. Redemption period between 25th Sep-1st Nov, max. 3 same-day receipts per redemption.
Redeem a blind box plushie & customise it for free
[Update: This event has ended as of 11th October]
Keeping with the creepy – and potentially cursed – toy theme, Tampines 1’s Main Atrium will also be transformed into a toy factory concept. Try your hand at customising your own little doll, which is an immersive experience in and of itself as you sit there stitching and glueing away. Gasp… Are you the toy factory worker in this scenario?
This is a unique collaboration between Box Hunt – a blind box haven – and the Singapore Fashion Council .
Grumpipi’s Whispers To Dreamland plushie series.
Image credit: Calembou
Remember how we said hitting a minimum spend of $150 across up to 3 same-day receipts can get you a set of 4 tickets to the Halloween gamified maze? From 5th-11th October , you’ll also get to redeem a blind box plushie, with options ranging from the Grumpipi and OPanDee Zombie Party series – both spookily adorable in their own way.
The OPanDee Zombie Party series.
Image credit: HappiBox
With your lil cute-creepy companion by your side, head to the customisation zone to adorn your new plushies with decorations and accessories as you see fit. The customisation activity is free, with recycled materials provided by the Singapore Fashion Council. Guidance will also be provided onsite, so don’t worry about being left out of this fun activity if you’re not the best at sewing.
Location: Tampines 1 Main Atrium
Date: 5th-11th Oct
Time: 10am-10pm for blind box redemption, 12pm-9pm for customisation activity
Get spooked at theTampines 1 Halloween Scaretacular 2026
Whether you’re braving Toy Factory 444’s scares on the rooftop or stitching up a cute-creepy companion in the Main Atrium, Tampines 1’s Halloween Scaretacular 2026 has plenty to keep East-siders – and visitors from all over the country – entertained this October.
Round up your bravest kakis and time your shopping haul right, and you could walk away with maze tickets and a blind box plushie in one go. Just don’t blame us if your new plushie starts giving you funny looks at night…

body:
7 Paintings at Conrad Singapore Marina Bay turns dinner into a hands-on art class. The new seven-course dinner show, called 7 Paintings: The Art of Dining, invites guests to paint, play and puzzle their way through works by Michelangelo, Banksy, Picasso, Pollock, Warhol, Dali and Van Gogh.
Image: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay
Seven artists, seven courses, one table
The experience runs for about two and a half hours at Lounge by the Pool on Level 4. Each course is dedicated to one artist and a defining work, and each asks diners to take part by painting, listening to short stories or solving a riddle.
Some of the courses are built for play. Banksy’s Girl with Balloon is stencilled onto the plate, ready for guests to finish with spray cans. Pollock’s course brings a palette of spinach coconut, beetroot and pumpkin puree to paint with. The finale is a chocolate painting on citrus cake, where chocolate-chilli, white chocolate raspberry and tart strawberry sauces let guests add finishing touches to Van Gogh’s iconic work.
Image: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay
The concept sits naturally in the hotel, which holds a collection of more than 3,400 sculptures and paintings by local and international artists.
Menus and prices
There are four menus, each following the same seven acts. The Classic Menu (S$190++) features pan-seared snapper and grilled Black Angus beef fillet. The Premium Menu (S$230++), created by Executive Chef Thomas Jakobi and the culinary team and found exclusively at the hotel, includes flamed Murray River cod and Wagyu beef tenderloin with smoked morels.
Image: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay
The Vegetarian Menu (S$190++) reinterprets all seven courses, from beet carpaccio to roasted falafel. The Children’s Menu (S$99+) offers kid-friendly dishes across all seven courses for children aged 6 to 12. Free Flow Drinks Packages are available as add-ons from S$20++.
Image: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay
Dates, times and how to book
Dinner starts at 7pm on Thursdays, Fridays and Sundays. Saturdays have two sessions, at 5pm and 8.30pm. From 1 November, the experience expands to Wednesdays, also from 7pm.
Reservations can be made through 7paintings.com/en/singapore . The hotel is at Two Temasek Boulevard, Singapore 038982.
Another immersive dinner is coming to town: 4 Elements arrives at ANTI:DOTE, Fairmont Singapore from 4 November . For more from the hotel, see its Race Week specials .
summary: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay launches 7 Paintings: The Art of Dining, a seven-course dinner show where guests paint through works by Banksy, Pollock and Van Gogh.
title: 7 Paintings: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay Launches a Seven-Course Art Dinner Show

The 4 Elements immersive dining experience makes its Singapore debut at ANTI:DOTE, Fairmont Singapore, from 4 November 2026. Part dinner, part theatre, it pairs projection mapping and interactive challenges with a five-course menu inspired by Earth, Fire, Water and Air.
Image: InterDine
A dinner set in the Kingdom of Hoshena
Produced by immersive dining specialist InterDine, 4 Elements follows runs in Hong Kong and Edmonton, Canada. It sits in the same fantasy universe as Banquet of Hoshena, which has been staged in Singapore before.
The story unfolds in the Kingdom of Hoshena, ruled by Queen Serena, where the four elements have lived in harmony until her mischievous sister Nyxara escapes from imprisonment. Animated characters, tabletop projections and interactive challenges turn diners into participants, with each course opening a new chapter.
Image: Fairmont Singapore / InterDine
The five-course menu
Fairmont Singapore’s Director of Culinary, Nicholas Issel, created the menu. It opens with Parmesan and rosemary popcorn and an amuse-bouche of dried beef, heirloom tomato and Queen olive.
Earth arrives as an edible garden of petite vegetables, rainbow roots and greens from the hotel’s rooftop aquaponics farm, with heirloom carrot dressing. Fire brings Wagyu beef fillet with potato espuma, truffle crunch and ANTI:DOTE’s steak sauce. A lemongrass elixir, guava sorbet and drunken plum interlude follows, before Water serves roast black cod, Hokkaido scallop, scallop cracker and XO fried rice.
Air closes the evening with a Grand Cru cocoa dessert featuring fruit orchard, woody vanilla cocoa fruit, almond sable tart and fruit fluid gel, alongside an Earl Grey chocolate drink. The Premium menu adds shaved black truffle and lobster tail, and vegetarian and children’s menus are available.
Cocktail flight from ANTI:DOTE
ANTI:DOTE Head Mixologist Adonis Endozo Reyes has created an optional four-cocktail flight, one for each element. Earth combines Codigo 1530 tequila, mezcal, cherry and blood orange. Fire uses Jura 12 whisky, lemon myrtle, Moscato, sage and honey, and is finished with flames. Water pairs Glenfiddich 12 with almond milk, salted apple and peat smoke, while Air is a lighter mix of cucumber-infused Bacardi white rum, berries and citrus, finished with edible air.
Image: Fairmont Singapore / InterDine
Prices, timings and booking
Menus are priced at S$188++ per person for Classic and Vegetarian, S$248++ for Premium, and S$108++ for the Children’s menu, which is open to children aged six and above and includes free-flow orange and apple juice. The cocktail flight is an extra S$88++ per person. Diners also get 15% off drinks at ANTI:DOTE before and after their meal.
Shows run on selected dates through April 2027. Performances are on Wednesdays and Thursdays at 7pm, Fridays and Saturdays at 7pm and 9pm, and Sundays at 1pm and 7pm, with extra timings on selected dates over the festive period. The experience takes roughly two hours. Reservations are handled by InterDine at booking.4elementsdinner.com/Singapore .
Image: Fairmont Singapore / InterDine
ANTI:DOTE is on Level 1 of Fairmont Singapore, Singapore 189560, a short walk from City Hall and Esplanade MRT stations. Looking for other splurges this season? See our guide to early-bird Christmas turkey takeaways at hotels , or how Aro prices its tasting menu .
Image: Fairmont Singapore / InterDine
summary: InterDine brings 4 Elements to ANTI:DOTE at Fairmont Singapore from 4 November 2026, with a five-course menu from S$188++ and an optional cocktail flight.
title: 4 Elements Immersive Dining Debuts at ANTI:DOTE, Fairmont Singapore From 4 November

Huaiyang set lunches start at S$98++ a person at Imperial Treasure Moutai House , the restaurant Imperial Treasure has opened for reservations inside Moutai House at The Fullerton Waterboat House.
Scallops with preserved mei cai are part of the S$98++ Lunch Course A. Photo: Imperial Treasure
The 45-seat dining room is at #03-01, 3 Fullerton Road, with nine tables, one private room and a wine cellar. It opens daily from 11am to 3pm and 6pm to 10pm. The nearest MRT station is Raffles Place.
The idea is Moutai at the dinner table, poured with the food rather than saved for a toast. Imperial Treasure cooks Huaiyang cuisine, the eastern Chinese tradition of careful knife work and slow braises, alongside the sour and spicy flavours of Guizhou, the province where Kweichow Moutai is distilled.
Five set menus, S$98++ to S$398++
Lunch Course A, at S$98++ a person, is the entry point. It opens with a Huaiyang trio of marinated pig’s head, Yangzhou-style fried cod and pickled radish skin, then shredded beancurd with uni in thick soup, braised pork meat ball with abalone, scallops sauteed with preserved mei cai, Yangzhou fried rice and a seasonal dessert.
Lunch Course B is S$138++ a person, for a minimum of two. It adds yellow-braised shark’s fin with seafood and bamboo pith, shrimp with honey peas in black truffle oil, and Jiangnan braised pork with a five-head fresh abalone.
Pork meat ball soup in Yangzhou style is on the a la carte soup list. Photo: Imperial Treasure
Dinner runs on three courses, all for two or more. Course C is S$188++ with steamed soft-shell turtle in chicken oil and braised pork with Hokkaido sea cucumber. Course D is S$328++, with shark’s fin in sour soup and eight-head Australian dried abalone. Course E, at S$398++, includes egg white sauteed with caviar and a 15-head South African dried whole abalone with superior fish maw.
The a la carte premiums
Luxury items are priced by the piece. A whole premium sea cucumber is S$500, or S$250 for half. Superior fish maw is S$66 a piece, a whole Hokkaido sea cucumber S$54 and a five-head fresh abalone S$46 each, with a choice of braised in brown sauce, deep-fried with scallion or yellow-braised.
Live fish, including coral trout, soon hock and empurau, is priced per 100g, and the empurau needs advance ordering. Every price is subject to service charge and GST. Pork runs through the menu, so the restaurant is not halal.
Design render of the restaurant entrance at #03-01, 3 Fullerton Road. Photo: Imperial Treasure
The restaurant shares The Fullerton Waterboat House, part of The Fullerton Heritage, with Moutai House’s own rooftop bar. Reservations for Imperial Treasure Moutai House are on 8666 9778.
summary: Imperial Treasure's 45-seat restaurant in Moutai House at The Fullerton Waterboat House has five Huaiyang set menus from S$98++ to S$398++, open daily for lunch and dinner.

I’m Donut? is opening in Singapore
Image credit: The New Yorker
Frequent Japan visitors like me are probably familiar with I’m Donut , a Japanese doughnut chain that built a cult following for their fluffy nama doughnuts and has over 10 outlets in Japan. After announcing the launch of their first Malaysian outlet in KL, I’m Donut has just teased the opening of their first store in Singapore.
Japan’s Viral I’m Donut To Open First Malaysia Outlet In KL On 12 Sep
Image credit: @i.m.donut
In December 2026 , the chain will debut in Singapore at ION Orchard , Basement 2, bringing its signature nama donuts to local fans for the first time.
Image credit: I’m Donut
In case you don’t know, I’m Donut uses a brioche dough that’s enriched with pumpkin and fermented at low temperatures before it’s fried quickly at high heat. The doughnuts are then topped with a variety of creams and toppings made fresh in-house. The result is a light, airy, and clean-tasting doughnut said to melt in your mouth.
Image credit: I’m Donut
The menu for Singapore’s outlet isn’t out yet, but you can probably expect to see their best-selling I’m Donut? Original (price TBD) , a powdered sugar doughnut made with the aforementioned brioche dough. Their Custard Cream (price TBD) is another popular variant, with Kyushu cream whipped into a smooth Diplomat cream and generously piped inside. Matcha lovers can also look forward to their popular I’m Donut? Matcha (price TBD) , featuring dough that’s said to have been kneaded and fully coated with Yame matcha from Fukuoka.
Image credit: Keisuke Tanigawa via Time Out
Every item is handmade in-house, from the dough to the fillings and toppings.
Currently, that’s all the details we have. However, we’ll be on the lookout for more updates.
In the meantime, check out Yamamoto Hamburg , another Japanese chain outlet that has opened its doors in Singapore, specialising in Japanese hamburg. If you’re looking for Japanese pastries instead, our guide to the best Japanese cafes in Singapore has you covered.
Address: 2 Orchard Turn, #B2-19, ION Orchard, Singapore 238801
Opening hours: TBD
Website
I’m Donut is not halal-certified.

Feature image adapted from The New Yorker and I’m Donut
summary: Popular Japanese chain I'm donut, known for their nama doughnuts, will open their first Singapore store at ION Orchard in December 2026!

Two all-day restaurants now share the Ginger Garden at Singapore Botanic Gardens, with brunch from a S$14 kaya brown loaf and soft-boiled eggs up to a S$45 ribeye off the charcoal grill. Tembusu , a Straits dining house from Fleursophy Group, runs the Ginger Garden building that was home to The Halia, while The Bloomhouse by Little Farms sits a few steps away at Block 2, with its own Picnic Basket kiosk.
The rule for this list is simple: places to eat inside the Ginger Garden with a menu their operator published for September or October 2026. Three made it. Prices at both restaurants are subject to GST and service charge.
Tembusu opens 8am to 9pm from Wednesday to Sunday. Photo: Tembusu
Tembusu
Tembusu cooks local and Straits dishes under timber beams, with tall windows onto the garden. Brunch is where the menu is most local: the homemade kaya brown loaf with French butter and two free-range soft-boiled eggs is S$14, and the Tembusu nasi lemak with blue pea basmati rice, chicken hindquarter, sambal, achar and otah is S$26.
Later in the day, udon laksa with Andaman sea prawn, surimi and sakura ebi is S$25, the Singapore chilli crab pasta with soft-shell crab and blue swimmer crab is S$27, and an Andaman prawn risotto in lobster bisque is S$32. Kopi and teh start at S$5.50, made with beans from Vietnam’s Gia Lai Highlands roasted in Singapore by Generation Coffee Roasters.
Two details matter for planning. Pets are allowed in the air-conditioned dining room, which is rare inside the Gardens. Local craft beer on tap drops to S$13 from S$16 during happy hour, noon to 5pm.
Tembusu opens 8am to 6pm on Mondays and Tuesdays, and 8am to 9pm from Wednesday to Sunday. A kids’ section has a junior chicken burger combo at S$16 and a cherry tomato pasta at S$12.
Pets are allowed in Tembusu’s air-conditioned dining room. Photo: Tembusu
The Bloomhouse by Little Farms
The Bloomhouse is open every day from 7.30am to 8pm. Its menu, updated on 1 September, works ginger and other botanicals from the ginger family into the cooking, a nod to the garden outside.
Breakfast runs until 2pm. The Bloomhouse forest omelette is S$19, eggs Benedict with smoked salmon or nitrate-free ham is S$24, and the brekkie platter with two eggs, pork sausage, bacon and sourdough is S$33.
From 11am the kitchen moves to bowls, pasta and a charcoal grill. The Bloomhouse bowl with spiced chicken, avocado and wild rice is S$22. Its chilli crab fettuccine with fried mantou is S$30, three dollars more than Tembusu’s chilli crab pasta next door. The grill has a 250g picanha at S$38 and a 300g ribeye at S$45, and the Bloomhouse burger with a 180g beef patty is S$30.
The Bloomhouse menu starts at S$19 for its forest omelette. Photo: Little Farms
Picnic Basket
Picnic Basket is The Bloomhouse’s takeaway counter, for anyone heading out onto the lawns rather than sitting down. Coffee starts at S$5.50 for an espresso, a long black or flat white is S$6.50, and house teas such as Ginger Garden herbal, with blue pea, torch ginger and lemongrass, are S$8.50.
Smoothies are S$12. Hot sandwiches run from S$11 for a ham and cheese croissant to S$14 for mortadella and scamorza. Event and group bookings go to events@littlefarms.com.
Picnic Basket is The Bloomhouse’s takeaway counter. Photo: Little Farms
Getting there
Both restaurants are inside the Ginger Garden at 1 Cluny Road, deeper in the Gardens than the Nassim Gate visitor centre that map apps point to. The nearest MRT station is Botanic Gardens on the Circle and Downtown lines; enter by the Bukit Timah Gate and walk through to the Ginger Garden. Drivers should use the Learning Forest carpark, the closest drop-off point.
Both menus include pork dishes, and neither restaurant states a halal certification. Tembusu takes general enquiries at hello@tembusu.sg.
summary: Tembusu and The Bloomhouse by Little Farms now share the Ginger Garden at Singapore Botanic Gardens. Published prices, hours, kids' menus, pets and how to get there.
title: Tembusu and The Bloomhouse now share Botanic Gardens’ Ginger Garden, with brunch from S$14

BTS ARMYs, you can look forward to a month of city-wide celebrations as BTS THE CITY ARIRANG arrives in Singapore from 1 to 31 Dec 2026 . The island-wide fan activation is organised by the Singapore Tourism Board (STB) in partnership with HYBE, BTS’ agency.
The month-long celebration coincides with BTS’ 4-night concert run at the National Stadium on 17, 19, 20 and 22 Dec 2026. Moreover, Singapore will also light up landmarks in Marina Bay and along the Singapore River in the group’s signature ARIRANG red from 8 to 22 Dec 2026 .
Credit – Singapore Tourism Board
Lucky for us, Singapore is the first and only stop in Southeast Asia in 2026. It is also the final stop of the year’s THE CITY. The event extends the concert experience beyond the stadium by bringing BTS-themed experiences to venues across our red dot. This will be the biggest island-wide fan activation for any recording artist in Singapore so far. Expect Singapore to be transformed into the ultimate playground for ARMYs.
Credit – HYBE
Jewel Changi Airport will feature a themed light and music show at the Rain Vortex . Mandai Wildlife Reserve will host a themed takeover of Exploria , its new immersive multimedia attraction. At National Gallery Singapore , an Art Trail will pair BTS’s music with artworks from Pop: Art around Us. There will also be themed light and sound installations at the National Museum of Singapore .
Credit – HYBE
Over at Resorts World Sentosa , Universal Studios Singapore will host a fireworks display choreographed to BTS songs , alongside other themed experiences. Plus, Sentosa will also feature a rave , a drone show set to BTS music, a themed race and immersive installations .
Closer to where the concert is happening, The Kallang will introduce interactive experiences across multiple themed zones. If you want to party after the concert, Zouk Singapore will host opening and closing night takeovers with dedicated music and experiential programming.
Best Korean skincare in SG: Innisfree, Laneige, COSRX & more
summary: BTS THE CITY ARIRANG takes place across Singapore from 1 to 31 Dec 2026, with themed experiences at attractions, museums, entertainment venues and nightlife spots. Coinciding with BTS’ 4 National Stadium concerts on 17, 19, 20 and 22 Dec 2026, the celebrations also include red landmark light-ups around Marina Bay and the Singapore River from 8 to 22 Dec 2026, giving fans ways to join in beyond the concerts.
title: BTS THE CITY ARIRANG Singapore – 1st & only SEA stop in 2026
