Calling all photographers and visual storytellers! The festival for all things photography-related is back. The Singapore International Photography Festival (SIPF) 2026 is happening from 16 October 2026 to 31 January 2027 , featuring exhibitions, workshops, and tours.
Photo-Audio Walks
Credit: SIPF
One of the most unique experiences at this year’s SIPF is Passing By Paradise: Photo-Audio Walk , open from 16 October 2026 to 29 November 2026 . Hidden away in Geylang , you will find installations telling the stories of Geylang residents.
As you stroll through Geylang’s Lorongs , streets, and alleys, an audio track and images will accompany you. You will also discover photographic installations in local shops, homes, and public spaces that will connect you more deeply with the neighbourhood.
For a guided tour by the artists behind this experience, you can purchase General Tickets at S$25 or Concession Tickets at S$15 . If you’d prefer, you can also conduct your own self-guided walk for free . Register and book your time slot here .
Singapore Photography
Credit: SIPF
Of course, since it’s SIPF, one of the main highlights is seeing the works of Singaporean photographers. This includes Singapore Index by acclaimed filmmaker and artist Tan Pin Pin.
For the entire duration of SIPF, visitors to Shop-House by DECK will get to see black-and-white images captured between 1991 and 1992, during a transformational era in our nation.
At Mizuma Gallery at Gillman Barracks, Shifting Images: Photography From Singapore 2000 – 2025 ( Image After Image ) takes you beyond the 90s into the 2000s. In fact, you will explore over 2 decades of evolution in photography practices.
Works From Outside Singapore
Credit: SIPF
For those of you who want to set your sights (or lenses) on works from outside Singapore, there are also exhibitions for you. For instance, from 16 October 2026 to 29 November 2026 , there are 2 exhibitions at Shop-House by DECK featuring works by Korean photographers .
In the Comfort of All Things spotlights the everyday lives of elderly residents in an old multi-family housing complex, as well as colourful images of a university hospital.
FEM: Women, Lives, and Korean Photobooks presents a collection of photobooks that showcase the diverse experiences of different generations of Korean women. You will see through the eyes of photographers in their twenties, all the way to those in their eighties.
Both exhibitions are open to the public from Wednesday to Sunday, 12pm–7pm .
Talks & Workshops
Credit: SIPF
If you’re a photographer who wants to find inspiration or expand your creative skillset, there is a series of talks and workshops you can sign up for at SIPF too. One interesting session is The Photobook Clinic with Shi Zhen taking place on 24 October 2026 .
The 3-hour session invites creatives working on photobook projects to come together for a constructive exchange. Whether they are just starting on their creations or nearing completion, participants will benefit from professional guidance that will help elevate their work.
General Tickets are available at S$130 , while Concession Tickets are priced at S$90 . If this is your cup of tea, reserve a seat here .
Credit: SIPF
Beyond what is mentioned in this article, SIPF 2026 has much more to offer for creatives and storytellers looking to expand their horizons or sharpen their craft. For a full list of exhibitions, activities , and event venues , visit SIPF’s website .
See you out there, photographers.

This November , Fortuna ’s regular diners can look forward to a refreshed menu filled with brave, playful interpretations of familiar Italian favourites by the newly appointed Executive Chef Silvio . He’ll be bringing his Italian roots and years of international culinary experience to Fortuna, along with unexpected twists on Italian classics .
With most of the menu reworked, Fortuna takes diners Dal Sud al Nord (from South to North). Here’s what we can’t wait to try , course by course.
Antipasti
Credit: Fortuna
The journey begins with Pumpkin Arancini (S$26) , a fried rice ball filled with pumpkin purée and pancetta, finished with balsamic glaze. If fresh tomatoes are your thing, the Caprese (S$22) brings together marinated heirloom tomatoes and basil pesto, with the option to add Prosciutto to make it fancier!
Carb Loading, Italian Style
Credit: Fortuna
One dish I noticed that is staying on the menu is the Maflde (S$38) , my ultimate favourite, especially when drizzled with their crispy chilli oil. Something new is the Trottola (S$35) , bringing together porcini mushrooms, shaved black truffle and Parmigiano.
Good Things Come in Slices
Credit: Fortuna
I’ve been to Fortuna at least twice, and the pizzas were always a hit, leaving no crust and crumbs behind. Personally, I’m intrigued to try the Barbara (from $34) , inspired by lasagna, with Parmesan-Ricotta mousse, and crispy pasta shards and the New Gen Mushroom Trip (from S$36) .
Dessert
Credit: Fortuna
End your meal with their Frittelle (S$18) , a deep-fried dough coated in cinnamon sugar, served with custard and Nutella for maximum indulgence. Otherwise, their Coppa al Pistachio (S$18) has also caught my attention for a sweet treat fix.
Sip Happens
Credit: Fortuna
Beyond the food, there’s also The Story in Six Drinks , a new cocktail collection where each creation tells its own story. Drinks I can’t wait to try are A Broken Promise pairs rum with salted caramel, and Nina , a concoction of mango and Aperol.
For coffee lovers, Fiesta mixes bourbon and espresso, and Riflessione , a clarified Mezcal Espresso Negroni, might be the drink for you!
Together, the restaurant is serving up new food and cocktail menus, signalling a fresh chapter for Fortuna and bringing renewed creativity to both the kitchen and bar. Dal Sud al Nord will be available at Fortuna from November 2026.

If you’re looking to throw an intimate party but your cooking chops are mediocre at best, these Christmas food delivery and takeaway spots in Singapore are here to save the day. They dish out drool-worthy set menus, festive classics (yes, roast turkey, ham and log cakes included), and hearty side dishes. Leave your lunch and dinner spreads in their great hands, so you can put all your effort into finding the perfect decorations and Christmas tree in Singapore . Psst: don’t miss our ultimate guide on Christmas in Singapore as you get in the merrymaking mood!
Psst: we’re still in the midst of updating this roundup for 2026, so keep your eyes peeled!
Best Christmas delivery and takeaways in Singapore
1. Violet Oon Singapore
Photography: Violet Oon Singapore
Are your annual holiday parties feeling like rinse and repeat? Switch things up with a Nyonya-themed feast from Violet Oon Singapore. Yes, you can enjoy iconic signatures from this well-loved Peranakan restaurant in Singapore for Christmas. The party trays make hosting easy-breezy, featuring all-time favourites like kueh pie tee, dry laksa, beef rendang, buah keluak ayam and chap chye.
Each party tray feeds up to 15 guests, so there will be plenty to go around – second helpings, included. We highly recommend the VO’s Shepherd’s pie for an easy crowd-pleaser for all ages. Don’t forget to save room for desserts. Violet Oon has got you covered with a pillowy-soft coconut log cake, Brandy-infused tropical fruit cake, and gula melaka cake topped with cashew crumble.
Best for: A Perankan-inspired festive feast
Prices : Party trays from $73.07; festive cakes from $59
When to order: Online pre-orders open now; available for delivery and collection
Where to purchase: Order online; party tray collection from Violet Oon at Dempsey Hill with a minimum two-day notice, festive cake collection from Violet Oon at Ion Orchard
Order from Violet Oon Singapore
2. Little Farms
Photography: Little Farms
Bring the indulgence home with Little Farms’ festive takeaway collection that looks oh-so-enticing. These folks have got everything from premium roasts to seasonal sides and desserts. For your scene-stealing holiday roast, choose among the whole roasted turkey, pineapple and honey glazed ham, and prime beef rib roast.
Complete the spread with side dishes like green bean almondine, charred cauliflower salad and pillowy-soft golden honey buns. When you’re done with the savouries, bring out the pumpkin pie or vanilla and black currant log cake for a sweet finale. Or, spare yourself the effort of curating a feast and go for one of the three Christmas sets.
Best for: Classic Christmas delicacies for a homely feast
Prices: A la carte items from $14; sets from $308
When to order: Online pre-orders open now; available for delivery and collection from 5 to 31 Dec 2026
Where to purchase: Order online
Order from Little Farms
3. Living Menu
For your picture-perfect holiday feast, leave the heavy lifting to catering services like Living Menu. This multi-vendor catering platform in Singapore partners with hawkers, chef-run food shops and caterers to deliver a satisfying spread. This means you can enjoy the best dishes from each vendor in a single order!
The Christmas menus come in four tiers – opt for a higher tier to enjoy more dishes at premium quality. With crowd-pleasers like chicken stroganoff with creamy mushroom sauce, mixed seafood drenched in cajun butter sauce, and spaghetti marinara, the line-up won’t disappoint.
Best for: A crowd-pleasing spread from various vendors and caterers
Prices : Mini buffets from $15 per pax (minimum order of 75)
When to order: Online pre-orders open now; available for delivery from 1 Dec 2026 to 3 Jan 2027
Where to purchase: Order online
Order from Living Menu
4. Da Paolo
Photography: Da Paolo
Have yourself an Italian-inspired festive celebration with the Christmas takeaway collection from Da Paolo. We love how the brand puts a unique twist on holiday classics while retaining its Italian roots. With a variety of party trays, sides and desserts to choose from, putting together a spread is as easy as it gets.
Curious what caught our attention? Juicy, homemade beef meatballs simmered in tangy tomato sauce; sous vide salmon served with a lemon, caper and white wine sauce; and decadently layered beef lasagna. An Italian spread is incomplete without tiramisu. Pick between the classic and pistachio version, or just get both ‘cos you deserve the year-end treat.
Best for: Authentic Italian delicacies from meatballs to tiramisu
Prices: A la carte items from $48

body:
146 Famous Bukit Merah Ang Ku Kueh has handmade kueh
Vintage finds have been on the rise lately, from digicams to vinyl records and thrifting. Amid the froyo craze and matcha fatigue, I find myself craving traditional desserts from time to time, so I’m glad shops such as 146 Famous Bukit Merah Ang Ku Kueh are still around and thriving—an old-school kueh shop specialising in handmade kueh with a modern twist.
Tucked under a void deck at Block 146 Bukit Merah , this kueh shop first started as a provision store in 1981 before pivoting to sell ang ku kueh in 1991. It’s run by a husband-and-wife duo, who pride themselves on making all their kueh by hand to yield the thinnest skin and softest mouthfeel.
Back then, the shop only sold Peanut and Mung Bean ang ku kueh, but now offers 13 flavours. Unique ones include Sweet Corn , Coconut , and Durian , to name a few. Each ang ku kueh is priced affordably at $1.60 .
Though ang ku kueh is what they’re famous for, they offer a plethora of other treats, including soon kueh, png kueh and more. The kueh looked too enticing to pass up, so we had to get some ourselves.
We were spoilt for choice, so we opted for the Mini Assorted Ang Ku Kueh ($8) , which gives you a box of 10 different flavours, alongside Ondeh-Ondeh ($2.60 per box) and Green Tea Ang Ku Kueh ($1.60) .
Most people start their day with caffeine, and I did the same with the Coffee ang ku kueh—the coffee flavour was prominent without being overpowering. What really stole the show for me was its thin and chewy skin, and I appreciated that the kueh was stuffed generously with mung bean and coffee paste.
Next up, I tried the purple-coloured Yam , which ended up being my favourite flavour. I was worried it would be too jelak, but it turned out impressively well-balanced. I liked that I could still taste the nutty mung beans through the subtly sweet yam. Plus, the yam paste was creamy and smooth, melting in my mouth with every bite.
Of course, I also had to try the OG Mung Bean . The filling was made of grainy mung beans, which gave it a grittier texture, and the skin felt thicker than the others. Texture aside, it was still a familiar and nostalgic classic, though it’s nothing to rave about.
Next up was the Green Tea Ang Ku Kueh, which was massive. It had a floral fragrance, and strong hints of tea coming through in each bite. It’s almost as if I were drinking the actual thing and was surprisingly refreshing to eat.
Besides kueh, we also snagged the last box of o ndeh-ondeh for the day. One nearly burst as I picked it up, which I took as a good sign of how delicate the skin was. Upon the first bite, it exploded with rich gula melaka syrup and was incredibly shiok to eat.
The coconut flakes helped to cut through the sweetness of the liquid gold within and added a nice crunch, giving it a satisfying mouthfeel. We could see why it sold out in only a few hours of opening.
As someone who was initially not too big on ang ku kueh, I’d say that these definitely changed my mind. Their grit and innovation are worth applauding, and I’d certainly go back to try the other flavours and creations.
On the topic of old-school treats, check out our Love Confectionery feature for some affordable bakes in Queenstown. Read our Everton Park food guide for more good eats in the area.
Address: 146 Jalan Bukit Merah, Block 146, Singapore 160146
Opening hours: Daily 7:30am to 7pm
Tel: 6273 5159
Website
146 Famous Bukit Merah Ang Ku Kueh is not halal-certified.

This was an independent visit by Eatbook.

Best Golden Mile Food Centre food
Situated opposite the now-closed Golden Mile Tower Complex, which many people flocked to for cheap Thai food, Golden Mile Food Centre was sometimes overlooked by people looking for good food in the area. A shame really, considering how much yummy grub the place offers. This listicle serves as a guide to some of the best stalls in the hawker centre.
1. Chung Cheng Chilli Prawn Noodles
One of the stalls here that draws long queues daily is Chung Cheng Chilli Prawn Noodles , and it’s not surprising why. Known for their house-made signature chilli sauce, the uncle preparing their Chilli Mee (from $4.50) shows no mercy as he adds spoonful after spoonful of the piquant sauce into the noodles. Each bowl comes with pieces of pork ribs, prawns, taupok, fishcake, as well as a hard-boiled egg. Remember to mix it all up so that you don’t eat the chilli by itself.
Read our Chung Cheng Chilli Prawn Noodles review .
Unit number: #01-59
Opening hours: TBD
Chung Cheng Chilli Prawn Noodles is not halal-certified.
2. Charlie’s Peranakan Food
Calling all Peranakan food lovers, Charlie’s Peranakan Food is where to go for simple and classic dishes. Everything at Charlie’s Peranakan Food is made from scratch in-house, according to the recipes passed down through Charlie’s mother. Be sure to try dishes such as Ayam Pongteh ($12), Beef Rendang ($14) , and Satay Ayam ($8) for a taste of some perennial Peranakan classics done right.
Read our Charlie’s Peranakan Food coverage .
Unit number: #B1-30
Opening hours: Daily 11:30am to 7:30pm
Website
Charlie’s Peranakan Food is not halal-certified.
This Golden Mile Stall Has Been Serving Peranakan Food Since The 1980s—Does It Still Hold Up?
3. Ashes Burnnit
Run by the ex-founders of popular Western food joint Burgs by Project Warung, Ashes Burnnit sells affordable burgers at Golden Mile Food Centre. Their burgers start from $8.40 , with the Ashes Cheeseburger being the popular option. Served with a striking charcoal bun, the burger patties are smashed on the grill for an extra charred crust. Each order comes served with thick-cut fries too. The stall also has unique charcoal roti john, such as the Cheesy Fish Burger ($10) , a mammoth of a burger filled with charred fish fillet, omelette, smoked cheese and more.
Read our Ashes Burnnit review .
Unit number: #B1-24
Opening hours: Daily 11:30am to 3:30pm, 4:30pm to 9pm
Website
Ashes Burnnit is Muslim-owned.
4. Flourful Delight
Flourful Delight is known for their Xiao Long Bao ($6 for six) , where dumplings are packed with a flavourful pork filling. More crowd favourites include the Wonton In Chilli Oil ($6 for 10) , where silky meat dumplings are tossed in a tangy chilli-vinegar dressing, and the Braised Beef Noodles ($6) , served with a generous helping of la mian and thick chunks of braised beef and vegetables.
Read our Flourful Delight review .
Unit number: #01-85
Opening hours: Tue-Sat 10.30am to 8pm
Tel: 8118 1217
Flourful Delight is not halal-certified.
Flourful Delight Review: Handmade XLB And Braised Beef Noodles From $5 In Jurong West
5. Mr Baguette
Mr Baguette is the only place in Singapore that sells lava baguettes. Despite the glorious molten fillings, the baguette still had a good crisp on the outside. One of the must-tries here would be their Hazelnut Lava ($2.80) . Packed with a rich hazelnut chocolate filling, this is one for all with a sweet tooth! My personal favourite would be their savoury Cheese Lava ($2.80) that’s brimming with hot, melted cheese.
Read our Mr Baguette review .
Unit number: #B1-51
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 12pm to 4:30pm, Sat-Sun 12pm to 6pm
Tel: 9184 1257
Website
Mr Baguette is not halal-certified.
6. 75 Ah Balling Peanut Soup
To tang yuan lovers, 75 Ah Balling Peanut Soup is definitely not a new name. Since they started business in 1947, they have been famous for old-school tang yuan that come with explosive fillings. While their Peanut Soup is their best-seller, do try their Ginger Soup and Almond Milk as well. Each bowl of their dessert comes with four pieces of glutinous rice balls, with fillings such as peanut, sesame , and yam to choose from. A bowl of tang yuan starts from $2.80, with a minimum of four pieces per order.
Read our 75 Ah Balling review .
Unit number: #01-75
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 11am to 8:15pm, Sat 10am to 8:15pm, Sun 10:30am to 8:15pm
Website
75 Ah Balling Peanut Soup is not halal-certified.
7. Hainan Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee
Hainan Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee is helmed by an old couple, where the uncle will fry each batch of Hokkien Mee ($5) with care. The classic mix of wok hei-filled yellow noodles and bee hoon is left to simmer in a seafood stock, leaving a natural sweetness on the dish. The wok hei here is the stall’s claim to fame—fans have noted how much aroma and flavour it adds to the dish. Don’t miss out on their sambal chilli, too, which is said to be wonderfully spicy, tangy, and fragrant.
Unit number: #B1-34

If you’re anything like me, videos of huge, chunky New York-style cookies have been dominating your feed for the past couple of months. I finally made it down to Golden Mile Food Centre along Beach Road to try out a homegrown version of the viral cookie at ATECOOKIES.SG .
The bright white sign hanging above the stall instantly stands out against the sea of heritage hawkers. The stall is helmed by young self-taught baker Donovan, who uses his own cookie recipes crafted entirely from scratch. Donovan sets time aside daily to R&D new recipes or to improve existing ones.
Aside from the mouthwatering options available right now, he shared that they are currently developing new flavours, such as a pistachio lava cookie planned for launch in the coming months. You should definitely keep an eye out for future releases!
What to order at ATECOOKIES.SG
I settled on 2 signature cookies and 1 premium cookie. What immediately stood out to me was how craggy the tops of the cookies were, indicating that I would be in for a crispy treat.
I started off strong with a bite of the Walnut Choco (S$5.50) . The cookie was liberally studded throughout with a mix of chocolate chips and walnut bits, which add a great crunch. I was pleased to find it wasn’t overly sweet or jelak , even after I was 3/4 of the way through the decadent cookie.
All cookies I tried from this stall are deliciously crunchy on the outside while maintaining a wonderfully chewy brownie-like texture inside, making hem that much more addictive.
Next, I moved on to have a bite of the Matcha Macadamia ( S$5.50) . This turned out to be my absolute favourite out of the 3 cookies because of its perfectly balanced flavour.
I felt the flavours of both the matcha and macadamia came through nicely, which I didn’t initially expect. Neither component overpowers the other and instead pairs fantastically. The addition of premium white chocolate adds a delicious layer of richness to every bite.
Last but definitely not least, I sampled the Chocolate Lava (S$7) . Don’t let its humble appearance fool you — this cookie was insanely generous with the chocolate lava filling which remained perfectly ooey-gooey even after bringing it home to enjoy.
They use 55% dark chocolate, which is incredibly smooth and tastes lightly sweet as it coats your tongue. The ratio of the viscous chocolate filling to cookie was perfect, so you can get a little of that creamy filling with every bite.
10 places with the motherfudging chunkiest cookies in Singapore
Who is ATECOOKIES.SG best for?
I’d recommend this stall to any cookie lover out there because they offer what many would consider to be a masterclass in cookies. The chunky bakes are chock-full of high-quality ingredients which really do make a difference in the final product.
I can imagine the cookies making for great gifts to friends and family members as ATECOOKIES.SG offers online ordering bundles and delivery services on their website.
How to get to ATECOOKIES.SG
ATECOOKIES.SG is located within Golden Mile Food Centre, which is a quick 7-minute walk from Nicoll Highway MRT Station . The station connects to the Circle Line of Singapore’s Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) train system. Take Exit A and walk along Java Road before turning left onto Beach Road.
If you prefer to travel by bus, alight at Opp St. John HQ (01411) or St. John HQ (01419) along Beach Road. Do note that bus service 961M operates exclusively on Sundays and public holidays, while all other bus services operate daily.
Do we recommend ATECOOKIES.SG ?
For sure! I’d recommend buying extra to store at home as they last up to 3 days at room temperature and 7 days in the fridge, as shared by the owner.
The combination of crisp edges, rich chewy centres, and generous toppings makes this Beach Road bakery stall an absolute must-visit hawker next time you’re in the area.

Priced from S$5.50 to S$7 each, signature creations include Walnut Choco, Matcha Macadamia, and dark chocolate lava options featuring crisp exteriors and chewy centres. It is ideal for dessert enthusiasts and gift buyers seeking artisanal bakes accessible via Nicoll Highway MRT station or online delivery.

body:
Think you’ve seen all there is to eat around Petaling Street ? A little detour down one of Chinatown’s quieter side roads might just change your mind. Laksa Tiam , which opened in June 2026, brought southern Thai-inspired laksa with freshly made rice noodles.
The menu features bowls ranging from turmeric-infused fish laksa to fragrant green curry chicken. Laksa Tiam is also under Old China Cafe , the long-standing Nyonya restaurant known for its traditional Peranakan fare .
What to order at Laksa Tiam
The menu is fairly simple, with 4 varieties of Thai-inspired laksa alongside cendol and drinks. Each bowl costs RM18 , or RM22 when paired with a Lemongrass Lime drink . Naturally, we went for the combo.
We started with the Green Curry Chicken Laksa , which delivered the fragrant, herbaceous flavours you’d expect from a good green curry. The broth was flavourful and tasted fairly authentic, although it leaned a little salty for my liking.
Its freshly made rice noodles were on the softer side, breaking apart more easily than I would have preferred. Still, I enjoyed their silky texture, which soaked up the curry nicely.
There was plenty going on in the bowl, too, including chicken, eggplant, suan cai , bean sprouts, long beans, cucumber and egg. The assortment gave each mouthful a mix of textures, making this a hearty option for anyone who enjoys their laksa loaded with ingredients.
Teow Kee Beef Noodle: 8-topping springy beef noodles with rich tonkotsu-style soup & tender cuts at TRX
However, if you’re visiting for the first time, I’d actually recommend skipping the Signature Turmeric Fish Laksa in favour of the Prawn Peanut Laksa . The staff recommended this one to us, and spoiler alert: it was damn good .
For RM18 , the prawns were generous in both quantity and size, and thankfully, they were already deveined. The bowl came with a similar assortment of vegetables and other ingredients as the Green Curry Chicken Laksa , with the prawns taking centre stage.
But honestly, the broth was what made this bowl memorable. It’s difficult to pin down exactly what went into it, but the closest comparison I could make was sambal udang , with a subtle hint of kerisik lending it an almost toasted, nutty depth. It was savoury, fragrant and deeply moreish, with a flavour unlike the usual laksa broths I’ve tried. I’d go as far as saying it was one of the most distinctive laksa broths I’ve tasted.
Look a little deeper into the bowl and you’ll find crushed peanuts, adding another layer of texture and nuttiness to the mix. Every spoonful had me going back for more, and this was easily my favourite of the two. If you’re someone who enjoys bold, savoury flavours, I’d say this is the bowl to order.
To wash everything down, we had the Lemongrass Lime drink. It was refreshing, although the lemongrass was more pronounced than the lime. I appreciated that the sugar syrup came separately, allowing us to adjust the sweetness to our liking rather than having it dictated to us.
Who is Laksa Tiam best for?
Laksa Tiam is worth a visit for anyone looking to switch up their usual Chinatown food crawl with something a little different. The cosy dining space suits casual meals with friends, although it can feel a little stuffy, especially when the restaurant gets busy.
Its location also makes it a convenient lunch option for office workers around the area, so expect more of a crowd during peak hours.
One thing to note is that the restaurant is located upstairs and has no lift, which may pose a challenge for wheelchair users and diners with mobility difficulties.
How to get there?
Laksa Tiam is a short walk from Pasar Seni MRT Station , making it relatively easy to reach by public transport. If you’re exploring Petaling Street on foot, it’s also worth adding to your itinerary when you need a break from the main thoroughfare.
Do we recommend Laksa Tiam?
Yes, particularly if you enjoy laksa but are keen to try something beyond the familiar local versions. The Green Curry Chicken Laksa makes for a satisfying bowl, but the Prawn Peanut Laksa is what truly won me over. Its distinctive, sambal udang -like broth with a hint of kerisik was so memorable that I’d happily return just to have it again.

Where do I go for the best brunch and date nights in Bangsar?
summary: Laksa Tiam is a Thai-inspired laksa eatery along a quieter side road in Petaling Street, Kuala Lumpur, serving four varieties of laksa with freshly made rice noodles from RM18 per bowl. Suited to laksa lovers seeking distinctive broths for casual lunches or Chinatown food crawls, it stands out for its Prawn Peanut Laksa, with a savoury, nutty broth. The upstairs restaurant has no lift, which may limit access for diners with mobility difficulties.
title: Laksa Tiam: This hidden Chinatown spot serves Southern Thai prawn peanut & green curry laksa with freshly made noodles

body:
Pasar Pagi JB – W eekend flea market
If your usual JB itinerary consists of cafe-hopping and shopping malls , here’s somewhere different to check out on your next trip across the Causeway. Pasar Pagi JB is a weekend flea market where you can hunt for vintage gems, quirky collectibles, and second-hand fashion without necessarily breaking the bank.
Located at the outdoor parking area of Angsana Mall Johor Bahru and held every Saturday, this morning market has plenty to browse and lots you can score a bargain for.
The current exchange rate is S$1 = ~RM3. 20 as of 20th October 2026.
A Saturday morning flea market with over 120 vendors
Image adapted from: @hellopasarpagi via Instagram
Tucked away in the Level 1 open-air car park of Angsana Johor Bahru Mall , Pasar Pagi isn’t your typical morning market. Instead of fresh produce and groceries, you’ll find yourself lost in rows and rows of stalls packed with vintage treasures, antiques, and second-hand goodies.
Image credit: @hellopasarpagi via Instagram
The market first opened in 2024 , after an antique enthusiast from Perak came up with the idea. Having been involved in the local collector’s scene and online vintage trading, the founder wanted to bring that same passion for nostalgic finds to a physical marketplace.
View this post on Instagram
What initially started with around 100 vendors has since grown to approximately 120 to 130 vendors . You’ll find both first-time sellers as well as seasoned collectors here, making every stall worth a little peek.
Fun fact: “Pagi” means “morning” in Malay, which explains why this flea market kicks off bright and early at 7am in the morning!
Score vintage clothes & pre-loved designer pieces
Image credit: Pasar Pagi Johor Bahru via Facebook
Thrift shopping enthusiasts, this one’s for you. Pasar Pagi has plenty of second-hand fashion finds, from vintage T-shirts and streetwear to pre-loved branded and designer clothing .
Image credit: Pasar Pagi Johor Bahru via Facebook
If you’re a fan of retro fashion, keep an eye out for clothing from the 1960s and 1970s. You can also browse accessories such as caps , bags , and shoes .
Some clothing pieces are priced as low as RM10 (~S$3. 20 ) to RM20 (~S$6. 30 ) , while others are priced around RM40 (~S$12.5 0 ) . Prices vary between stalls, so be sure to check with the vendors before getting too attached to a particular find.
Hunt for nostalgic collectibles & retro furniture
Image credit: Angsana Malls Malaysia via Facebook
The vintage stalls at Pasar Pagi also take you on a little trip back in time. Vendors here sell old-school cameras , classic vinyl records , cassette tapes , CDs , radios , and even vintage lighters .
Image credit: Visit Malaysia via Facebook
Those looking to give their homes a retro makeover can also browse second-hand furniture , nostalgic posters , and artwork . You might just stumble upon a piece that looks straight out of your grandparents’ living room, in the best way possible.
Image credit: Visit Malaysia via Facebook
There’s also an assortment of vintage toys , action figures , old electronics , and glassware for collectors to explore. Prices range from as low as RM1 (~S$0 . 3 0 ) to RM2,000 (~S$627. 10 ) for really unique finds, so there’s something for casual bargain hunters and serious collectors alike.
Browse quirky home decor, books & handmade crafts
Image credit: Visit Malaysia via Facebook
Fashion and antiques aside, Pasar Pagi also has a selection of miscellaneous finds that make browsing the stalls all the more interesting. Expect books , magazines , watches , musical instruments , and handmade crafts .
Image adapted from: Visit Malaysia via Facebook
For those who love collecting unusual home decor, keep a lookout for pieces such as an intricate glass ornament priced at RM95 (~S$29. 80 ) or a small handheld drawer going for RM55 (~S$17.2 0 ) .
With so many different items on display, you could arrive looking for a vintage T-shirt and end up leaving with an entirely unexpected decorative addition to your home.
How to get to Pasar Pagi JB
View this post on Instagram

Singapore Airlines new in-flight amenities
When it comes to providing stellar service, no airline does it better than our beloved Singapore Airlines. There’s a multitude of reasons why it’s been crowned the best in the world this year, and pretty soon, you’ll have another one that just might convince you to fly with SQ over other carriers.
Come November , passengers aboard SQ flights lasting more than 6 hours across all cabin classes can receive new in-flight amenities to make their time in the air that much more enjoyable. Whether you’re a frequent business traveller or a vacationer with your EOY holiday plans lined up, here’s what you can expect on future SQ flights.
What are Singapore Airlines’ new in-flight amenities?
Just last week, Singapore Airlines announced that in November 2026 , they’ll be swapping out their current set of in-flight amenities, which includes products from brands like Lalique and Le Labo, with a refreshed range.
Moreover, these amenities will be provided to passengers across all cabin classes , from Suites & First Class all the way to Economy. However, do note that they’ll be available only for SQ flights with flight times of at least 6 hours . Without further ado, take a peek at what you can look forward to receiving during your flights with SQ during the upcoming holiday season.
Suites & First Class
For the fortunate few who’ve got the luxury to nab a seat on SQ’s Suites and First Class, you’re in for a treat. You’ll be pampered with goodies from French luxury cosmetic maison SISLEY ; additionally, there are amenity kits for both him and her, a thoughtful touch for their most esteemed passengers.
Image credit: Singapore Airlines
The ladies’ offerings include a curated range of products from SISLEY’s Sisleÿa range. These include the Black Rose Cream Mask , L’Intégral Anti-Age Eye And Lip Contour Cream , Essential Skin Care Lotion , Restorative Hand Cream , and the L’Eau Rêvée d’Eliya fragrance , all bundled up neatly in a white amenity kit embellished with the brand’s logo and gingko leaf pattern.
Image credit: Singapore Airlines
Meanwhile, the gents receive their amenity kits in a sleek black , packed with products from the brand’s Sisleÿum range. Included in the self-care package are the L’Eau Rêvée d’Alma fragrance , Restorative Hand Cream , Nutritive Lip Balm , Anti-Age Mattifying Gel-Cream , Ecological Compound , and All Day All Year Essential Anti-Aging Protection .
Image credit: Singapore Airlines
The premiums don’t end there; Suites and First Class flyers will also get a new 100% cotton sleeper suit that subtly sports the airline’s signature batik motif, along with coral fleece slippers with improved padding, all befitting of royalty.
These sleeper suits, along with the ones given out on Business Class flights, will be available on selected medium-haul overnight flights of more than 6 hours and on all long-haul trips .
Image credit: Singapore Airlines
When you’ve got to freshen up, the aircraft lavatories here will be equipped with Eau De Campagne Moisturising Body Lotion , Floral Spray Mist , and Eau De Campagne fragrance , all courtesy of SISLEY. Similarly, travellers waiting for their flights at The Private Room and First Class Silver Kris Lounge can look and smell their best with the help of SISLEY toiletries .
Business Class
Image credit: Singapore Airlines
The new Business Class amenities ain’t too shabby as well. For starters, you’ll get a BYREDO amenity kit, featuring the luxury Swedish brand’s Blanche Hand Cream , lip balm , and Blanche Eau de Parfum , alongside eye shades and a dental kit .
Image credit: Singapore Airlines
Weary travellers sitting in Business Class, you’ll be pleased to know that for the first time, you’ll be getting a comfy sleeper suit too. Designed in navy blue, the poly-cotton sleepwear also bears the same batik motifs as its Suites and First Class counterparts, while grey poly-cotton slippers complete the look.
Image credit: Singapore Airlines
Over in the Business Class lavatories, you’ll find BYREDO’s Blanche body lotion and Vitamin E chamomile facial toner to complement your skincare routine.
Premium Economy Class
Image credit: Singapore Airlines
Those on a slightly tighter budget are not forgotten, as Premium Economy Class ticket holders can also enjoy a sweet SIA-designed zip pouch that’s made out of recycled materials. Inside awaits an exclusive INK & WATER white tea-scented lip balm , eye shades , socks , and a dental kit .
Economy Class
Image credit: Singapore Airlines
Last but not least, Economy Class travellers’ amenity kits trade in the zip pouch for a roomier drawstring pouch splashed with the airline’s iconic batik motif. Reach inside, and you’ll find handy travel essentials such as eye shades , socks , and a dental kit .
Extra goodies for children
Image credit: Singapore Airlines

summary: Goodies for every cabin class.

body:
Gallia Phinisi Batam
When staycations are mentioned, it’s usually hotels and resorts that come to mind. But if you’re bored of your usual staycation haunts and looking for a new type of experience, here’s one that might quite literally float your boat.
Just a short ferry ride away from Singapore, Gallia Phinisi in Batam lets you spend the night aboard a traditional wooden ship. And with rooms advertised from S$40/night , you can easily swap your typical hotel room for a cosy cabin overlooking the sea without burning a hole in your wallet.
Spend the night aboard a traditional wooden ship
A stationary ship life experience
Image credits: Booking.com
At Gallia Phinisi Batam, you’ll be staying aboard a phinisi , a traditional Indonesian wooden ship known for its distinctive design. The vessel itself is docked at Bengkong Laut , an urban village in the Bengkong district of Batam, and is designed specially to accommodate overnight guests.
From the outside, the wooden structure makes a unique backdrop for holiday photos fit for the ‘gram. Then step aboard, and you’ll find guest cabins, communal spaces, and outdoor areas where you can wind down and take in the sea scenery.
Image credit: Agoda
Just keep in mind that this is a stationary accommodation rather than a sailing one, so don’t expect to wake up in a new destination the next morning. Here, you get to experience life on a ship, minus the actual sailing. Think of it as a hotel with a nautical twist, rather than a cruise experience.
Book cosy cabins with sea views, from S$40/night
Image credit: Agoda
If your mental image of a ship’s accommodation is cramped bunk beds and shared toilets, fret not, as the ship comes with private guest rooms fitted with amenities.
For the budget-conscious, the 12sqm Standard Room is one to consider. It’s admittedly quite snug, but there’s room enough for a queen-sized bed and the typical essentials, like a private bathroom with a shower.
Image credit: Agoda
You’ll also get air-conditioning and a sea view, which makes this a perfect option for couples who want to explore the offerings of Batam without paying a more premium price tag for a proper hotel room.
Image credit: Agoda
Those who prefer more breathing room can look at the 25sqm Superior Room , which also features 1 queen-sized bed. Besides having more floor space, it also has a balcony and marina views, so you can step outside to enjoy the surroundings.
Image credit: Agoda
Alternatively, the Deluxe Room also offers 25sqm of space, sea views, but comes with additional comforts such as a king-sized bed. And if you’re after something even more spacious, there’s an Executive Room measuring 40sqm with the ability to host up to 3 adults.
Image credit: Agoda
Rooms start from around S$40/night for the Standard Room , S$74/night for the Superior Room , S$109/night for the Deluxe Room , and S$149/night for the Executive Room , at the time of writing. Take note that room prices are not fixed and may vary depending on the booking date.
Open-air sun terrace & community kitchen
Image credit: Agoda
There’s more to do at Gallila Phinisi than just enjoying its cosy cabins. You can also head up to the open-air sun terrace to lounge in the sun or under the stars, soak up the sea breeze, and snap some photos against the marine backdrop. Those whose staycations aren’t complete without a classic karaoke sesh will also enjoy the karaoke room on the premises.
Image credit: Agoda
If you’re adventurous, you might even want to check out its water activities, including fishing and canoeing , for an extra cost.
As for food, the ship also has a shared kitchen and offers complimentary breakfast depending on your booking, so you won’t have to worry about heading out for food first thing in the morning.
Beach club just next door that’s known for its aesthetic pink sand
Image credit: Zoom Travel International
The fun doesn’t have to end at lounging in cabins with sea views, especially for those who fancy a good party. Right next to the ship is Blue Fire Beach Club , where you can spend the afternoon at the pool before partying into the night.
One of its main highlights is the pink sand beach area , which looks straight out of a Barbie film. The sand is artificially coloured, but still makes for a pretty photo-op, especially paired with waterfront views.
Image credit: Muhammad Fadil via Google Maps
And, if you want to cool off in the Batam heat, there’s also a swimming pool surrounded by seating areas where you can take a splash, or kick back and relax.
Those who prefer some sports and action can try the beach club’s water sports, which include jet skiing , kart boating , parasailing , and more. However, do note that these activities all incur separate charges.
Image credit: Blue Fire Beach Club via Facebook
…
summary: The beach club next door is just a 1-minute walk away.
title: You Can Stay In A Traditional Wooden Ship In Batam, With A Pink Sand Beach Club Right Next Door

body:
Coliwoo Bukit Timah Fire Station
Singapore has no shortage of heritage buildings that have been given a new lease of life . From the former Nan Chiau High School becoming New Bahru to the old St Andrew’s Mission Hospital transforming into KADA , these spaces now offer plenty of reasons to visit beyond their historical significance.
Joining the list is Coliwoo Bukit Timah Fire Station , a former fire station that’s now home to co-living spaces, restaurants, and creative workshops. We went down for a visit as the revamped property celebrated its 1st anniversary on 15th October 2026 , and here’s what you can expect when you pop by this lifestyle enclave.
From a fire station to a lifestyle destination
Former Bukit Timah Fire Station, taken in 1991.
Image credit: Urban Redevelopment Authority via Facebook
Built in 1956 , the former Bukit Timah Fire Station served as a familiar Singapore landmark for 49 years before ceasing operations in 2005 amid the area’s urban development. The Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) then gazetted the landmark in 2019 for conservation, ensuring its unique architecture would be preserved for years to come.
Redevelopment plans took a few twists and turns along the way. In 2021 , the project was initially awarded to Homestead Holland Pte Ltd, but faced multiple delays. In April 2024 , the Singapore Land Authority (SLA) and URA handed over a 5-year lease to Coliwoo’s parent company, LHN Facilities Management.
Image credit: Coliwoo
In 2025 , the property was transformed into a mixed-use development, now known as Coliwoo Bukit Timah Fire Station, while preserving its original architectural character.
What to expect at Coliwoo Bukit Timah Fire Station
Today, the space combines co-living spaces with dining establishments, retail shops, and hands-on workshops. It’s also conveniently located near Bukit Timah Nature Reserve , Rifle Range Nature Park , and the 24km Rail Corridor , making it a handy stop for those exploring the area on foot or by bicycle.
Get creative with crafty workshops
You don’t have to be a resident to enjoy what Coliwoo Bukit Timah Fire Station has to offer. Apart from the co-living space, the property is also home to several businesses offering hands-on experiences, whether you’re interested in cooking, arts and crafts, or picking up a new skill.
The Sundowner
Image credit: The Sundowner
If you’ve ever wanted to try your hand at something beyond the usual pottery or painting workshop, The Sundowner has quite the selection of activities.
For starters, its Rooftop Farm Experience introduces participants to organic gardening and beekeeping in a 2-hour session. You’ll get to put on a bee suit, feed rescued honeybees, sample different varieties of honey, and even make a cocktail. It’s priced at $115/adult and $85/child .
Image credit: The Sundowner
There’s also the Bees! Ants! Worms! Workshop that lasts for 1.5 hours , where participants can observe ant colonies, search for earthworms, and learn how composting works. It’s an interactive way to discover the smaller creatures that play an important role in our ecosystem. To attend the workshop, prices are $85/adult and $65/child .
Image adapted from: The Sundowner
Foodies can sign up for the Pizza Making Experience at $135/adult and $95/child , which involves 3 hours of preparing dough and sauce, gathering fresh herbs, and baking pizzas in a wood-fired oven.
Alternatively, the Pasta by Hand workshop, priced at $125/adult and $95/child , teaches participants to make fresh pasta, with varieties such as pappardelle, tagliatelle, and ravioli depending on the session. Each session lasts about 3 hours .
Pizza Making Experience (left) and Pasta by Hand (right).
Image adapted from: The Sundowner
Those who enjoy their morning cuppa can try Roast Your Own Coffee , where they’ll roast green coffee beans over a fire, grind them, and experiment with different brewing techniques in the 2-hour session. Brunch is included in the experience, too. It’s priced at $95/adult .
Image credit: The Sundowner
Other activities include Bean to Bar Chocolate , a 2 – hour session priced at $110/person , where participants turn cacao beans into their own chocolate bars, and Brew Your Own Beer , a 2 – hour session priced at $110/person , which covers craft beer tasting, draught beer basics, and preparing a bottle for fermentation.
Book an experience at The Sundowner .
World of YING
Image credit: World of YING
Put on your little artist hats, because World of YING offers intimate, atelier-style workshops that turn everyday materials into personalised creations.
Its Wearable Art Experience , priced at $350 , lets participants paint their own cape blouse under the guidance of artist Ying. Each person receives a blouse in their chosen colour, and no previous painting experience is needed. However, this workshop is currently fully booked at the time of writing, so keep a lookout for any available dates on their website.
Image credit: World of YING
…
summary: Who knew you could learn beekeeping on a staycation?
title: This 70-Year-Old Fire Station Is Now A Lifestyle Hub With Workshops Like Beekeeping & Cake Decorating

Kobo x NLB Sit-n-Read Node at City Square Mall
Unique reading spaces have been quietly popping up around Singapore, from the Sci-Fi Pop-up Library to the Stories by the Beach installations. Continuing these efforts, the National Library Board (NLB) has teamed up with Rakuten Kobo to launch the Kobo x NLB Sit-n-Read Node at City Square Mall , bringing digital and physical books together in one place.
What is the Kobo x NLB Sit-n-Read Node all about?
Image credit: @publiclibrarysg via Instagram
The collaboration is part of NLB’s ongoing mission to get more Singaporeans reading through its ReadSG initiative. It also marks Rakuten Kobo’s 1st standalone presence in Singapore, as the digital reading brand looks to make reading a bigger part of everyday life.
As the latest Sit-n-Read Node, the space continues NLB’s efforts to make reading more accessible by setting up dedicated reading spots in places people frequent . The node’s open layout means you can pop in from any direction, making it easy to squeeze in your 15 minutes of daily reading even when you’re out and about.
What to expect at the Kobo x NLB Sit-n-Read Node?
Browse through NLB’s digital collection on Kobo eReaders
Image credit: @publiclibrarysg via Instagram
This is the 1st and only hybrid Sit-n-Read Node featuring Kobo eReaders . You can try out 3 of the brand’s latest models, including the Kobo Libra Colour, Kobo Clara Colour, and Kobo Clara BW.
There are 8 eReaders spread across the space that are free to use, offering a curated selection of eBooks from NLB’s digital catalogue for you to browse. For those planning to get a Kobo device, this is the perfect chance to explore what reading on one feels like before you commit to the purchase.
While the digital books are only available as short previews at the node, you can keep reading beyond that by scanning the QR code at the end of the preview to find the full book in NLB’s digital collection, then borrow it to finish reading on your own eReader.
Bring home pre-loved books for free
For those who prefer physical books, NLB also has curated shelves of pre-loved titles for both adults and children. The good news is you can bring these books home with you without needing to borrow them, but you are encouraged to return them to the node once you’re done so others can enjoy them as well.
The selection will be refreshed regularly, so look out for new titles to discover whenever you visit.
Settle down with a book in cosy reading nooks
Image credit: @publiclibrarysg via Instagram
Once you’ve picked out a title, make yourself comfortable in one of the colourful reading nooks found around the space. There are 4 cosy nooks for adults and another made for families, each equipped with their own eReaders.
Are food & drinks allowed?
Food and drinks are strictly not allowed within the node; this is to maintain the cleanliness of the community-shared space, books, and eReaders.
Can I donate books to the Sit-n-Read Nodes?
Some of the titles available at the Sit-n-Read Node.
You can’t donate your pre-loved books to these nodes as NLB curates the selection to ensure the contents are appropriate. If you’re looking to get rid of unwanted books, you can drop them off at these selected libraries with donation corners:
• Bedok Library
• Bishan Library
• Geylang East Library
• Jurong Library
• Toa Payoh Library
• Woodlands Library
Enjoy reading at the Kobo x NLB Sit-n-Read Node
Image credit: @publiclibrarysg via Instagram
Whether you prefer flipping through physical books or giving eReaders a go, the Kobo x NLB Sit-n-Read Node gives you the chance to do both while in the middle of your usual mall run. The next time you’re at City Square Mall, make sure to swing by and check out the space for yourself.

body:
The Intan Peranakan Museum
The Peranakan culture has a vibrant heritage and rich history, and no word captures its many facets better than the intan , which translates to “rose-cut diamond” in Malay. Like its namesake, The Intan is an award-winning museum-home situated in the heart of Joo Chiat , an eastside enclave known for being the heart of Peranakan culture in Singapore.
Owned by Alvin Yapp, The Intan is a manifestation of his lifelong passion for the culture and boasts one of the widest collections of Peranakan antiques you can find on our little red dot. From colourful tingkat carriers to rare pieces of furniture, here’s what’s in store at this cosy museum that’ll make you feel like you’ve just stepped into an old baba’s home from back in the day.
What is The Intan?
Image credit: @zesty_ruffles via Instagram
Nestled in a double-storey terrace unit along Joo Chiat Terrace, The Intan has a very rustic and homely exterior – the thought of it being a museum is something that probably wouldn’t cross your mind.
Image credit: @tangenghui via Instagram
Open the doors, though, and you’ll step into a time capsule of the olden days. Having been an avid collector since he was 15 years old, Mr Yapp has spent the last 30 years collecting Peranakan artefacts, with more than 1,500 displayed in this museum.
A Peranakan himself, Mr Yapp’s deep interest in the heritage was sparked after watching a play with his parents. Through collecting antiques, he now lives and breathes the culture, even in the literal sense – the second floor of The Intan is his comfortable abode.
What to see at The Intan Peranakan home museum
Image adapted from: @pattywoo21 , @xperiencesingapore
As seen in homes nowadays, enamel tiffin carriers, also known as tingkat , are frequently used as display collectables to add a nostalgic touch to the space. In the past, they were used as dabao containers, where people could pack lunch to bring to their workplaces or to deliver to friends and family.
Image adapted from: @hellozizilovepanda
Another object that was seen in kitchens was the kamcheng , a covered jar used to serve food during mealtimes.
Image adapted from: @ykworksonstilts , @tunastwins
There are also many pairs of kasut maneks on display, which are beaded slippers handsewn with delicate floral patterns. They are part of the uniform for SIA stewardesses, together with their iconic sarong kebaya outfit.
Image adapted from: @hellozizilovepanda
The space is filled with intricate wooden furniture that makes up the Peranakan style of decor. In fact, Mr Yapp’s first antique that he acquired was a planter chair found in the same style, which he found at a garage sale with his father.
Image credit: @hellozizilovepanda
Displayed along the walls are these intricate embroidery patterns, which were widely practised by Nyonya women back then.
Image adapted from: @aozo55 , @eunicekwah , @jupcraft
Of course, we can’t go without the iconic Peranakan-style tiles, a familiar aesthetic commonly seen on the shophouses along Joo Chiat Road.
The Intan tea experience & other tours
Image credit: @kazumi__kin , @mkreuch
Sharing is caring, and Mr Yapp is one who loves to host visitors who come around. On top of acting as their tour guide around the place, he also organises The Intan Peranakan Tea Experience ($64.20) . It lasts for an hour, and you will dig into delicious Nyonya kueh and tea once you’re done viewing the place. The Intan tea experience can also be booked with your SG Culture Pass credits.
The tea experience is available on Fridays at 4pm, Saturdays at 10am and 4pm, and Sundays at 4pm.
For a more holistic experience, you can consider The Intan Private Dinner Experience ($180) . After touring the place, you’ll get to dig into an authentic Peranakan meal hosted by Mr Yapp, which will feature favourite dishes like bunga telang , babi pongteh and homemade ngoh hiang .
Can I book The Intan for wedding photoshoots & events?
Image credit: @amperiansg
Yes, The Intan is also available for private group visits for up to 40 guests, wedding photoshoots, and special meals. Do reach out to them directly for more details on availability and rates.
How to get to The Intan
The Intan is tucked away on a quiet residential street in Joo Chiat. Since entry is strictly by appointment, book your slot before heading down.
• Address: 69 Joo Chiat Terrace, Singapore 427231
• By MRT (East-West Line): Eunos MRT (EW7) is the closest station, about a 10-minute walk away. Head south from Changi Road into the Joo Chiat estate, and The Intan is a short stroll from the junction of Joo Chiat Place and Tembeling Road.
• By MRT (Circle Line): From Dakota MRT (CC8), take bus 33 from the stop at Exit A and alight 5 stops later at Bef Joo Chiat Place on Tembeling Road. The Intan is a 2-minute walk from there.
• From Paya Lebar MRT (EW8/CC9): It’s roughly a 15-minute walk, and a nice option if you want to pass Joo Chiat’s colourful shophouses on the way.
…
summary: At The Intan, where you'll discover that just like its classic Nyonya Kueh, Peranakan culture comes in many layers & colours rolled into one.
title: The Intan: Peranakan Home Museum Filled With Antiques As Diverse & Colourful As Nyonya Kueh

Our favourite shopping event, Boutiques Singapore, returns for its Gifting Edition! If you think this is just another flea market in Singapore , think again. Celebrating all things independent, original, local, and design-forward, it spotlights over 300 designers. It’s the place to be for exclusive launches and unique finds, from fashion to home decor and food. Got a shopping itch you need to scratch? This is one of the hottest things to do over the weekend in Singapore .
Boutiques Singapore: Details at a glance
Photography: Boutiques Singapore
Best for: Shopaholics and tourists looking for uniquely Singaporean souvenirs
Date: 20 to 22 November 2026
Opening hours: Friday and Saturday, 11am to 9pm; Sunday, 10am to 6pm
Prices: Tickets start from $8
Address: Boutiques Singapore 2026 , F1 Pit Building, 1 Republic Boulevard, Singapore 038975
What’s new at Boutiques Singapore: The Gifting Edition 2026
Art & Design Experiences with Gofy. Photography: Ying Xuan Leong
Keep an eye out for more than 300 local and international brands at Boutiques Singapore: The Gifting Edition 2026. This includes a record-high number of new fashion and accessory labels! Plus, we’re excited to see cult-favourite regional brands making their Singapore debut.
This edition also sees the arrival of several new experiences and discoveries!
Singapore Design Gift Store
Located in Room 2A, you can explore local designs curated by Priscilla Tan (Principal Designer at Supermama) and Clara Yee (designer and co-founder of Magicfruit). Expect design collectives like Just A Band Of Creatives, Observation House, and Printcentre, and discover their ideas.
Gofy’s Naughty or Nice Concept
Gofy is making gifting fun again with its playful wrapping paper and gift card pairing. With a $10 donation to one of five charity partners, you can pick wrappings with sayings like “Frenemy vs Bestie” or “Spicy vs Sweet”. Various artists design the wrapping paper, and you can drop in for artist-led workshops and activities for all ages and skill levels.
Hideaway
The massage and bathhouse concept from New Bahru is offering 15-minute neck and shoulder or hand and arm massages if you need a quick rest stop from shopping all day. And yes, Hideaway will have a booth with a range of personal care essentials around its signature scent.
Aura Obscura
Ever wondered what your aura looks like? Head to Aura Obscura and use a camera with biofeedback sensors, translating subtle changes in your body’s electrical activity into colourful aura portraits.
The Artground & That’s Neat
Kid-free shopping is in your future thanks to the Artground and That’s Neat, who have created a new expanded kids’ drop-off area. As you browse the plethora of brands available, the tots can get busy with workshops like candle-making and recyclable weaving.
F&B brands
Plenty of new food options are available at the upcoming Boutiques Fair! Satiate your sweet tooth with Arc-en-ciel Patisserie’s ice cream parfaits or Birds of Paradise’s gelato. Need something more filling? Enjoy some of Kafe Utu’s African-inspired food and coffee, or head to The Garage Cafe to get grilled cheese sandwiches from Cheeselads and Mahmud’s Tandoor’s Pakistani-Indian favourites.
Stylish brands in the spotlight
You deserve a wardrobe refresh, especially when several stylish fashion brands are bringing in exclusive designs at Boutiques Singapore! View the full list on the Boutiques Singapore brand directory .
Tow Tow: The Singapore label debuts its System Collection with an ecosystem of interchangeable straps, pouches, hardware, and charms to build your perfect bag.
Sea Apple: To mark its 10th anniversary, this children’s brand will debut The Sea Apple Hotel, a collection inspired by boutique hotels with personalisation and made-to-order T-shirts.
Maison Q: Personalise your clothes and accessories with hand-drawn doodles transformed into embroidered designs!
Vor: This brand will debut a new jewellery collection at Boutiques with stainless steel rings, necklaces, and bracelets, all created in small quantities.
Tauruscamp: Minimalist wallets and everyday-carry pieces with hot-stamp personalisation available at Boutiques.
The Needy Socks: Created by a nurse, these compression socks are both functional and come in fun designs.
Homeware, beauty brands and more
Photography: Heirloom Garden and Eden Living
If you’re tired of your home aesthetic and want to jazz things up, Boutiques Singapore has plenty of design-led brands that’ll give your space some extra pizzazz. It’s also the perfect opportunity to refresh your skincare routine with new beauty products! View the full list on the Boutiques Singapore brand directory .
Wastd: Using a material-led approach to crafting, this design studio creates unique furniture made with recycled materials.
Kii Workshop: Hand-crafted wood furniture combining the beauty of traditional craft with everyday contemporary living.
…
summary: Our favourite shopping event, Boutiques Singapore, returns for its Gifting Edition! If you think this is just another flea market in Singapore, think again. Celebrating all things independent, original, local, and design-forward, it spotlights over 300 designers. It’s the place to be for exclusive launches and unique finds, from fashion to home decor and food.

body:
Unique matcha drinks in Singapore
Strawberry matcha used to be the adventurous order, but these days, it’s practically the default. With new matcha cafes opening every other week, the ones worth the trip are the ones doing something different with their flavours. From local nostalgic flavours to more experimental concoctions, here are 11 cafes with unique matcha drinks in Singapore that every matcha lover should try.
10 Best Matcha Cafes In Singapore Ranked—Hvala, Tsujiri And More
1. Tofu Tofu
The last time we visited Tofu Tofu , they were still a matcha home cafe in Bedok. They’ve since opened their first brick-and-mortar store at East Village Mall along Upper Changi Road, with a menu of locally inspired matcha lattes. The Kaya Matcha ($6.90) pairs creamy, earthy matcha with fragrant pandan kaya for a nostalgic twist, while the Bandung Matcha ($6.90) swaps in floral rose syrup for another Singaporean take.
You can also pick your matcha powder here. The house Tofutofu Ceremonial Grade is balanced, with mid-level umami and nutty notes. For something grassier, there’s the Yamamasa Koyamaen Aoarashi ($8.90) . You can also choose between hot-whisked or cold-whisked matcha, the former resulting in a stronger matcha flavour, while the latter gives your drink a creamier mouthfeel.
Upsizing to 500ml or upgrading to a 350ml bottle costs $2 each, and oat milk is an extra $0.50 .
Read our Tofu Tofu coverage .
Address: 430 Upper Changi Rd, #01-89, East Village, Singapore 487048
Opening hours: Wed-Fri 10am to 5pm, Sat-Sun 11am to 7pm
Website
TofuTofu is not halal-certified but uses no pork or lard.
We Tried Kaya Matcha And Caramel Hojicha Latte At This Bedok Home Cafe
2. Studio Frond
Image credit: @saladbawl
Studio Frond is a weekend-only matcha bar in Joo Chiat that doubles as a flower bar. Your matcha is served on a tray that also holds a DIY floral arrangement, so you get to make your own mini bouquet while you sip. The standard kit starts from $15 and comes with a floral base, a focal flower, and an accent flower.
I’m a huge fan of Studio Frond’s Miso Butterscotch Matcha Latte (from $8) , which pairs matcha with house-made miso sauce and rich butterscotch for a sweet-salty cup. For your tea, you can pick between Frond Matcha #01 , sourced from Zhejiang, China, and Frond Matcha #02 from Uji, Japan.
Read our Studio Frond coverage .
Address: 216 Joo Chiat Road, #01-05, Singapore 427483
Opening hours: Sat 10am to 6pm, Sun 10am to 5pm
Website
Studio Frond is not halal-certified.
This New Joo Chiat Cafe Serves Matcha With DIY Floral Bouquets
3. Bouche
Image credit: @saladbawl
Tucked under a HDB block near Holland Village, Bouche has a sleek black entrance that’s hard to miss. The one to order is the Pistachio Matcha ($8.90) , which pairs thick, rich matcha with nutty pistachio sauce. You can choose your sweetness level and your powder— Tenzo is creamy and umami-forward, while Samidori is stronger and nuttier, with a kinako-like profile.
Part of the fun is the final pour. The baristas will offer to finish your drink right in front of you, so get your camera ready. The space seats only a handful of people, but camping chairs are set up outside, and an old-school TV screen inside has been repurposed for mirror selfies. If you’re a regular, there’s also a $50 membership that gets you any seven drinks.
Address: 40 Holland Drive, #01-27, Singapore
Opening hours: Thurs-Fri 11am to 8pm, Sat-Sun 10am to 8pm, Mon-Tue 11am to 8pm
Website
Bouche is not halal-certified.
4. Ghost Kakigori
Image credit: @breadiexeats
Ghost Kakigori is best known for its Japanese shaved ice and chilled dorayaki, but its “Matcha Ritual” drinks are where it gets experimental. The one to order is the Durian Cheese Royale Matcha ($8.90) , a rich, creamy cup of savoury cheese foam, earthy matcha, and Mao Shan Wang durian. When I tried it, I found the durian flavour strong, with a distinct richness from Mao Shan Wang. If durian isn’t your thing, the Fresh Mango Boba Matcha ($6.90) is a fruitier take, while other additions include the Pomelo Zesty Matcha ($6.90) and Taro Mochi Bliss Matcha ($6.90 ).
Website
Ghost Kakigori is not halal-certified.
5. Creamie Sippies
Image credit: Creamie Sippies
Banana pudding matcha is what put Creamie Sippies on the map, but their Earth Day ($8.90) is the more unusual order that most people sleep on. Made with butterfly pea and Creamie Sippies’ in-house Uji matcha, the blue and green drink is meant to represent the colours of Mother Earth. Flavour-wise, it’s light, floral, and refreshing. It also comes in a 500ml Sippie cup with 8g of matcha, so you’re getting a proper dose of caffeine.
Their newest outlet on Bugis Street also has a DIY banana pudding bar if you want something sweet on the side.
Read our Creamie Sippies coverage .
Website | Full list of outlets
Creamie Sippies is not halal-certified.

6. Little Rituals
Image credit: @offdaytreats

Baskin-Robbins launches new Japanese-inspired ice cream flavours
Image credit: Baskin-Robbins Malaysia
It’s no coincidence that stressed spelt backwards is desserts —I can always count on a sweet treat to brighten my day. Now, we have good reason to eat our sorrows away: Baskin-Robbins has recently launched three new flavours as part of their Japan Summer Series , available only for a limited time.
Image credit: @baskinrobbinssg
A longtime fan-favourite, Popping Shower (price TBD) is making its debut in Singapore. It’s been hailed as Baskin-Robbins Japan’s number one flavour for years. Fun fact: it’s also the top pick of popular Japanese figure skater Yuzuru Hanyu!
Image credit: @baskinrobbinssg
This whimsical flavour combines milky white chocolate and refreshing mint ice cream with red and green popping candies, which crackle and fizz with every lick. It’s a nostalgic, playful treat that’s also fun to eat.
Image credit: @baskinrobbinssg
Adding to the fun are two more flavours: Matcha (price TBD) and Musk Melon (price TBD) . Matcha aficionados would be pleased to know that the ice cream is made with authentic Kyoto Uji matcha, so you know you’re getting the real deal.
If matcha isn’t your cup of tea, the latter is a fruitier option that sounds just as enticing—it’s made with premium musk melon from Japan.
Image credit: @baskinrobbinssg
If you’re spoilt for choice or just want to try them all, the Japan Triple Fun Scoop ($8.50) is the way to go. Here, you get all three flavours in one waffle cone.
Image credit: @baskinrobbinssg
The series doesn’t end here. Baskin-Robbins also offers the massive Japan Trio Waffle ($13.90) that sees all three flavours atop a waffle for the ultimate indulgent dessert.
Image credit: @baskinrobbinssg
PSA: Get a free puffy sticker sheet with a minimum order of one item from the Japan Summer Series per receipt, while stocks last.
Speaking of Japanese desserts, check out our I’m Donut feature for first dibs on the viral Japanese Chain’s debut in Singapore. For more new Japanese chain openings, our Matsuya feature covers the deets on their very first outlet at Suntec City.
Website | Full list of outlets
Baskin-Robbins is halal-certified.

body:
Nothing is sadder than seeing a once-important building fade away into obscurity. Thankfully, Coliwoo Bukit Timah Fire Station on Upper Bukit Timah Road is giving this old landmark a second life near some of Singapore’s best hiking trails
Bukit Timah Fire Station protected the community for 49 years before closing in 2005. It was gazetted as a conservation site in 2019. In 2025, Coliwoo reopened the building as a co-living space with several workshops, programmes and even a restaurant on site. As you can probably tell, the building had a long history that went well beyond its time as a simple fire station.
Fun fact: During my National Service, my encik – who has since retired – actually served at Bukit Timah Fire Station. He is a wonderful man who told all sorts of stories about his time there. I’m sure he would be glad to know his former home is still helping the community years after its closure.
What I experienced at Coliwoo Bukit Timah Fire Station
When I got there, I was greeted by cordial staff who were truly excited to show off the fire station. The longer I spent there, the more I understood their pride. After a brief but informative speech from the Senior Minister of State Ms Low Yen Ling and Coliwoo founder, Kelvin Lim , we got a tour. Only then did I realise how much work went into this place.
Despite the rain and the very bad haze, the view was still astounding. The fire tower is painted with a beautiful mural, set against the greenery that the same fire station used to protect. The mural represents the bountiful nature that surrounds this side of Singapore.
Though I will say, I’m surprised I didn’t see any monkeys in the art. According to one of the tenants, some of those mischievous rascals tend to play around the pool, swinging around pool noodles and such. Aside from that silly detail, the art really gives the place a warmth to it.
After the tour, we got straight into the workshops. If you like lo-fi , a good book on a rainy day or anything ‘chill’, you’d love them. The first workshop was flower arranging at Dawn Q Flowers . The store itself was small and slightly squeezy for a big guy like myself, but it felt comforting nonetheless. When you enter, you are surrounded by a floral aroma, refreshing and breezy. It was a gloomy day, but just sitting there felt therapeutic.
Sorting between pom-poms and Cathrine roses and adding just enough shrubbery to accentuate the centrepiece, I genuinely felt like a princess for a second.
Above is my own creation. Flower aficionados, please be merciful. I personally think it’s beautiful. A 1-hour workshop at Dawn Q Flowers costs S$69.90 , and each session comes with a new variety of flowers. They also have more options on their website . I can genuinely see myself doing it a few times a year now.
Workshops in Singapore: Celebrate creative birthdays, bachelorettes & anniversaries
The next workshop I attended was cake decorating by Haute Cakes . This is another very chill workshop.
I was given an edible flower to paint using these colourful powders. It was simple and chill, but everyone was fully locked in on painting.
Once we were done, the instructor gave us a slice of honey cake. Let me tell you, it was one of the best cakes I’ve had in a long time. I’m not a cake person, so this really took me by surprise. It turns out the honey used in the cake came from another tenant that provides a beekeeping workshop.
To see the community come together and help one another is truly heartwarming. The full cake decorating workshop is 4 hours and costs S$180 per person, with more options on their Instagram and their website .
Who is Coliwoo Bukit Timah Fire Station best for?
I’m hard-pressed not to say ‘everyone’, but it is best for hikers. It makes a natural pit stop for Bukit Timah Nature Reserve , Rifle Range Nature Park and several other hiking hotspots nearby.
While you take a load off, you might end up roaming the grounds and finding workshops to try with your family. They also work as dates with the one you love.
There is also a restaurant on the grounds, Decker Barbecue , which serves American BBQ . Decker Barbecue has a very impressive rating on Google, but I personally did not get to try it.
How to get to Coliwoo Bukit Timah Fire Station
There are actually several ways to get there. You could take the Downtown Line (blue line) to Hume. It takes around 15 minutes to walk from there. Personally, I would consider this a hike.
Cross the road from the exit at Hume station and follow the path straight to Coliwoo Bukit Timah Fire Station. The path is actually quite nice as you walk along the forest. Alternatively, there is a bus stop named Springdale Condo , next to the fire station. It has less greenery, but it’s only a 1-minute walk.
Do we recommend Coliwoo Bukit Timah Fire Station?
…
summary: Coliwoo Bukit Timah Fire Station is a conserved former fire station on Upper Bukit Timah Road, now a co-living space with workshops such as flower arranging (S$69.90) and cake decorating (S$180 for 4 hours). It sits near Bukit Timah Nature Reserve and Rifle Range Nature Park, making it best suited for hikers, families and couples. Hume MRT station on the Downtown Line is the nearest station.
title: Coliwoo Bukit Timah: Old fire station gets a 2nd life with cake decor & flower arrangement workshops

Pack your luggage, ladies & gentlemen. It’s time to fly ! The Time To Fly Travel Fair 2026 is happening from 23 to 30 October 2026 and features discounts on over 380,000 Singapore Airlines (SIA) and Scoot tickets .
Curious about which destinations are included in this sale? Keep reading and look out for your favourite cities !
Visit Over 70 Destinations at Lower Prices
Credit: Pelago
During the sale period, more than 200,000 return tickets from SIA will be discounted across Business Class , Premium Economy Class , and Economy Class on flights from Singapore to 78 destinations.
Confirmed destinations and discounted round-trip Economy Class tickets include:
• Bangkok from S$258
• Da Nang from S$258
• Hangzhou from S$388
• Taipei from S$388
• Sydney from S$558
• London from S$988
• Los Angeles from S$988
• Madrid from S$988
SIA tickets purchased during this sale will be for travel between 1 January 2027 and 30 September 2027 . For more deals and promo codes , visit SIA’s website on 23 October 2026 , where special credit card offers will also drop.
Credit: Scoot
Another website to watch is Scoot’s Time To Fly page . Customers can look forward to over 180,000 discounted tickets in ScootPlus and Economy Class , from Singapore to 70 destinations .
The special fares will only be unveiled on 23 October 2026 , but Scoot has already dropped some teasers. Expect new routes to destinations such as Belitung , Chiang Rai , Guiyang , and Okinawa .
Scoot tickets purchased during this sale will be for travel between 9 November 2026 and 15 October 2027 . Bookmark Scoot’s page and check back again on 23 October 2026.
The Time To Fly Travel Fair promotion will be available online from 23 to 30 October 2026 via SIA and Scoot’s respective websites , mobile applications , and appointed travel agents .
3-Day Physical Travel Fair
Credit: Singapore Airlines Facebook
Beyond online sales, Time To Fly will also present itself as a 3-day physical travel fair from 23 to 25 October 2026 at the Suntec Convention Centre . Visiting this physical fair will give you access to exclusive deals from over 30 travel agents and partners .
This includes 1-for-1 travel deals from Hong Thai Travel , up to S$500 in travel savings from Trip.com , up to 50% off flights, hotels and cruises via Traveloka , and more.
There will also be giveaways and a grand Lucky Draw you can take part in. Top prizes include SIA Business Class return tickets to Cebu , Hangzhou , and Sydney with hotel accommodation .
Other daily draw prizes include Scoot vouchers worth up to S$2,000 , KrisShop vouchers worth up to S$800 , and more SIA Business Class return tickets . For more information on what to expect at Time To Fly Travel Fair 2026, click here .
It’s time to gather your family and friends to plan for your 2027 holidays . May the fastest flight bookers win!

body:
Orang Laut SG , the community group that has sold Southern Islander food mostly through weekend deliveries since 2020, opens its first walk-in cafe on Friday, 23 October, CNA Lifestyle reported. Called Terumbu, it runs at Chef X, #03-103/104 Clarke Quay Central, until 26 December.
Terumbu opens at Chef X on 23 October. Photo: Orang Laut SG
Terumbu is Malay for coral reefs. The pop-up is the 15th residency at Chef X, Far East Organization’s space for home-based and private-dining cooks to run a commercial restaurant for a fixed stint, with a professional kitchen, a dining room for up to 24 and mentoring from chef Isaac Tan of Commonwealth Concepts.
Two savoury dishes and island kueh
The menu is short. The Pulau Bowl is S$15.90 and puts three seafood dishes over jasmine rice with vegetables: asam pedas ikan karang (coral reef fish in a sour, spicy gravy), sotong hitam (squid cooked in its own ink) and sambal udang (stir-fried prawns in sambal).
The sotong hitam uses green-eyed squid, known as sotong nos, which is traditionally caught by line. The family picks it for the amount of ink it carries.
The second dish is bubur lambuk tenggiri, a Spanish mackerel porridge cooked with lemongrass, coconut milk and black pepper. It is S$11.90 with prawns or with squid, and S$13.90 with both.
Bubur lambuk tenggiri is S$11.90 with prawns or squid. Photo: Orang Laut SG
This is not the bubur lambuk handed out at mosques during Ramadan. On the islands it was an everyday dish, made by grinding leftover coral fish, bones and all, at a time when families had no fridge to keep the catch.
Dessert is kueh koleh-koleh and puteri salat, made by a former Pulau Bukom islander. The menu names coral fish without naming the species, because the fish changes with what islander fishermen bring in, including the few bubu (fish trap) makers who still go out to sea.
A family kitchen from Pulau Semakau
Founder Firdaus Sani is a fourth-generation Orang Pulau and Orang Laut whose family lived on Pulau Semakau for generations. They were moved to the mainland in 1977, and the island is now Singapore’s offshore landfill.
His mother does most of the cooking at Terumbu, with his aunt Rohaini running the floor and cousins helping out. The recipes come from his grandmother, Nenek Ninah, and are cooked by feel rather than by measurement.
The family runs Terumbu’s kitchen and floor. Photo: Orang Laut SG
Orang Laut SG started in 2020 as an Instagram page recording the memories, food and traditions of communities moved off the Southern Islands. Terumbu also has a small community gallery on the history of those islands.
Details
Details from CNA Lifestyle:
