Cherry Garden by Chef Fei at Mandarin Oriental, Singapore has put hairy crab and Matsuba crab on its autumn menu, which runs from 1 October to 30 November 2026. The Cantonese and Teochew restaurant is serving the crab dishes in a six-course set and as à la carte plates.
The dining room at Cherry Garden by Chef Fei. Image: Mandarin Oriental, Singapore
The six-course autumn set
The autumn set costs S$288 a person, for a minimum of two diners. It opens with an appetiser trilogy of Teochew-style pork fritter, raw langoustine in garlic chilli oil with Siberian sturgeon caviar, and organic fioretto scented with wild sansho pepper.
After that come chicken consommé with fish maw and Hetian fig, braised Imperial bird’s nest with crab roe and jade melon, and crab roe xiao long bao. XO sauce stir-fried Matsuba crab with Chaoshan-style pickled vegetable and vermicelli follows, and the meal ends with double-boiled Autumn Moon pear with golden fungus and lily bulb, served with a ginger-infused crab meat pastry.
Diners can add the 15-year Shaoxing wine marinated hairy crab as a supplementary course at S$48 for half a crab or S$68 for a whole one. Availability of the hairy crab depends on supply.
Autumn dishes à la carte
Several of the autumn dishes are also sold on their own:
• 15-year Shaoxing wine marinated hairy crab, S$68 for a whole crab
• Teochew-style pork fritter, S$38 for six pieces
• Raw langoustine in garlic chilli oil with Siberian sturgeon caviar, S$108 for six pieces
• Organic fioretto scented with wild sansho pepper, S$28
• Chicken consommé with fish maw and Hetian fig, S$68
• XO sauce stir-fried Matsuba crab with Chaoshan-style pickled vegetable and vermicelli, S$288
Sautéed diced Wagyu beef with Sichuan peppercorn. Image: Mandarin Oriental, Singapore
The regular set menus
Cherry Garden’s regular sets run alongside the autumn menu. Bamboo, at S$138 a person, has a dim sum trilogy, double-boiled fish maw with scallop and matsutake, sautéed diced Wagyu beef with Sichuan peppercorn, and Yang Chun noodle with shrimp roe in chicken broth.
Lotus costs S$198, Jasmine S$218 with Xisha Island lobster in creamy garlic sauce, and Peony S$268, which includes boneless crucian carp congee.
Boneless crucian carp congee. Image: Mandarin Oriental, Singapore
Appetisers at Cherry Garden by Chef Fei. Image: Mandarin Oriental, Singapore
All prices are in Singapore dollars and subject to a 10 per cent service charge and prevailing government taxes. Cherry Garden is at Mandarin Oriental, Singapore, 5 Raffles Avenue, and takes bookings on +65 6338 0066.
summary: Cherry Garden by Chef Fei serves a six-course autumn crab set at S$288 a person, plus drunken hairy crab from S$48, until 30 November.

body:
Behind the scenes of Project Wolbachia – Singapore
Singapore recorded a 7-year low in dengue cases in 2025, with about 4,000 cases reported. This was thanks in part to residents doing their part to keep mosquito breeding at bay, alongside mosquito suppression efforts with Project Wolbachia – Singapore .
The results of Project Wolbachia have been encouraging. In Project Wolbachia release areas, Aedes aegypti mosquito populations have fallen by 80–90%, while dengue risk has been reduced by over 70%.
Today, Project Wolbachia has expanded to cover more than half of Singapore’s households, and is the first in the world to use Wolbachia suppression technology to control mosquito population in a dense, high-rise tropical city.
Behind this project is a dedicated team working tirelessly to protect communities from dengue. We had the opportunity to see how it all works:
How does Project Wolbachia actually work?
The different life stages of an Aedes aegypti mosquito.
But first, what is Project Wolbachia , and how does it actually work? Wolbachia is a naturally occurring bacterium found in more than 60% of insect species. Launched in 2016, the project breeds male Aedes aegypti mosquitoes carrying this bacterium and releases them into the community.
The Aedes aegypti mosquito is Singapore’s main dengue-spreading vector. So, the magic happens when these Wolbachia -carrying males mate with female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes in the wild – the eggs produced do not hatch.
Up to twice a week, these mosquitoes are released at selected sites, which have been chosen based on factors such as historical dengue risk, and Aedes aegypti mosquito population.
Over time, the population of Aedes aegypti mosquitoes in the area decreases, and in turn, dengue numbers drop too.
ICYMI, male mozzies don’t bite. And no, there is no genetic modification at work.
It all begins with gazillions of mozzie eggs
Each black dot is a mosquito egg.
But how does NEA get so many male Wolbachia -carrying Aedes aegypti mosquitoes to constantly release into the wild? At NEA’s mosquito production facility in Ang Mo Kio, Aedes aegypti mosquitoes carrying Wolbachia are bred at scale using in-house designed technologies. Female mosquitoes naturally pass the bacterium to their offspring, enabling a steady supply of mosquitoes for the programme.
Millions upon millions of eggs are on standby at any point in time, waiting to be dipped in water and hatched.
Like a high-tech farm, but for mozzies
“These mosquitoes are highly spoiled,” we are told, and they honestly are.
Automated larvae counters. Once the eggs hatch, the larvae are counted and distributed into trays to prevent overcrowding and ensure healthy development. In the early days of Project Wolbachia , this was done manually, with staff each taking more than 3 hours to count about 4,000 larvae per tray
Today, an automated Larvae Counter can process 25,000 larvae per tray in just five minutes, dramatically increasing the programme’s production capacity.
Premium fish food is mixed with water to achieve just the right consistency and poured into automatic feeders that dispense a precise amount of food to the larvae.
The mixed feed is poured into automatic dispensers.
The conditions are optimised for them – think 28°C rooms, maintained at an ideal 80% humidity, and let’s not forget the premium feed.
Every single step of the process is painstakingly monitored and supervised; nothing is left to chance.
Going through the sorting hat
The pupae stage comes after the larvae stage, and this is where sex sorting takes place.
Loading small samples of pupae for the Pupae Size Scanner.
To ensure accurate sex separation, a sample of pupae from each batch is scanned using a Pupae Size Scanner. The separation of male and female pupae is primarily based on their size differences.
The Pupae Size Scanner measures the size distribution of male and female pupae in each batch.
The system quickly analyses pupal size distribution, allowing the team to select the optimal sieve size and minimise the chance of female pupae slipping through with the males during the sorting process.
Male pupae are smaller than female ones, so the pupae are sorted through sieves that sift out the smaller males and collect them separately.
A pupa separation system with changeable sieve sizes is used to separate the male and female pupae.
And as an added safeguard, every batch of sorted pupae undergoes low-dose X-ray irradiation to sterilise any females that may have slipped through, before release.
The most pampered mosquitoes you’ll ever meet
Then, these sorted male Aedes aegypti pupae are counted and dispensed into the lids of mosquito launchers.
The lids are attached onto the mosquito launchers, where the pupae will emerge into adult male Aedes aegypti mozzies.
Of course, the pampering doesn’t stop at the premium fish food of their baby era.
…
summary: Don't worry, these mosquitoes do not bite.
title: We Went Behind The Scenes Of Project Wolbachia To See How Dengue Control Works

Hiking trails in Singapore
Sure, Singapore may be teeny tiny. We don’t have our own Alps, or the extremely long Trans Bhutan Trail . But our Little Red Dot happens to be pretty green, with loads of nature parks we can pop by, or even cycle through with its many long-distance cycling routes .
We’ve got easy peasy hikes as short as 0.4km to challenging ones stretching 150km. Young or old, beginner or fitspo, there’s going to be something for you in the mega-list of 50 walking and hiking trails below:
All you need to know before hiking in Singapore
The great thing about hiking in Singapore is that there isn’t much to prepare beforehand. A pair of walking shoes is really all you need, even for the hardest trails. Trade them for trail-running shoes or boots if you’re worried about slipping on some of the muddier routes.
There’s no recommended attire but long pants or leggings will prevent mozzie bites. If you’re going for a tank top and shorts combo, just be sure to slather on sunscreen and insect repellent so you don’t end up burnt or covered in itchy bites. You’re pretty much good to go from here.
That said, it’s the weather that can make hiking strenuous. The heat and humidity can drain you fast, so bring along plenty of water and snacks to keep hydrated and fuelled.

Ah, these cake delivery services in Singapore make life oh-so-easy when you have a sweet tooth. Head to the website or dial a number, and you’ll have a decadent cake right at your doorstep. We’ve trawled the island for rich chocolate cakes, bespoke creations, the most exquisitely crafted cheesecakes in Singapore , and the best tiramisu in Singapore , and brought you our personally vetted selection. Some of these brands offer same-day cake delivery in Singapore, so there’s no reason not to satisfy your cravings. Psst: on your special day every year, look towards our guide on the best birthday cakes in Singapore !
Why trust this guide
Our food writers have sampled our way through Singapore’s cake shops, across every neighbourhood and price point, so our recommendations come from personal experiences, not press releases. We only include brands we love and would go back to (or already have), and we update our food guides regularly to make sure nothing on the list has slipped and all information is accurate. Honeycombers has been covering Singapore’s food scene for over 15 years, so we know what a great spot looks like here – and what doesn’t make the cut.

Photography: Yuki Ling
Searching for Instagram-worthy cakes that taste as good as they look? Look no further than Cakebar. Crafted with premium ingredients, these artisanal cakes have us falling in love at first bite. From rich, decadent chocolate to unique French flavours, the wide variety will leave you happily spoilt for choice. If you still can’t decide, get the miniature versions to try a bit of everything.
We went for the signature creations and were not disappointed to say the least. Those who like your desserts rich and indulgent will adore the Earl Grey sea salt hazelnut cake. Bite into layers of airy Earl Grey chiffon cake complemented with creamy praline buttercream and crunchy roasted hazelnuts. If you prefer lighter flavours, go for the refreshing osmanthus oolong cake topped with floral jelly, or the strawberry lemon pistachio featuring moist lemon sponge and luscious strawberry cream.

body:
Tiong Bahru Bakery has giant croissant from 6 November
Tiong Bahru Bakery is launching its most ambitious creation yet. From 6 November to 31 December 2026 , look forward to The Grand Croissant ($29.90++) , measuring a whopping 28cm long.
The fun doesn’t stop there; they’re bringing the viral crombolinis to Singapore, which are a croissant-bombolini hybrid. And the icing on the cake are three new limited-time viennoiseries: Kra Pao Chicken Pain Suisse ($8++), Mochamisu Croissant ($8.50++), and Maple Pecan Pear Croissant ($7.50++).
They are also running a promotion during this period: get a free Signature Kouign Amann for every three crombolinis purchased, available at all outlets.
Let’s talk about the giant croissant. For those worried the pastry’s size might affect its flaky texture, we’re happy to report it’s just as light and buttery as you’d expect a regular croissant to be. The dough was perfectly laminated, making for a layered, airy cross-section.
It’s served with three dipping sauces: Jalapeno and Cheese , Strawberry Cheesecake , and Caramel Toffee Brittle.
The jalapeno cheese sauce had an intense umami flavour with a spicy kick from the jalapeno, while the strawberry cheesecake was tangy and mild, similar to strawberry yoghurt. My favourite was the caramel toffee sauce, which tasted exactly how you’d expect: deeply sweet with burnt sugar notes.
If you’re getting it to go, it comes in an adorable takeaway box that’s sure to turn a few heads. Preorder here !
The crombolinis come in six flavours: Truffle Mushroom ($8++), Biscoff ($6.80++), Raspberry Mascarpone ($7.50++), Pistachio ($8++), Hazelnut Chocolate ($6.80++), and Monster Curry ($8++) , a special collaboration with the popular restaurant.
The Monster Curry Crombolini reminded us of an upgraded curry puff, with a similar savoury filling encased in a softer, slightly sweeter pastry that complemented the rich curry nicely.
I also enjoyed the Truffle Mushroom—the sauce was creamy and rich, with a strong umami flavour. It was also piled high with shimeji mushrooms, adding a nice chewy texture.
The sweet selection was incredibly decadent, as each crombolini was filled to the brim with a rich cream. The pistachio stood out for its intensely nutty flavour.
The limited-time viennoiseries are also worth a try. Savoury folks can get the Kra Pao Chicken Pain Suisse , inspired by the Thai basil chicken dish.
However, as a certified sweet tooth and coffee addict, the Mochamisu, a tiramisu-and-mocha-inspired flavour, and Maple Pecan Pear truly hit the spot.
If you’re around the Tiong Bahru area, here are the best Tiong Bahru market stalls for dragon fruit cheong fun, kway teow and more. And for more cafes to check out, here are the best cafes in Singapore you must try.
Website | Full list of locations
Tiong Bahru Bakery is not halal-certified.
20 Best Tiong Bahru Market Stalls For Famous CKT, Dragon Fruit Cheong Fun And More
Photos taken by Genecia Tan.
This was a media tasting at Tiong Bahru Bakery.
summary: Tiong Bahru Bakery is launching a new giant croissant, alongside six flavours of the viral crombolinis and three limited viennoiseries.

Telok Ayer food guide
Telok Ayer is packed with cafes known for their chic interiors and chill brunches. Amoy Street Food Centre is nearby too. But if you think that is all to Telok Ayer, you are missing out. Here are some underrated Telok Ayer food places that we like.
1. Daily Beer
Popular Korean fried chicken chain Daily Beer opened its first outlet in Singapore sometime in May 2024, making it one of the most vibey chimaek spots in the CBD. We recommend getting the crowd-favourite Angry Bird , which is essentially tender, deep-fried chicken priced at $32++ for eight pieces. Pair this with their toasty Cheese Balls ($12++ for five) , featuring mozzarella cheese packed in a mochi-like fried ball. Your experience isn’t complete without having their craft beers, where there are seven flavours to choose from. Prices range from $13++ to $17++ .
Read our Daily Beer feature .
Address: 212 Telok Ayer Street, Singapore 068645
Opening hours: Mon-Thurs, Sat 11:30am to 11pm, Fri 11:30am to 12:30am, Sun 11:30am to 10pm
Tel: 6669 8090
Website
Daily Beer is not halal-certified.
Daily Beer: Popular Korean Fried Chicken And Craft Beer Chain Opens In SG
2. Toku Nori
Toku Nori is a Japanese restaurant serving up handrolls, appetisers, and a variety of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages. The restaurant is a quick three-minute walk from Telok Ayer MRT Station ! During our visit, we enjoyed the Wagyu & Uni ($16++) handroll, starring Wagyu karubi, Hokkaido uni, and caviar. An equally delicious alternative is the Foie Gras ($16++) handroll, featuring aburi foie gras topped with a spicy leek and garlic soy glaze. Substantiate your meal with the sweet-salty Chicken Ribs ($14++) : crispy, fried chicken ribs covered in yakisoba sauce.
Read our Toku Nori feature .
Address: 200A Telok Ayer Street, Singapore 068638
Opening hours: Daily 12pm to 2:30pm, 5:30pm to 11pm
Tel: 8082 6536
Website
Toku Nori is not halal-certified.
Toku Nori: New Japanese Specialty Restaurant With Wagyu, Uni, And Foie Gras Handrolls In Telok Ayer
3. L’antica Pizzeria da Michele
L’antica Pizzeria da Michele is one of Naples’ oldest pizzerias and has been around since 1870. Good news: their Club Street outlet marks the restaurant’s first outlet in Southeast Asia! If you don’t know what to get, start with the classic Margherita ($28++) , featuring tomato sauce, Pecorino Romano DOP, Agerola fior di latte (fresh mozzarella), and some basil. For those who prefer punchy flavours, get the Cetara ($36++) instead. You get the same toppings in the Margherita, as well as Cetara anchovies, Leccino olives, and capers.
Read our L’antica Pizzeria da Michele review .

4. Moss Cross Tokyo
Moss Cross Tokyo has opened their first overseas outlet in Singapore. This is an omakase restaurant that fuses both French and Japanese cuisine, creating new and interesting dishes you can look forward to. Last time we went, we tried their Wakon-Yosai ($150++ per person) , which came in a beautiful platter with nine mini plates of assorted starters.
Check out our Moss Cross Tokyo review .

This Tokyo Restaurant Opens In SG With $69++ Omakase, Their First Overseas Outlet
5. Um Yong Baek
For legit Busan-style pork rice and soup, head to Um Yong Baek , a popular Korean restaurant in Telok Ayer. Visit during lunch for their signature Dwaeji Gukbap, a traditional dish that originated during the Korean War. The UYB Clear Daejigukbab ($22++) is a must-try; you get a clear broth that’s uber flavourful yet light, boiled for at least eight hours to fully extract the rich essence of the pork. It’s also packed with a generous mix of pork collar, tender pork cheek, and pork stomach, atop a bed of short-grain rice. If you’re here for dinner, the restaurant offers Korean BBQ instead!
Read our Um Yong Baek review .

Is Um Yong Baek’s Famous Korean Pork Soup Still Worth The Hype?

ICYMI, Thachang has moved to Telok Ayer after the closing of Golden Mile Complex. This restaurant is known for their Special Pork Boat Noodle ($10.90++). Our favourite was the Special Beef Boat Noodle Soup ($11.90++) for its rich and robust beef broth.

A Hot Hideout and PlayMade launch mala pearls
When people online joked about the ultimate Orchard Central itinerary, it went something like this: mala at Yang Guo Fu Mala Tang, a sweet treat at Yo-Chi , and a drink to cool down at Molly Tea or CHAGEE. Now, two brands, A Hot Hideout and PlayMade , are taking things a step further by combining mala and bubble tea into one unlikely creation.
A Hot Hideout Review: Is This Famous SG-Born Mala Chain Still Worth The Hype?
From now till 6 November 2026 , fans can try the new Mala Pearls , available at selected PlayMade and A Hot Hideout outlets. Get them at PlayMade outlets for $1.40 or $1.60 for a medium or large size , respectively, or at A Hot Hideout for $0.60 with drinks and $1.20 with food.
Don’t knock it before you try it; the pearls are perfectly QQ with a slight sweetness, paired with the familiar kick of mala.
Drench them in your mala tang so the pearls soak up all of their collagen goodness and, in turn, lend a hint of sweetness to the broth.
Or if you’re a purist, get them in PlayMade’s signature Taiwan Milk Tea with Mala Pearls for a spicy rendition of the beloved drink. The rich creaminess of the milk tea mellows out the fiery kick of the mala pearls, resulting in an addictive sweet-and-spicy combination.
PlayMade is also bringing back their fan-favourite Pomelo Blossom Milk Tea ($4.90++) —a blend of their smooth milk tea and tangy, refreshing pomelo. You can get it with the new Mala Pearls, or with the brand’s signature Pink Cactus Pearls .
That’s not all: PlayMade is also adding their aforementioned Pink Cactus Pearls to A Hot Hideout’s signature Thai Milk Tea , in both red and green milk tea flavours for just $0.60 . Alternatively, you can also pair the Pink Cactus Pearls with food for just $1.20 .
If you’re unimpressed with the size of the Mala Pearls, go biiig with their Mega Mala Boba (price TBD) , a Halloween-exclusive special that’s only available on 31 October 2026 at selected PlayMade outlets: Tampines 1 , 313@Somerset , Northpoint City , and Westgate .
Imagine a scaled-up version of the same Mala Pearls, with the same chewiness and punchy mala flavours. There are only 10 servings per outlet, so be sure to set your alarms to get there early.
Head down to your nearest A Hot Hideout and Playmade outlet to give this collab a go before it’s too late!

Newton Food Centre guide
Apart from famous food centres such as Golden Shoe and Old Airport Road Food Centre , Newton Food Centre is another popular eating spot that can satisfy your craving for hawker food. And with close to 100 stalls, it’s no wonder this food centre got chosen to be featured in Crazy Rich Asians. Here is a guide to making your experience in Newton Food Centre one that’s as memorable as Rachel Chu’s first meal here.
Local specialties
1. Hup Kee Fried Oyster Omelette
Image credit: @fantasyee08
If you spot a stall with a beeline of customers, chances are the stall belongs to Hup Kee . Ever since their days in Glutton’s Square at Orchard Road in the 1960s, Hup Kee has been known for their tasty Fried Oyster Omelette ($8/$10/$12) . This dish consists of starchy egg batter that turns into a crispy omelette upon frying, and each plate comes with huge juicy oysters. Fresh parsley is served as a garnish, alongside house-made chilli.
Read our Hup Kee Fried Oyster Omelette review .
Unit number: #01-73
Opening hours: Wed-Sat 5:30pm to 12am
Hup Kee is not halal-certified.
Hup Kee: Must-Try Oyster Omelette With Plump Oysters In Newton Food Centre, Open Since 1966
2. Heng Carrot Cake & Oyster Omelette
Image credit: Sophia Ho via Google Maps
Heng Carrot Cake & Oyster Omelette is on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list for good reason. Its owner has been serving up fried carrot cakes for over 50 years, and they are fried with an improvised, agak agak feel that lends a medley of textures to the dish. Both Black or White Carrot Cakes go from $5 , with the mixed plate priced at $8 . You can also go for the Oyster Omelette (from $8) as an alternative to those at Hup Kee.
Unit number: #01-28
Opening hours: Wed-Mon 6pm to 11pm
Heng Carrot Cake & Oyster Omelette is not halal-certified.
3. TKR Satay
Image credit: @feedmethatnow
Satay makes a good choice if you don’t want something too heavy. There are several satay stalls in Newton Food Centre, but the sticks of satay from TKR Satay are exceptionally juicy. The stall offers choices of Chicken, Mutton, and Pork Satay priced at $1 each . The meat has a charred aroma from being barbecued over a bed of charcoal, and is irresistible when dunked in chunky peanut sauce served on the side.
Unit number: #01-33
Opening hours: Wed-Mon 4pm to 12:30am
TKR Satay is not halal-certified.
4. Kwee Heng Duck Noodle
Image credit: @terenceongwh
Featured in the Michelin Bib Gourmand 2023 list , Kwee Heng offers an extensive menu of roast chicken and duck dishes. But the one to go for is their Braised Duck Rice ($5/$6/$7) or Braised Duck Noodle ($5/$6/$7). They sell out quickly even with the stall’s short opening hours, so make sure to head down early. To amp it up, request a bowl of herbal soup on the side for when the noodles get dry. The soup has a strong herbal taste but is surprisingly pleasant on the palate.
Unit number: #01-13
Opening hours: Mon-Tue, Thu-Sat 8:30am to 9pm
Kwee Heng is not halal-certified.
Here Is The Full List Of Michelin Bib Gourmand Winners In Singapore For 2023
5. Kwang Kee Teochew Fish Porridge
Michelin Bib Gourmand-minted Kwang Kee Teochew Fish Porridge is where you want to go for comfort food when you’re at Newton Food Centre. The stall has over 60 years of legacy, and is run by a second-generation hawker. They sell all the usual suspects found at a fish soup stall, including Fried Fish Soup (from $6) and Dual Fish Soup (from $7) . The bantang fish here is sweet and fresh, complementing their flavourful, light Teochew-style broth that is slowly simmered from fish bones.
Read our Kwang Kee Teochew Fish Porridge review .
Unit number: #01-20
Tel: 9769 9893
Opening hours: Tue-Sun 11am to 8pm
Kwang Kee Teochew Fish Porridge is not halal-certified.
Kwang Kee Teochew Fish Porridge Review: Michelin Bib Gourmand Fried Fish Soup In Newton
6. Hajah Monah Kitchen
Image credit: Shengyang Yu via Google Maps
For a hearty meal, head to Hajah Monah Kitchen for a plate of nasi padang! This stall is known for their delicious and extensive range of liao. Some examples include their Chicken Wing (from $1.50) , Squid (from $3) , and Beef Rendang (from $5) . Many customers sing praises about the beef rendang, as it’s said to be tender and rich thanks to the robust gravy.
Unit number: #01-83
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 7am to 2pm
Hajah Monah is Muslim-owned.
7. Indian Kitchen
Image credit: S. via Google Maps
Indian Kitchen is where you can get some legit naan. Many customers would always buy either a piece of Garlic Naan ($2.50) or Butter Naan ($3) to go along with their mains which goes to show how irresistible these can be. Also, many vegetarians love their wide menu offerings such as Veg Fried Rice ($4.60), Chilli Paneer ($10) , and Aloo Gobi ($7) —stir-fried potatoes in aromatic spices.
Unit number: #01-44
Opening hours: Daily 11:30am to 11:30pm
Website
Indian Kitchen is not halal-certified.
8. Newton Old Signboard 25
Image credit: Jes Jassi via Google Maps

body:
You are never short on options at Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre , but surely not all of them are good, right? Well, I went down to try a stall that not many have talked about: Takdenama . Since 2018, Takdenama has been serving homemade nasi goreng , the kind you might find in most Malay homes. But that begs the question: if I can have it at home, why would I buy it when I’m out?
With this review, I intend to answer that question. What truly sets them apart from a nice home-cooked meal, which I could get for free? This is probably biased, but I’m fairly certain their nasi goreng doesn’t come close to my grandma’s.
What to order at Takdenama
One of the things that impressed me was the variety of nasi goreng styles. None were too unfamiliar, but seeing all those variations on one menu was quite the surprise. It was kinda like Pokémon ; you didn’t really realise how many there were until you looked at the whole list. I decided to go with one I was familiar with and one I wasn’t.
I got the Nasi Goreng Pattaya (S$7) and Nasi Goreng Ayam Black Pepper (S$7) . Maybe it’s just a Geylang thing, but the food was prepared staggeringly fast. Both plates were ready in less than 5 minutes, which is very impressive. I was trying to photograph the makcik frying the rice, but she plated my dish before my camera could even focus.
First, the Nasi Goreng Ayam Black Pepper , a version I had yet to try at the time. While not uncommon, I would still consider it underrated and under most people’s radar.
To be frank, it was a little disappointing. The rice, while fried nicely and perfectly separated, was one-dimensional. The taste of sambal was barely noticeable, but I was pleasantly surprised by the smoky wok hei flavour. The black pepper chicken added a change of scenery, but that change held my attention only briefly.
The sauce was too sweet, as the kicap manis (sweet soya sauce) was a bit overpowering. You could only slightly taste the black pepper. I will say I liked that they used whole peppercorns, as the crunch gave the dish a much-needed kick. I would recommend they maybe reduce the soya sauce slightly. Some lemon, calamansi or something sour would balance the dish, and chopped chillies fried with the rice would be nice as well. Overall, it was not too bad.
We tried Singapore’s highest-rated zi char
Now the Nasi Goreng Pattaya was a surprise. Aside from your regular nasi goreng, I would consider it a basic variation. They say, ‘If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it’, and this dish proves it.
Nasi Goreng Pattaya has two important components: the omelette and, of course, the nasi goreng itself. Ideally, the omelette has to be almost paper-thin, without any holes. You would then draw whatever you like on top using sweet chilli sauce. This is very reminiscent of omurice , a fried rice variant from Japan.
As we pierced the omelette shell, we were rewarded with a treasure trove of goodies. I expected it to be the same rice we had for the Nasi Goreng Ayam Black Pepper , but boy was I wrong. There were many toppings, from thinly diced cabbage and green onion to thick fishcake and chunky shrimp. My colleague Aaron and I were both surprised.
As I took a bite, I tasted a medley of flavours. The slightly sweet and meaty shrimp, the bouncy fish cakes and the cabbage added a very light crunch to the entire affair. The best part? The wok hei was much more prominent in this dish. My only complaint was that after a while, the rice covered by the omelette was slightly mushy. I’d suggest just mixing everything, but my OCD didn’t let me do it myself.
Who is Takdenama best for?
I think this stall is perfect for someone who wants something very quick and satisfying. Based purely on what I ordered, each nasi goreng seems distinct from the others, yet that unmistakable rustic flavour ran through both dishes. If you’re on lunch and having a particularly bad day at work, I’d suggest paying this place a visit. Nothing like a taste from home away from home, to lighten the mood.
How to get to Takdenama
There are a few ways to get to Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre. If you are taking the bus, there is a stop opposite the market called Joo Chiat Complex , and another behind it called Block 416 .
If you are taking the MRT, the closest stop is Paya Lebar (green line), around an 8-minute walk away. Once you reach the market, the stalls are on the second floor, so take the escalators at the centre of the building. Do note that some stalls at Geylang Serai accept only cash , so be sure to bring some. While Takdenama accepts PayNow, some of the drink stalls may not.
Do we recommend Takdenama?
…
summary: Takdenama is a nasi goreng stall on the second floor of Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre, serving homemade-style fried rice since 2018. Its Nasi Goreng Pattaya (S$7), wrapped in a thin omelette with fishcakes, shrimp and cabbage, stands out more than the sweeter Nasi Goreng Ayam Black Pepper (S$7). Fast service and generous portions suit a quick lunch, with breakfast available from 7am.

body:
A Walk Through Time 2026
There was a time when going online meant hogging the home phone line, sitting through the screech of a dial-up modem, and hoping nobody picked up the receiver halfway through your MSN chat or Adobe Flash games. Holiday photos lived in physical photo albums, songs were enjoyed via cassette tapes or CDs, and the bulky family computer came with a strict time limit enforced by a parent hovering nearby.
Fast forward to today, and the phone in your pocket handles all of that before breakfast. Now AI can draft your emails and plan your next vacation, and a world of info and entertainment is perpetually at our fingertips. It’s easy to forget how many times our gadgets have been swapped out in a single lifetime.
That’s the whole idea behind A Walk Through Time , a free exhibition by Skills Development Academy (SDA) that takes you from the tech you grew up with to the AI tools of today, one item at a time. Warning: you’ll be flooded with major nostalgia as you course through the exhibition zones.
Old-school tech you’ll definitely remember owning
Before we get to the exhibition, here’s a quick memory test. If you grew up in Singapore in the 80s, 90s, or early 2000s, at least a few of these probably passed through your hands, and every one of them will be on display at A Walk Through Time, happening from now till 20th Dec 2026 at various malls throughout Singapore:
• A pager that always beeped at the worst possible time
• A Nokia 3310, plus all the hours lost to Snake and Snake II
• A Walkman, with a pencil on standby for tangled tape
• A phone card tucked in your wallet for the payphone outside school
• Floppy disks for school projects, labelled in marker
• A chunky TV that needed a good smack whenever the picture went fuzzy
If you’re nodding along, you’re exactly who this exhibition was made for. If you’ve never seen half of these, even better: it was made for you too. Yes, we’re looking at you, Gen Z and Gen Alpha youngsters who think the floppy disk in the universal “Save” icon is a vending machine .
A look at how tech has changed our lives
A Walk Through Time is a free interactive exhibition by Skills Development Academy, an adult training provider that has helped over 150,000 Singaporeans develop practical, future-ready skills.
You’ll start with familiar setups and nostalgic items from the past, then make your way to the AI era we’re living in today. For those who grew up with the retro items, it’s a reminder of how far things have come. For younger visitors, it’s a rare chance to see the gadgets their parents won’t stop talking about.
The best part: admission is free, so it makes for an easy family outing on a weekend. They’re also conveniently located at malls throughout Singapore, so you’ll be able to jalan jalan and makan before and after the exhibition, all while escaping the heat and haze in a comfortable air-con space.
What to expect at A Walk Through Time
Take a stroll down an immersive Memory Lane setup
The first zone is Memory Lane , a row of setups that look like they were lifted straight out of an 80s or 90s HDB estate.
Start at Mama Diam , a recreation of the neighbourhood mama shop with a coin phone, an old-school marble folding table, red plastic stools, and shelves of old-school snacks. It’s where a whole generation once blew their pocket money after school.
Over in the Retro Study Room , you’ll find a CRT monitor, a typewriter, floppy disks, and a fax machine. Plenty of us typed out our first school project at a desk exactly like this one. There was no ChatGPT back in the day to help us with our assignments. Parents, this is your cue to start the “Last time ah…” stories.
In the Retro Living Room , an old-school TV sits on a wooden cabinet alongside a VCR player, a radio cassette player, and a stack of cassette tapes. There’s a Sega Saturn by the TV, an old-school fan, and a traditional telephone set too.
It’s the kind of cosy corner where the whole family once crowded onto the sofa for the evening Channel 8 drama, back when catching up on a show meant being home when it aired. Gosh, who else misses the Golden Age of Mediacorp dramas?
Beyond the room setups, the nostalgic items showcase gathers the gadgets that defined each era in one place. Phone fans can trace the whole line-up, from the Motorola “Big Brother Big” brick phone and pagers to the Nokia 3310, Nokia 8250, Sony Ericsson W20, and BlackBerry 9790. For those who have never experienced the pre-smartphone era, these models were the heavy hitters of the time.
Music lovers get to reminisce many hours of enjoying tunes through a Walkman, Discman, and eventually an MP3 player. And on the communications and transportation front, an assortment of phone cards, old transport cards, a street directory, and a GPS device round out the collection.
Then vs now: how much our everyday tech has changed
…
summary: The exhibition runs daily from 11am to 8pm until 20 December 2026.
title: This Free Nostalgic Exhibition Lets You Relive Childhood Memories & Spot What You Remember

Opus Bay in Batam
When it comes to overseas getaways, JB isn’t the only place Singaporeans flock to; Batam is another firm favourite, known for fresh seafood, affordable spa treatments, and things to do outside the Batam city centre .
And if you’ve been to Batam more times than you can count, you’ll be glad to know that a new attraction is opening very soon. Opus Bay is a new integrated resort set to open in phases from December 2026 , giving you yet another reason to book that Batam trip for the year-end holidays.
What is Opus Bay?
An artist’s impression of Opus Bay.
Image credit: MySgProp
Located on the west coast of Batam, Opus Bay is a 125ha waterfront resort that began development in 2021 by Singapore-based property developer Tuan Sing Holdings. The resort will be Indonesia’s 1st fully integrated township , bringing accommodation, retail, and recreational facilities together in 1 destination.
Starting from December 2026 , Opus Bay will begin opening its doors with Marina Bay Ferry Cove , the resort’s very own ferry terminal, and Residence on Opus Bay , which includes the 493-room Balmoral Tower hotel.
How long will it take to get to Opus Bay from Singapore?
An artist’s impression of Marina Bay Ferry Cove.
Image credit: Opus Bay
The ferry ride from the Singapore Cruise Centre will take roughly 45 minutes , where you’ll be dropped off at Marina Bay Ferry Cove in Batam. From there, it’s a 3-minute walk to the hotel, so you can start on your getaway as soon as you step off the ferry.
Check into Batam’s largest hotel or private luxury villas
An artist’s impression of Residence on Opus Bay.
Image credit: Tuan Sing Holdings
Opus Bay’s 1st development phase will feature Residence on Opus Bay , which will offer 2 types of accommodation for guests, from hotel suites to private villas.
An artist’s impression of a room in Balmoral Tower.
Image credit: Opus Bay
Standing 35 storeys tall, Balmoral Tower will be Batam’s largest hotel when it opens in December 2026. With 493 rooms ranging from deluxe studios to 2-bedroom suites, there’ll be plenty of options for couples and families looking for a comfortable stay.
An artist’s impression of a villa in Cluny Resort.
Image credit: Residence on Opus Bay
If you’re after more space and privacy, Cluny Resort will offer 57 villas across 7 categories, with options of up to 3 bedrooms for different group sizes, so larger groups can spread out without giving up that tucked-away feel.
Shop & dine by the waterfront
An artist’s impression of Bay Boulevard Marina Promenade.
Image credit: Opus Bay
While major shopping malls are a 30-minute drive from the resort, you won’t have to venture far for retail and dining once Bay Boulevard Marina Promenade opens in early 2027 .
Spanning across 10,000sqm , the waterfront precinct will feature nearly 80 retail and dining outlets , alongside a food hall and supermarket , giving you a wide range of food and shopping options without having to leave the resort.
Stay active with padel & pickleball courts
An artist’s impression of the Sports Park.
Image credit: Opus Bay
Also set to open in early 2027 , the Sports Park will be a 5-minute walk away from Residence on Opus Bay, so squeezing in a workout during your stay won’t take much convincing.
The outdoor space will consist of 3 padel courts , including a competition-standard court, and 4 pickleball courts , surrounded by lush greenery and open skies. The Sports Park will also be open to the public, with an on-site food kiosk for light refreshments after a game.
Plan your next Batam stay with Opus Bay
With its own ferry terminal, hotel, private villas, and upcoming shopping and sports facilities, Opus Bay is shaping up to be the next easy escape from Singapore. The resort opens progressively from December 2026, so bookmark this spot if a Batam trip is on the cards.

body:
DUDU Duck Cafe in JB
Forget the usual cat and dog cafes in JB , because there’s now a new spot where you can hang out with fluffy little ducks instead. Head over to DUDU Duck Cafe , located in Tasek Central Mall , just a 20-minute drive from the JB checkpoint , where you can get up close with adorable Call ducks, snap some photos, and grab a bite while you’re at it.
The current exchange rate is RM1 = ~S$0.3 0 as of 26th October 2026.
What is DUDU Duck Cafe?
Image adapted from: Tiff & Erica Soh via Google Maps
Opened on 21st July 2026, DUDU Duck Cafe is home to a flock of white Call ducks, a breed known for their petite size, round bodies, and fluffy feathers. And yes, they’re just as adorable as they sound.
Meet 8 adorable Call d ucks
Image adapted from: Yi Ting Tay & Xin Ying Lee via Google Maps
There are currently 8 resident ducks at the cafe, each with their own name. The original residents are Dudu , Butter , Mochi , and Boba , while Sesame , Lala , Lulu , and Cheesy joined the flock in August 2026.
Image adapted from: Dudu Duck Cafe via Facebook
Unlike your usual cafe visit, you can actually spend some quality time with these feathered friends. Head into the dedicated duck-petting area , where you can interact with the ducks, give them gentle pats, and snap plenty of photos for your camera roll.
How much is admission to DUDU Duck Cafe?
Image credit: famili_setiatropika via Google Maps
Admission to the duck-petting area costs RM15 /adult (~S$4. 70 ) and RM10 /child (~S$3.10) on weekdays . On weekends and public holidays , tickets are priced at RM20 /adult (~S$6.20) and RM15 /child (~S$4. 70 ) .
Grab a bite with duck-themed drinks & desserts
Once you’ve had your fill of duck cuddles, it’s time to refuel. DUDU Duck Cafe serves up a selection of Western and Japanese-inspired dishes, along with pastries and drinks.
Image adapted from: Elizabeth Chua & Drake Zero via Google Maps
For something filling, tuck into the Japanese Chicken Katsu Curry Rice (RM24, ~S$7.4 0 ) , Mentaiko Fried Chicken Donburi (RM26, ~S$8. 10 ) , or Mushroom Carbonara Pasta (RM24, ~S$7.4 0 ) .
Those who prefer small bites can go for the Mentaiko Fries (RM26, ~S$8. 10 ) , Korean Fried Chicken (RM26, ~S$8. 10 ) , or Japanese Chicken Gyoza (RM20, ~S$6.20) .
Image credit: Edward via Google Maps
There’s also a selection of croissants and bagels, including the Hazelnut Lava Croissant (RM17, ~S$5. 30 ) , Salted Egg Lava Croissant (RM18, ~S$5. 60 ) , and Smoked Salmon Cream Bagel (RM30, ~S$9.30) .
Image credit: Gena Polycarp via Google Maps
Then wash everything down with one of the cafe’s signature drinks, such as the DUDU Strawberry Matcha (RM26, ~S$8. 10 ) , DUDU Mango Yakult (RM20, ~S$6.20) , or DUDU Chocolate Frappe (RM24, ~S$7.4 0 ) .
Image credit: Tay Ls via Google Maps
And if you’re still in the mood for something sweet, keep an eye out for the cafe’s DUDU Mango Pudding (RM18, ~S$5.6 0 ) , which comes in an adorable, wobbly duck design that’s almost too cute to eat.
Image adapted from: @dududuck.my via Instagram
Don’t miss out on their holiday-themed bites either. DUDU Duck Cafe has treats for special occasions as well, such as duck-themed mooncakes for Mid-Autumn Festival as well as duck-themed fizzy drinks embellished with cotton candy, skulls, and tiny pumpkins for Halloween.
Get your hands on limited-edition DUDU merchandise
Image credit: K Xinyi (Au Latte) via Google Maps
Want a little souvenir to remember your visit? DUDU Duck Cafe also sells its very own DUDU Duck Cap , a green baseball cap for your OOTD.
Image credit: Sook Wei Tan via Google Maps
There are also adorable duck plushies up for grabs if you’d rather bring home a cuddly version of your new feathered friends. These make for a cute little keepsake from your visit, especially if you can’t get enough of the cafe’s fluffy residents.
Visit DUDU Duck Cafe on your next JB trip
If your usual JB itinerary revolves around shopping and cafe-hopping, DUDU Duck Cafe is worth adding to the mix. After all, it’s not every day you get to sip on a matcha latte and hang out with a flock of fluffy ducks.

Woksta has wok hei pasta from $7 in Bukit Merah
You’d typically expect pasta with bold flavours and bougie plating to only be found at atas Italian restaurants , but Woksta proves otherwise. This hawker stall at ABC Brickworks Market & Food Centre in Bukit Merah has gone viral for its wok-fried pasta that blends the beloved noodle dish with local flavours.
The stall is run by Chef Henry Yong, who used to work at Michelin-approved Scandinavian restaurant Dill. He swapped out the fine dining life for a hawker stall where he can spend more time with his family and return to his first love: cooking with a wok. Despite opening only about a month ago, Woksta has gained traction for their unique local take on pasta, and we had to see if the food was worth the hype.
Woksta’s menu is straightforward, with only three choices available , each plated beautifully and paired with their signature coconut sauce that’s made in-store.
Living up to their name, all their pasta is fried with a wok to achieve wok hei, AKA that char and smoky depth of flavour.
We started our pasta feast with the Curry Fried Chicken ($7) , which was served with generous chunks of fried chicken and a medley of vegetables, including capsicum, zucchini, and onions.
Initially, I was sceptical about how the coconut sauce would pair with the various noodle dishes, but it actually blended well with the curry flavour from the noodles. The sauce was silky smooth and added a lemak touch to the dish, reminiscent of coconut milk.
This dish had the strongest wok hei, as you can see from the char on each strand of pasta.
Each chicken chunk was generously coated with curry powder, adding a subtly spicy kick in each crunchy bite.
Next we tried the Fish & Coconut ($9) . Unlike the other two variations where the coconut sauce is plated on the side, the noodles here were completely doused in the sauce. The sauce was creamy and had a strong coconut taste that was not too cloying. I liked how the onions added a nice crunch to cut through the richness, while also adding a natural sweetness.
In terms of wok hei, this dish didn’t quite have a strong char as it was creamier than the rest, but it was still pleasant to eat.
Though it looks a bit like batang fish at first glance, the fish used here is seabass, fried until golden brown for a crispy exterior. The fish itself was flaky, though it did taste a tad fishy.
Last but not least is the Laksa Seafood ($10) , which turned out to be my favourite of the lot. Though it didn’t taste entirely like laksa, I enjoyed the subtle floral note from the laksa leaves on top and the crunch from the veggies.
The sauce also had a hint of spiciness from the chilli oil. I recommend mixing it all up to marry the flavours.
As a seafood lover, I appreciated the generous portions of both prawns and sotong, which were plump and QQ, giving the dish more texture and mouthfeel.
Overall, I’d say that the food did live up to the hype. I could taste Chef Henry’s heart in each dish, and it’s definitely worth heading down to give it a try for yourself. Do note that they’re only open for three hours per day, so it’s best to come early to beat the lunch crowd.
Check out our Dirty Pasta feature on a home-based pasta store located in Bukit Batok. In other noodle news, our Ng Kuan Chilli Pan Mee feature has the scoop on their upcoming Century Square outlet.
Address: 6 Jalan Bukit Merah, #01-113, ABC Brickworks Market & Food Centre, Singapore 150006
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 11am to 2pm
Website
Woksta is not halal-certified.
Popular Ng Kuan Chilli Pan Mee To Open At Century Square This Nov
Photos taken by Genecia Tan.
This was an independent visit by Eatbook.sg.
summary: Ex-fine dining chef Henry Yong now runs a hawker stall at ABC Brickworks Market & Food Centre specialising in wok-hei pasta from $7!
title: Ex-Fine Dining Chef Opens Bukit Merah Stall Selling Wok Hei Pasta From $7

For the first time in a decade, Canton Paradise is introducing a refreshed menu featuring 20 new dishes across dim sum , seafood , claypot , and wok-fried dishes .
Fans of the restaurant’s Hong Kong-style noodles , congee , roasted specialities, and dim sum now have even more options to choose from.
Credit: Canton Paradise
A new highlight of the Canton Paradise menu is the Steamed Duo Crispy Rice Roll with Prawn Filling and Black Truffle Mushroom Filling (S$11.90) . This unique take on a dim sum staple comes with 2 kinds of fillings, each wrapped in a deep-fried golden crust and silky steamed rice sheet.
Credit: Canton Paradise
Looking for some wok hei ? The Stewed Prawn and Vermicelli with Black and White Pepper in Claypot (S$29.90) is a new seafood dish simmered in rich chicken broth. I can already smell the fragrant, smoky aroma of the peppers.
Other hearty, savoury dishes that Canton Paradise is introducing include Stir-fried Pork Collar with Organic Cauliflower (S$19.90) , Mapo Tofu with Prawn (S$18.90) , and Braised Flounder with Pork Belly, Fish Tofu and Garlic (S$27.90) .
Credit: Canton Paradise
Adding to the refreshed menu are outlet-exclusive items at Alexandra Retail Centre (ARC) and Marina Bay Sands (MBS) . Diners visiting Canton Paradise at ARC will find the new Stir-fried Tender Pork Collar with Shrimp Paste and Lettuce in Claypot (S$22.90) – a delicious trio of tender pork collar slices, crisp lettuce, and rich shrimp paste.
At the MBS outlet, patrons can explore 5 additional items , including 4 different cod dishes . Whether you like your fish steamed , crisp-fried or braised , you will find something that suits your preferences.
As of the time of writing, there is no confirmed launch date for the refreshed menu yet, though it is safe to assume it’ll be available soon. Check your nearest Canton Paradise outlet and stay tuned to the restaurant chain’s social media pages!
Time to plan for your next family gathering with Cantonese cuisine in mind.

Are you a fan of the Italian menu at Casa Vostra and La Bottega , but also don’t mind exploring a different cuisine for a change? The team behind those 2 restaurants, Chef Antonio Miscellaneo and crew, has just unveiled a new Mediterranean restaurant at Dempsey .
Petra opened on 24 October 2026 , welcoming diners to experience Mediterranean hospitality and flavours. Highlights include house-baked bread , seasonal salads , fresh seafood , grilled meats , and more.
Credit: Petra
An experience that Petra wants to create for customers is open, interactive dining moments . This can be seen from a dedicated seafood counter showcasing the day’s fresh catch, a salad bar with seasonal greens and other colours, and a bread oven that produces the restaurant’s selection of Middle Eastern flatbreads.
Credit: Petra
If you’re getting one of these freshly baked breads (S$11–S$12) , the restaurant recommends complementing them with its housemade mezze dips . Want a variety of flavours? Opt for the Mezze Dip Trio (S$32) , which comes with hummus , matbukha , and taramasalata dips .
Credit: Petra
For the mains , diners can explore dishes From the Sea and From the Land . A potential sharing dish would be the Whole grilled lavrak (Mediterranean sea bass) with rosemary marinade, parsley, crispy capers, and spicy plate (S$108) . This signature dish can serve 3–4 people .
Those who prefer something meaty can go for the Lamb leg kofte with baharat spices and chimichurri sauce (S$32) . Pair this with a drink from Petra’s wide selection of cocktails , spirits , wines , and sodas , and you’ll have a wholesome, delicious meal.
Credit: Petra
Finally, add a sweet finish to your meal with Petra’s small but mighty dessert menu . Mouth-watering items include Muhallabia baklava cream with mixed berries and crispy phyllo (S$18) , and Dubai chocolate tart with white chocolate, pistachio, and kataifi (S$26) .
If you’re anywhere near Dempsey, check out the area’s newest destination for Mediterranean food culture.
Petra

Combine an island getaway with lavish living, and you’ve got one truly indulgent holiday . If you’re searching for the best luxury resorts in Bali, these luxurious stays deliver everything from beachfront villas to jungle hideaways.
Our picks include some of the most beautiful hotels in Bali, including Ayana Resort Bali, Six Senses Uluwatu and Hanging Gardens of Bali. Expect infinity pools, world-class spas and breathtaking ocean or rainforest views. (Psst: visit our sister site Honeycombers Bali for the inside scoop on the island!)
Best luxury resorts in Bali
1. Bvlgari Resort Bali
If you’ve ever wondered where the celebs hide out in Bali, this might be it. Bvlgari Resort Bali sits high on a 160-metre limestone cliff – which means world-class views are guaranteed. We’re talking about turquoise waters, stunning sunsets and lush nature, all accompanied by top-notch hospitality at this sophisticated luxury resort in Bali. The Italian-meets-Balinese architecture is just as stunning as the surrounding nature, with 59 exclusive villas and mansions awaiting your next adventure.
Dine at the recently-launched Il Ristorante – Niko Romito, a chic restaurant dishing up elegant plates celebrating local ingredients; dip your toes into captivating surf spots; soothe your nerves at the Bvlagri Spa (a must-try in our books); or simply lounge in your villa or along the idyllic beach. Wherever you are within this resort, you’ll be wowed by its dedicated hospitality and resplendent views.
Best for: Cliffside luxury with world-class surf spots and luxe dining
Room rates: From approx. $1,800 per night
Key highlights: Perched on a limestone cliff; turquoise water beaches; The Bvlgari Spa
Address: Bvlgari Resort Bali , Banjar Dinas Kangin, Jl. Goa Lempeh Uluwatu Bali, Pecatu, Kec. Kuta Sel., Kabupaten Badung, Bali 80364, Indonesia
2. Grand Hyatt Bali
Photography: Grand Hyatt Bali
Fancy staying at the biggest resort in Nusa Dua? Grand Hyatt Bali promises a family-friendly escape that’s a mere 15 to 20 minutes drive from Ngurah Rai International Airport. With 636 rooms, including swanky suites and lavish villas, expect panoramic views that’ll take your breath away. Here, you can wake up to serene garden views or the gentle waves of the ocean right from your private balcony.
Say goodbye to surprise expenses with Grand Hyatt Bali’s Club & Suites Indulgence package. This comprehensive, family-friendly package includes USD100 resort credit, which you can spend indulging in gourmet dining, invigorating spa treatments, and curated resort activities. Add to that a stay in the luxurious Club rooms or suites, alongside all-day refreshments and sunset cocktails at the Grand Club Lounge, and that’s your holiday agenda complete. Alternatively, go all in with the resort’s all-inclusive food and beverages offer, which comes with all three meals and free-flow alcoholic beverages, two hours of Oceania Kids Club access, five resort photoshoots, and 30% off selected dining, spa treatments, and resort activities. That’s all settled!
Best for: A family-friendly, beachfront escape
Room rates: Standard rates from US$160++ per night; Club & Suites offer from US$280++ per night
Key highlights: All-inclusive family packages, including food and drinks; convenient location near airport; lush gardens
Address: Grand Hyatt Bali , Kawasan Wisata Nusa Dua BTDC, Jl. Nusa Dua, Benoa, South Kuta, Badung Regency, Bali 80363, Indonesia
3. Hotel Indigo Bali Seminyak Beach
Photography: Hotel Indigo Bali Seminyak Beach
Beachfront location, striking interiors, and plenty of good food under one roof – Hotel Indigo Bali Seminyak Beach ticks all our boxes for a Seminyak getaway. Located in the heart of Seminyak, this five-star beachfront resort puts a contemporary spin on Balinese culture: think bold colours, geometric patterns and woven textures alongside thoughtful nods to traditional craftsmanship.
There’s plenty to explore without leaving the resort, especially when hunger strikes. Take your pick from Southeast Asian fare at Makase, a ‘borderless’ menu by the beach at SugarSand, or a laid-back coffee break at Pottery Cafe. Other spots dotted around the property include Tree Bar, Cave Pool Lounge and more, so you won’t be short of options throughout your stay.
That said, it’s the design that makes this resort particularly memorable. Rather than simply adding a few traditional touches to an otherwise contemporary space, the interiors weave elements of local heritage throughout the property, reimagining Balinese storytelling through a colourful, modern lens.
Best for: A tropical getaway in the heart of the lively Seminyak area
Room rates: From $320 per night
Key highlights: Seven unique restaurants; Sava Spa
Address: Hotel Indigo Bali Seminyak Beach , Jl. Camplung Tanduk No.10, Seminyak, Bali, Kabupaten Badung, Bali 80361, Indonesia

Christmas log cakes for 2026 are now on sale at three Singapore hotels, with voco Orchard’s D9 Cakery opening pre-orders on 2 November for a S$115 Strawberry Yuzu Log, on voco Orchard Singapore ‘s festive menu. The Fullerton Hotel has cut its Pistachio & Raspberry Yule Log to S$66, and Holiday Inn Singapore Atrium has a new calamansi log at an early-bird S$78.40.
The Pistachio & Raspberry Yule Log. Photo: The Fullerton Hotel Singapore
The Fullerton Hotel Singapore
The Pistachio & Raspberry Yule Log weighs 900g and comes in red and green. It is built from pistachio joconde, raspberry marmalade and Opalys namelaka. It costs S$66 in the online shop, down from S$88.
Orders need at least four days’ notice, and the last day to order is 21 December. Collection and delivery run from 20 November to 27 December.
Collection is daily from 10am to 7pm at The Fullerton Cake Boutique in the hotel lobby, except on 24 and 25 December, when it moves to the TDB Function Room on B1. Delivery is S$50 nett per location, and free for single orders above S$500 nett.
voco Orchard Singapore
D9 Cakery has two logs this year:
• Strawberry Yuzu Log, S$115: strawberry Bavarian mousse, yuzu curd and Valrhona Manjari ganache
• Mango Lime Gula Melaka Log, S$105: mango and kaffir lime mousse, gula melaka curd, apricot compote and dark chocolate ganache
Pre-orders run from 2 November to 18 December, with collection and delivery from 24 November to 28 December. There is no delivery on 24 and 25 December.
Citibank and OCBC cardholders and IHG One Rewards members get 15 per cent off. The festive menu also has Panettone at S$65, Christmas Stollen at S$40 and Christmas Fruit Cake at S$60. Enquiries go to +65 6730 3392.
The D9 Cakery Christmas menu. Photo: voco Orchard Singapore
Holiday Inn Singapore Atrium
The new Calamansi & Caramel Miso Log Cake weighs 1kg and serves eight to 10. It pairs calamansi with caramel miso.
The regular price is S$98, and the early-bird price on the hotel’s online store is S$78.40.

My first visit to Matsuya in Sapporo, Hokkaido, in 2019 was an unforgettable one. Just outside the entrance, my phone flashed an earthquake alert, and seconds later, the ground began shaking furiously beneath my feet. While the locals barely batted an eyelid, I froze in shock.
Thankfully, the piping-hot beef rice bowl waiting for me soon brought me back to my senses. Who knew that 7 years later, I’d be reunited with Matsuya, this time at Suntec City ’s basement in Singapore?
Located directly opposite Fish & Co., the eatery features self-service booths and spacious seating. The menu offerings mimic the ones you’ll find in Japan — an assortment of rice bowls including Unagi and Japanese curry .
Of course, we had to give the classic Gyumeshi Beef Bowl (S$5.50 for small) a try. There are also other sizes available – – – from Medium (S$5.90) to Double (S$10.90) . Savoury and tasty, the thin beef slices went well with the sweet onions and rice. Compared to its competitors, the beef at Matsuya offered a meatier bite with a leaner ratio of fat. We also added a Soft-Boiled Egg (+S$1.50) for maximum indulgence. Trust me, its worth it!
Our favourite was the Gyumeshi topped w/ Green Onion & Mentaiko Mayonnaise (S$8.50 for small) . Don’t be fooled by the intimidating sight of the green onion; it actually works! The combination of spring onions, creamy mentaiko , beef slices, and seaweed had multi layers of flavour that danced in my mouth.
We also tried the Soft Boiled Egg & Hamburg Steak with Tomato Sauce Set (S$13.50) which is known to be very popular in Japan. The meat was juicy and hearty, pairing perfectly with the tomato sauce and runny egg. The set comes with rice, miso soup, and a salad with mashed potato. To switch up the flavour, you can help yourself to the condiments on the table: Ponzu Citrus Sauce , Garlic Flavoured BBQ Sauce , Sesame Sauce , and more!
Come savour 60 years of hard work and dedication at Matsuya. For the best experience, we recommend ordering one variety of beef bowl each to share amongst your dining party.
Do note on the following:
• The restaurant is currently at its soft launch phase and will be operating from 11am to 3pm and 5pm to 11pm only
• The restaurant will be closed on Fri, 30 Oct 2026
• Chicken dishes will not be available during the soft launch and grand opening week
• Grand opening will be on Sat, 31 Oct 2026
10 best wallet-friendly Japanese hawker stalls in Singapore
summary: Matsuya’s Suntec City outlet serves Japanese-style beef bowls, rice bowls and set meals, with prices starting at S$5.50 for a small Gyumeshi Beef Bowl. Located in the basement opposite Fish & Co., the self-service eatery offers familiar options such as mentaiko mayonnaise beef bowls and hamburg steak sets, making it a practical choice for diners seeking affordable Japanese meals in central Singapore.
title: 60-year-old Japanese beef rice bowl chain opens 1st outlet in Singapore

Do you love to #supportlocal as I do? We’re in luck this weekend with the second edition of The Makers Ground . It returns to Singapore EXPO on 31 Oct and 1 Nov 2026 , 10am – 6pm daily . This indoor creative market will bring together nearly 50 homegrown brands across Level 1 and 2 of Foyer 2 . It will feature handmade crafts, artisanal goods, fresh produce, plants, pottery and more. It’s basically a haven for people who love discovering unique handmade products while supporting our homegrown businesses.
Credit – The Makers Ground
Organised by Singapore EXPO and BlueAcres Pte. Ltd., the market offers visitors an opportunity to browse products from local makers and chat with them. You can learn more about the craft behind their creations as well. Best of all, admission to The Makers Ground is completely free , so why not drop by?
Credit – The Makers Ground
If you’re interested in local produce, some brands you should take note of are: Herb Route Growing Solutions and Wendy’s Kampong Garden , among others. Do you always eyeball it while measuring stuff? Test out how strong your guesstimation skills are with Wendy’s Guess the Weight Challenge at Level 2 from 11.30am – 3.30pm . The closest guess of the weight of a giant melon will win you a mystery prize.
Credit – The Makers Ground
Other lifestyle brands to look out for include eueu & bunny (self-designed tote bags, prints, stickers and more), STiLL (vintage-inspired illustrations), My Lumie Scent (soft, delicate fragrances) and Cheeros Studio (sensory products such as fidget clickers). Don’t miss out on supporting Carer , a social enterprise that supports seniors through meaningful activities and care services. Products such as handcrafted bag charms made by carers and seniors from its activity clubs will be available at this market.
There will also be live performances by local duos. Plus, try your luck at their Spin & Win to win exciting prizes from participating vendors. Be sure to head down and discover your personal favourite brand and band this weekend!
My 10 favourite local lifestyle brands that make life bright & pretty
summary: The Makers Ground returns to Singapore EXPO on 31 Oct and 1 Nov 2026, featuring nearly 50 homegrown brands across handmade crafts, local produce, plants, pottery and lifestyle goods. With free admission, live performances, a Spin & Win activity and a giant melon guessing challenge, the indoor market is suited to visitors looking to discover local makers and support independent businesses over the weekend.
title: 45+ local brands at The Makers Ground on 31 Oct & 1 Nov 2026

Take home unique pieces starting with ceramics by Ora Clay and Pots Kez , one-of-a-kind fully customisable watch jewellery from Requisite , aesthetic leather journals curated by Syahs Journals , candles made with love by Apricot & Co , and accessories like bedazzled Sony Angels by Jelly Bun .

If you love an Italian meal that takes its time, Gotti Italiano ’s refreshed menu is built for lingering. Gather your group and order a few plates to share.
Photo by Adoncia Ho (Confirm Good)
The plating, the appearance, the taste – 10 out of 10. A must-try appetiser is the Capasanta e N’Duja (S$36) , pan-seared Hokkaido scallops with well-seasoned Calabrian mashed potatoes and crispy splanata.
New Menu, Same Gotti
Photo by Adoncia Ho (Confirm Good)
We tried Radiatori al Pomodoro e burrata (S$32) , built around house-made radiatori and soft burrata, with hints of fresh citrus and herby basil oil. The distinctive pasta shape, made from scratch every morning and refreshing tomato-based flavour profile elevated the eating experience. Easily my personal favourite! Another unique pasta worth trying next is Carota Carota Carota (S$30) , entirely carrot-based , with carrot jus , crisp carrot, and carrot-leaf pesto – talk about carrot overload.
Photo by Adoncia Ho (Confirm Good)
Not into red or white sauces? There’s another way. The Aglio Olio e Gamberi (S$32) might be your next obsession. It has a creamier texture than the classic Aglio Olio, featuring house-made spaghetti tossed in a silky butter emulsion and paired with fresh tiger prawns . My recommendation for this? Devour it yourself! For a heavier pasta, the Tuccu ‘Genovese’ (S$36) features a 24-hour wine-braised Wagyu chuck roll ragout, coating the hand-shaped pici pasta with a deep, savoury flavour .
Photo by Adoncia Ho (Confirm Good)
We watched the Tonno e Cipolla Bianca (S$36) come together behind the scenes, and my mouth watered. Topped with yellowfin tuna tartare and raw onions, it had a surprisingly pleasant, flavourful taste, with pickled onion gel for a hint of sweetness. If we had the stomach space, we would’ve tried the Pumpkin Speck e Fontina Noci (S$36) – another new addition to the menu.
Photo by Adoncia Ho (Confirm Good)
All meals end with a sweet note, and the Millefoglie Alla Ciliegia (S$16) is a lovely one. Delicate layers of pastry sandwich a mascarpone cherry custard , then pair it with macerated strawberry and a lemon cherry sauce for a slight tang that keeps it from feeling too heavy. It’s a light, bright finish to a rich meal, and one we’d happily order again.

SkinSha at Plaza Singapura
If you’ve been keeping up with popular C-dramas like Pursuit of Jade and The Early Spring , you’ll know that Chinese celebs have been winning fans over with more than just their acting chops. Their flawless on-screen visuals are also enough to make us wonder what skincare products they’re using. And while we can’t promise you’ll achieve their glass-skin glow overnight, you can at least take a page out of their skincare routines.
We recently discovered SkinSha at Plaza Singapura , a beauty store carrying over 60 C-beauty brands, including products endorsed by famous Chinese celebrities. So we went down to check out what’s in store, as well as the deals that make it easier to give C-beauty a go.
Shop C-beauty brands that have a cult following in China but are lesser-known here
While big C-beauty names like Joocyee and Judydoll have already opened brick-and-mortar stores in SG, SkinSha carries brands that are less familiar to Singaporeans but have a following in China.
When we visited, the store attendant introduced us to a few of these brands, including Watercome , which is known for its moisturising and brightening bodycare products.
There’s the AHA Skin-Smoothing Fragrance Body Wash ($9.90) , which can be paired with the Whitening & Brightening Body Essence Lotion ($16.90) as a final step in your routine. The latter is designed to moisturise and brighten your skin without leaving behind that sticky, greasy feeling Singapore’s hot and humid weather makes even more unbearable.
At under $20, these products are a relatively affordable way to try a brand you might not have come across otherwise.
Another brand to look out for is GUYU , a science-powered Chinese skincare brand founded in 2016. Its products focus on anti-ageing – if you’re looking to add some TLC to your under-eye area, the store attendant specifically recommended the Whitening Luminosity Repairing Eye Cream ($49) .
What makes it stand out is that it comes with a photonic eye massager, which is designed to help the product absorb better.
Browse brands endorsed by popular Chinese celebrities
C-drama fans have another reason to pop by SkinSha: you’ll get to shop brands endorsed by your favourite Chinese celebs too!
We spotted DearIrean , a hair and bodycare brand fronted by actor Hou Minghao. Its products are known for their fresh, clean scents that can last up to 6 hours.
One of the brand’s popular picks is the Floating Water Hair Eau De Parfum , which was unfortunately already sold out when we visited. But if you’re keen to try the brand while waiting for it to restock, there’s also the Floating Water Fragrance Shower Wash ($14.90) .
While you’re browsing, you can also pick up some skincare products for your boyfriend or husband. Inoherb , fronted by Zhang Linghe, is a skincare brand whose products are formulated with Traditional Chinese Medicine wisdom in mind.
If your other half’s skin tends to get oily quickly in Singapore’s hot and humid weather, check out the Dark Tea Cooling Oil-Control Cleanser ($9.90) . Alternatively, the Dark Tea Blemish-Care Cleanser ($8.90) is formulated to target acne spots.
Both products are designed for men, so this is your chance to help him get started on a proper skincare routine without having to nag him to use yours.
Get your hands on makeup, nail products & fragrances at wallet-friendly prices
Besides skincare and bodycare, SkinSha also stocks a wide range of makeup, nail products, and fragrances.
For everyday makeup looks, the Veecci Ribbon 11-Colour Eyeshadow Palette ($13.90) comes with a mix of pink and neutral shades that are easy to work into your usual makeup routine. There are also popular picks like the MR.WISH Glue-Free Eyelashes ($11.90) , which save you the hassle of applying lash glue.
We also spotted rows and rows of quick-drying nail polishes in a variety of colours and finishes, priced at just 5 for $10 !
SkinSha also carries Inside Flow Eau de Parfum , with a 30ml bottle going for $39.90 . It’s a handy size to add to your fragrance collection, especially if you’re looking to switch up your scent without committing to a full-sized bottle.
Girlies who love having long nails can stock up on press-on nail sets at 2 for $10 . There’s a whole range of designs to choose from, including dainty and intricate patterns as well as simple everyday styles.
Each set also comes with everything you need to get your nails on, such as glue tabs and a mini nail file.
And because no makeup haul is complete without a few new lippies, SkinSha also stocks a range of MLBB (my lips but better) shades to choose from.
The Mooekiss Spotlight Dewy Plumping Lip Gloss ($9.90) is worth checking out for a juicy, glossy pout. Meanwhile, the Mooekiss Acqua Velvet Glow Lip Glaze ($9.90) comes in 4 shades, giving you a few options to switch up your look depending on your mood.
Explore health & wellness products

Ski resorts in China
When it comes to winter holidays, ski resorts in Japan are probably one of the first destinations that come to mind. But flight tickets, accommodation, ski passes, and equipment rentals can all add up, resulting in a trip that can leave quite the dent in your wallet.
So if you’re dreaming of carving through fresh snow without blowing more than your entire travel budget, consider ski resorts in China near popular cities instead. From beginner-friendly slopes to mountains that have hosted international winter sports competitions, there are plenty of options that won’t necessarily cost you an arm and a leg.
The current exchange rate is S$1 = ~RMB5.20 as of 25th October 2026, and all prices stated are only references based on the latest published prices.
Ski resorts near Beijing
1. Nanshan Ski Resort
Suitable for first-timers & day trips
Image adapted from: @美式T_T via RED
If you’re heading to Beijing and want to ski, check out Nanshan Ski Resort , located in Beijing’s Miyun District , around 1.5 to 2 hours from the city by car. The location makes it easy to squeeze into your itinerary as a day trip.
Nanshan Ski Resort has 30 ski trails catering to different skill levels, including gentle beginner slopes where first-timers can learn the ropes. There are also ski instructors available for private lessons, along with a dedicated children’s ski area for families.
Meanwhile, more experienced snowboarders can make a beeline for Nanshan Mellow Park , with obstacles for practising tricks. And if skiing isn’t quite your thing, you can still join in the fun with other snow activities such as sledding.
Image credit: Tripadvisor
The best part is you don’t have to stay overnight to make the trip worthwhile. If you’re staying around the city centre, you can take a high-speed train from Beijing Chaoyang Railway Station to Miyun Railway Station , which takes approximately 30 minutes, before transferring to the resort’s complimentary shuttle to get there.
Alternatively, drive or take a cab from central Beijing, which will get you there in approximately 1 to 1.5 hours , depending on traffic.

For those who want to spend 2 to 3 days skiing
Image adapted from: @丹哥不吃白人饭 via RED
Sometimes a quick ski session isn’t enough to satisfy your winter sports cravings. In that case, consider spending a couple of days at Wanlong Ski Resort . Located in the mountains of Chongli, Zhangjiakou , this resort has 32 ski trails spanning approximately 47km , so there’s plenty of ground to cover.
Wanlong is popular among experienced skiers and snowboarders, but newbies aren’t left out either. There are gentler beginner slopes where you can practice your turns before progressing to more difficult terrains.
Dragon Palace Hotel.
Image credit: China Holiday
Those planning to stay a couple of days can also book a room at the Dragon Palace Hotel , where you can stay close to the slopes.
When your legs are tired or numb from the cold, you’ll also get to retreat to one of the resort’s restaurants, cafes, or bars for a break. There are additional hot spring facilities where you can unwind after spending hours out in the cold.
To get there, hop on a 1 to 1.5-hour high-speed train ride from Beijing to Taizicheng Railway Station , followed by an approximately 15-minute resort shuttle ride .

For anyone who’s always dreamt of spending winter in a quaint European village, Thaiwoo Ski Resort might just be the next best thing. With its Alpine-inspired buildings, snow-covered rooftops, and surrounding mountains, the resort looks like something out of a Christmas card.

And when you’ve had enough skiing for the day, there’s an entire village to explore. You’ll find restaurants, cafes, bars, and shops, where you can enjoy a meal with mountain views or grab some souvenirs.
