‘Tis the season to be jolly and immerse yourself in the Yuletide spirit at Christmas events in Singapore. From family-friendly activities to adults-only beachside fun, there’s plenty to do in November and December. For more festive magic, make your way to Christmas markets in Singapore to tick items off your gift list!
Psst: we’re still in the midst of updating this list, so keep this page bookmarked for when we refresh it again!
Best Christmas 2026 events in Singapore
1. Singapore Symphony Orchestra’s year-end concerts
Photography: Chris P. Lim
From uplifting Yuletide tunes to Broadway and Disney hits, the Singapore Symphony Orchestra’s year-end concerts have something for everyone. Round up your loved ones, fellow musical theatre fans, or friends attending their first orchestra concert for these spectacular live music experiences at the Esplanade Concert Hall.
On 11 and 12 December 2026, the Singapore Symphony Orchestra presents its annual Christmas concert. Joined by the Singapore Symphony Chorus, the joyous celebration features traditional Christmas medley singalongs, alongside selections from Tchaikovsky’s The Nutcracker, John Rutter’s Gloria, and Thomas Hewitt Jones’ A Christmas Cracker. Oh, and keep your ears peeled for familiar Christmas carols like O Holy Night, Joy To The World and Winter Wonderland.
Next, save the dates on 17 and 18 December 2026 for On My Own: Nathania Ong with the Singapore Symphony, an evening that celebrates the best of musical theatre, Broadway and Disney. West End star Nathania Ong, accompanied by the Singapore Symphony Orchestra and fellow vocalists Preston Lim and Vanessa Kee, will perform beloved favourites from Frozen, Wicked and Les Miserables. Psst: SG Culture Pass credits are eligible for these performances, so call up your family and friends, and make the most of your credits!
Best for: First-time concertgoers and anyone who enjoys familiar musical favourites
Date: 11, 12, 17 & 18 December 2026
Time: 7.30pm
Price: From $28
Address: Singapore Symphony Orchestra’s year-end concerts , Esplanade Concert Hall, 1 Esplanade Drive, Singapore 038981
2. Christmas Wonderland 2026
Photography: Blue Sky Events
Singapore’s biggest Christmas event returns for more whimsical magic at Gardens by the Bay! This annual Christmas event in Singapore is a must-visit thanks to its sprawling event grounds filled with carnival games, opportunities to meet Santa Claus, a multitude of aesthetically pleasing photo spots, and stunning Spalliera display. Oh, and don’t forget to stroll through Mistletoe Alley’s Christmas shops for knick knacks and meet Santa Claus for photos.
Psst: full details about Christmas Wonderland 2026 have yet to be released, so keep your eye on our Christmas Wonderland guide for more info coming soon!
Date: December 2026; final dates TBC
Time: TBC
Price: TBC
Address: Christmas Wonderland , Gardens by the Bay, 18 Marina Gardens Drive, Singapore 018953
3. Christmas Train Show
Photography: Gardens by the Bay
The Flower Dome’s Christmas Train Show returns for its third edition, featuring a multitude of model trains chugging along looping tracks that roll past scenes of Singapore, the US, and Finland. It’ll wind through intricate botanical models of railway stations on the West Coast, East Coast, and American heartlands as a nod to the United States. This year, the show features several familiar landscapes celebrating Singapore’s own rail heritage with two SMRT trains running alongside reimagined MRT stations. The final stop is the snowy Rovaniemi – Santa Claus’s official hometown on the Arctic Circle.
Date: 20 November 2026 to 3 January 2027
Time: 9am to 9pm
Price: Tickets to the Flower Dome start from $12 for adults and $8 for children
Address: Christmas Train Show , Flower Dome, 18 Marina Gardens Drive, Singapore 018953
4. World Christmas Market
Photography: World Christmas Market Singapore via Facebook
With a name like that, you know it’s one of the most epic Christmas events in Singapore. A little Christmas magic is waiting to be discovered at the World Christmas Market, which will be taking its whimsy to Fort Canning Park this year! Gather your family and friends because there’ll be plenty of festive spirit to go around. We’re still awaiting final details, but we’re expecting a ton of food stalls, Christmas trinkets sold by local artisans, and many Christmas lights.
Date: 10 December 2026 to 3 January 2027
Time: Monday to Thursday, 5pm to 11pm; Friday to Sunday, 4pm to 11pm; Christmas ve & New Year’s Even, 4pm to 1am

Meet Singapore’s best mini buffet caterers, your perfect partner-in-crime for any home party, birthday, housewarming, or office bash. Thanks to their scrumptious menus, fuss-free set-ups and convenient doorstep delivery, these catering services in Singapore will save you time, stress and a whole load of dirty dishes. Plus, your guests can enjoy a gastronomic feast with local dishes, diverse international cuisines, and themed menus. Pick up the best party supplies in Singapore while you’re at it, and your celebration will be all set!
Why trust this guide
We’ve researched the mini buffet catering services on this list thoroughly, evaluating them on food quality, menu variety, dietary options, reliability, and value for different occasions – from intimate house parties to corporate needs. Where we’ve encountered these mini buffet caterers directly through our own events and community, we’ve factored that in too. Plus, we fact-check every listing to make sure it’s accurate and still operating before this guide goes live.
Our top picks for cosy parties and gatherings
If you’re searching for the best mini buffets in Singapore, here are our top picks:
• Customisable party packs: Manna Pot Catering
• Locally-inspired menus: Four Seasons Catering
• Healthier alternatives: Eatz Catering
1. Lavish Dine Catering
Photography: Lavish Dine Catering
Mini buffets that look as good as they taste? We’re swooning over the selection from Lavish Dine Catering! This halal-certified caterer, known for bespoke menus and thematic set-ups, has been dishing out epicurean experiences for over 20 years. Plus, it is the caterer of choice for esteemed clients like dignitaries and celebrities, and leading brand events. With customer needs and stellar service at the heart of everything, its premium catering services keep customers coming back.
The meticulously curated mini buffet includes the full works of salads, mains, vegetables, sides, staples and sweets. body:
133 Penang Authentic has cheap Penang food in Bukit Timah
Being half-Malaysian on my mom’s side, I’m usually sceptical about Malaysian food in Singapore, thinking it can never beat the real deal across the border. We’ll never settle the debate on Singaporean vs Malaysian food, but when I came across 133 Penang Authentic at Bukit Timah Interim Market & Food Centre, I had to put my theory to the test.
Before diving into the food, this humble hawker stall boasts quite a background. Founder and chef Gary Tan spent 10 years as an executive chef at top hotels such as Marriott and Dynasty. Trained in Western, French, and Peranakan cuisines, he’s won accolades at competitions across Asia. After two decades in fine dining, he shifted to hawker life, running 133 Penang Authentic with his wife for nearly 20 years.
All in all, he’s spent over 40 years in the food industry. When asked why he’s stayed so long, he simply attributed it to his passion for cooking. Intrigued by his decorated past, we had to see if the food lives up to the name.
Food At 133 Penang Authentic
My scepticism faded when I learned that Chef Gary and his wife, Constance, were both from Penang. Their signature dish is the Penang Char Kway Teow (from $5.50) , fried by Chef Gary himself in a massive wok.
Penang-style char kway teow features a lighter colour and milder flavour profile, unlike its Singaporean counterpart, which is darker in colour and doused in a sweet, dark soya sauce. Penang char kway teow is also known as the “white” version, and I enjoy it as it’s lighter on the palate.
As soon as it was fried up and served, I could smell the smoky aroma. True enough, it did have a strong wok hei that any good char kway teow should have. The noodles were springy, with each strand having a nice char from the wok.
There were generous amounts of liao found throughout the dish, with my favourite hum in abundance. The lup cheong was cut into small bite-sized pieces, making it easier to chew, while the tau gay was juicy and plump, adding a nice crunch alongside the crispy pork lard.
As someone with a high spice tolerance, I would have preferred it slightly spicier or served with some chilli, but it was a good plate nonetheless—I do think it’s as close to the original as it gets.
The other two dishes we ordered were cooked by Aunty Constance, and I was most excited to try the Assam Laksa ($6) as this dish is hard to come by in Singapore. Right off the bat, the broth had a brighter, more orange hue than the Penang version, which tends to be a darker red.
Our bowl came packed with ingredients, including mackerel, onions, and mint leaves. The mackerel had a salty taste, which helped cut through the sour broth. The mint leaves gave off a floral note, adding another layer of flavour in every slurp.
For the broth, it had a distinct sour and pungent aroma, though it tasted more savoury than sour. My guess is that they tweaked the recipe to suit a more local palate, but as a true Assam laksa fan, I thought the broth could be slightly spicier for that shiok kick.
It’s also served with the usual thick and slippery noodles, AKA lai fun, so I’d recommend eating it the traditional way: scooping up both the noodles and broth with a spoon to prevent unwanted mess and stains.
Moving on to the Penang Prawn Noodle (from $5) . We bought the soup version, as that’s the way it’s usually served in Penang. As a prawn mee fan, I’m happy to report that the broth was rich in umami and boasted a natural sweetness from the prawns.
Just like the other two dishes, it came loaded with ingredients, including succulent prawns and chunky pork slices.
You can’t go wrong with the classic bee hoon and yellow mee combo, which made for a massive noodle pull. Both were cooked to a QQ texture and topped with lard and a tasty sambal, which added a hint of spice when mixed with the broth. This tasted close to how I remember Penang prawn mee to be.
I particularly liked the crunchy fried onions and kang kong, which gave the dish more texture.
Ambience at 133 Penang Authentic
Image credit: Scribbling Geek via Google Maps
133 Penang Authentic is tucked in the corner of Bukit Timah Interim Market and Food Centre. We were greeted with a fairly quiet space as we arrived after peak hours, though there was still a steady stream of customers. As with any other hawker centre, it’s best to come early to avoid the lunch crowd.
Space-wise, the aisles between tables and the shops are quite narrow. Though it was breezy on the day we visited, the food centre is also equipped with fans for hotter days.
The food centre is a short three-minute walk from Beauty World MRT Station .
133 Penang Authentic – Eatbook Review
…
summary: 133 Penang Authentic in Bukit Timah has been run by award-winning chef Gary Tan and his wife for nearly 20 years.
title: This Award-Winning Chef Sells Penang CKT And Prawn Mee At Beauty World: Here’s Our Verdict

body:
Mollie Makes is a new Chinese dessert cafe in Johor Bahru
One of my favourite things to do in JB is to go dessert cafe hopping . I love travelling from matcha cafes to artisanal bakeries in search of sweet treats to satisfy my sweet tooth. Recently, I discovered Mollie Makes , a new cafe near customs serving Chinese desserts with a contemporary twist. If you’re looking for another spot to add to your JB itinerary, this one’s worth checking out.
The current exchange rate is RM1 = ~S$0.31 as of 27 October 2026.
15 Best Dessert Spots In JB For Matcha Cakes, Black Sesame Shaved Ice And More
The cafe boasts a rustic Chinese look with traditional motifs and wooden furniture that’ll send you back to Season One of The Rise of Phoenixes . There are plenty of photo spots, so be sure to get your camera ready.
As aesthetic as the spot may be, they didn’t skimp on the quality of the desserts either. You can expect a wide variety of Chinese desserts, ranging from traditional classics to modern variants.
As a pistachio fanatic , their Pistachio Beancurd Mochi (RM15.90) was basically calling my name. Imagine a bowl filled generously with pistachio-flavoured tau huay, topped with stretchy mochi and cheese foam, then garnished with chopped pistachios.
This bowl met my rather high standards for pistachio desserts: it had prominent earthy, umami pistachio flavours, without being too sweet. The mochi also added a nice textural contrast—soft and stretchy with an indulgent milky taste. The cheese foam tied the whole dessert together, adding a subtle saltiness that offset the sweetness.
My dining companion preferred the Oh Yeah! Mollie (RM14.90) , comprising a base of coconut jelly piled high with toppings, including coconut milk he fen AKA Chinese wide noodles, rose-infused chestnuts, and fresh mango cubes. It’s then finished with a heaping scoop of coconut ice cream and a sprinkle of toasted coconut.
This dessert can be described in one word: refreshing. The coconut jelly is QQ and jiggly, and reminded me of the Chinese dessert bing fen.
The coconut ice cream, on the other hand, was soft and creamy. The fragrant coconut flavour was further accentuated by the coconut he fen, which tasted very similar to actual coconut meat.
The fresh mangoes were also slightly sour, cutting through the richness of the dessert, while the rose-infused chestnuts provided a nice crunch.
To wash everything down, we ordered the Taro Milk Tea With Mochi (RM15.80) , comprising Assam milk tea zhnged up with taro paste and handmade mochi, finished with a layer of cheese foam.
If you’re an orh nee lover , this drink is basically tailor-made for you. The Assam milk tea base was quite light and fragrant, allowing the stronger-tasting yam paste to come through. The mochi also added a nice bite: it was soft and slightly chewy, making it feel more like a dessert than a drink.
Interestingly, the dessert cafe offers a lineup of fresh shio pan. We ordered their Mentaiko Shio Pan (RM8.90) , and surprisingly, it could rival my favourite salt breads. It had a crunchy, buttery base, with a soft and chewy middle, and was garnished with mentaiko mayo, seaweed, and a slab of creamy Kewpie mayonnaise.
That’s not all: the bread is split lengthwise and slathered with more creamy mentaiko mayo for added umami.
Mollie Makes is located a seven-minute drive away from CIQ Jalan Jim Quee .
For more places to tick off your JB cafe checklist, read our guide to the best cafes in Johor Bahru . Alternatively, if you have no idea on where to start, our JB food itinerary might lead you in the right direction.

Its offering covers hair design, colour, texture control, anti-frizz treatments, scalp care, head spa experiences and nail services.
The group has also received industry recognition including the Asia Honesty Enterprise Award , Asia Pacific Super Health Brand , and International Prestige Brand Award , reflecting its stated focus on quality, professionalism, service excellence and consumer trust. Bali in Singapore? Never heard of it. Welcome to Wheeler’s Tropikana ; your next summer paradise is closer than you think.
Credit: Wheeler’s Tropikana’s Facebook
Palms and lush greenery frame an open, al fresco dining area, with rattan seating, a sunny lawn, and a dipping pool at the centre. It feels more like a Bali retreat than a Singapore restaurant.
Brunch
Credit: Wheeler’s Tropikana’s Facebook
Wheeler’s Tropikana offer the kind of menu you’d expect poolside on holiday: relaxed, flavourful, and easy to graze through all afternoon. Not sure about you, but my kind of brunch calls for Omelette au Fromage (S$18) and the Pastrami Panini (S$24) . Prefer a heartier and messier kind of breakie ? The Salmon Benny (S$26) or Egg Florentine (S$24) might be your cup of tea, and it’s great for sharing.
Credit: Wheeler’s Tropikana
Wheeler’s Tropikana also serves Kombucha on Tap for S$8 per glass – Strawberry Mint, Pink Guava, and Raspberry Passionfruit. Apart from that, there’s also a Weekend Bottomless Brunch happening every Saturday and Sunday , from 11am to 4pm, priced at S$68++ for 2 hours of free-flow drinks – Red, White, Rosé, or Beer on tap.
Dinner
Credit: Wheeler’s Tropikana’s Facebook
Not a morning person? Come for slower afternoons with refreshing cocktails – Lychee or Apple Martini (S$15) and Long Island Iced Tea (S$19) , or knock yourself out with their Cocktail Jug for S$48 , with 2 kinds to choose from. Wheeler’s Tropikana is the kind of place where one drink turns into an evening. Catch the sunset with their fresh Summer Caprese (S$26) and indulge in pizza and pasta .
For a sociable evening with a bigger group, order a Rack of Lamb (S$48) with smoked tomato salsa and their special Jeju Pork Tomahawk (S$60) with charred leeks. Pair these proteins with sides of Broccolini (S$12) and Roasted Carrots (S$12) with tahini yoghurt on the side for dipping. For the crust, we can trust their Artichoke & Parma (S$26) and the Good Ole Marg (S$22) – a pizza that never goes wrong.
Credit: Wheeler’s Tropikana’s Facebook
Come for the food, stay for a good time, then linger for evening live music and DJs on certain nights. Make your retreat-worthy reservations here today!

Snoopy , Charlie Brown , and their friends are pop culture icons that have existed in my mind for as long as I can remember. Even though I’m not personally a fan of Peanuts , its characters have always popped up in my sight once in a while on TV, in a cafe somewhere, or on a shelf in a toy store.
Well, from 27 October 2026 to 19 September 2027 , this beloved gang is going to stay in our minds for a while with the Snoopy Pop-up Library at Plaza Singapura !
My colleague and I dropped by to check out the space and felt like we stepped into the world of Peanuts . If you’re a Snoopy fan or a parent who wants to spark your child’s interest in reading , you’ll love it even more!
Peanuts Brought to Life
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
The first thing you will notice at this pop-up is reading corners inspired by classic Peanuts comic strips and scenes . I had almost forgotten that these characters first existed in newspapers, but it’s nice to see this pop-up paying homage to their origins.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
You can visit a familiar bus stop , hop onto the Peanuts School Bus for a photo with Snoopy, hang out at the Snoopy Garden , or read some books with the friendly beagle in Charlie Brown’s Classroom .
If you’re a Peanuts fan, you will have fun spotting references and also find how they are incorporated into the library charming and fitting.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Some of you might be wondering whether this pop-up is only for kids and their parents. Good news for all the adult Snoopy fans – it’s not! A huge part of the library, made up of about 10,000 physical and digital books , is catered to children. However, there is also a collection suitable for all ages .
Visitors will discover popular Peanuts titles, as well as other books specially curated by the National Library & Archives Board (NLB) .
Lucy’s Book Recommendations
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
If you’re spoilt for choice and need some book recommendations, head over to Lucy’s Booth . Simply answer a few fun questions to find the perfect book for you. Fortunately, consulting Lucy is completely free of charge (not even 5 cents), and you can even print out your Reading Prescription in the form of a physical bookmark !
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
These bookmarks contain personalised recommendations based on your mood (answers) and will even direct you to parts of the library where you can find them. At the same time, they double as keepsakes that will remind you of your time at the Snoopy Library and inspire you to
summary: We stepped into the world of Peanuts at this Snoopy Pop-up Library that just opened at Plaza Singapura. Inner child activated.

body:
NLB Snoopy Pop-Up Library at Plaza Singapura
In a world riddled with 67 references and faddish TikTok dances, reading’s one way to curb the brain rot epidemic plaguing the little ones, and the National Library Board (NLB) concurs. In recent times, they’ve been going around the island setting up temporary themed libraries in a bid to keep folks – adults included – off their screens by digging into a good book.
Their earlier Sci-Fi , Star Wars , and Comics and Games Pop-Up Libraries float to mind, and now, you’ll be able to swing by one that’s inspired by the world of PEANUTS . Snoopy and gang are calling Plaza Singapura home for a bit, all nestled in a cosy reading nook that’s bound to have grown-ups and kids alike squealing with delight. Here’s all you need to know before heading down to NLB’s new Snoopy Pop-Up Library .
What is the NLB Snoopy Pop-Up Library?
The pop-up is right outside Best Denki, on Level 3 of the mall.
The Snoopy Pop-Up Library can be found in Plaza Singapura , #03-86 to 89 . Admission is free , and it’ll be up and running from now till 19th September 2027 , from 10am to 10pm daily . We recommend downloading the NLB Mobile app ( App Store | Google Play ) before visiting, as you can use it to enter the pop-up and borrow books there.
Much like its predecessors, the Snoopy Pop-Up Library is a part of ReadSG . It’s a national initiative by the NLB that encourages all to make reading a lifelong habit by making the hobby more exciting and accessible through installations integrated into everyday spaces like this one.
Also worth mentioning are the free Snoopy, Charlie & Lucy Meet & Greet sessions taking place right here. You’ll get to rub shoulders with Charlie and Snoopy on 7th and 9th November 2026 , while Lucy and Snoopy will make an appearance on 8th November 2026 . 3 sessions will be happening on each day, at 11am , 2pm , and 4pm .
What to expect at the NLB Snoopy Pop-Up Library?
Scattered around the library are the very comic strips that these faithfully-recreated sets are inspired by.
We swung by the Snoopy Pop-Up Library on its official opening day, and we were pleasantly surprised at how seamlessly it introduces the hobby of reading with a couple of intricately decorated zones. The lively colours, adorable sculptures and cutouts of the PEANUTS cast, and comfy seating areas all come together nicely to create a convivial haunt that’s bound to enthrall all visitors, bookworm or not.
But of course, books are still at the forefront of the pop-up, and there are plenty to choose from here, especially if you’re a budding reader. In order to enter, you’ll need to scan in with the eCard on your NLB Mobile app or a library-compliant card , like your NRIC, driver’s license, or school smart card.
PEANUTS School Bus
Longtime fans of Charlie Brown and his canine companion will recognise the various areas within the pop-up, as they’re all inspired by locations and beats portrayed in the comics. The first area you’ll come across is the PEANUTS School Bus .
It’s the first display you’ll see even before you step into the pop-up, as the strikingly yellow vehicle piloted by none other than Snoopy greets visitors from the outside. Inside, the beagle has thoughtfully left some space up front for you to ride shotgun, as he transports a school of Woodstocks in the back.
There’s also a bus stop set here, accompanied by a Snoopy in his flying ace getup.
Nearby, comics about Snoopy and his slice-of-life escapades are arranged neatly on a shelf for all to leaf through or borrow; in particular, there’s a book all about Charles Monroe Schulz , the brilliant American cartoonist behind the PEANUTS comic strips. There are both child-centric and adult reads here, perfect for OG and new fans to fall in love with the endearing series.
By the way, should any title suit your fancy and you’d like to borrow it to enjoy it at home, simply whip out your NLB Mobile app, tap on the orange “ Scan ” button on the bottom of your screen and scan the QR code that each book is tagged with. That’s it, you’re good to go; once you’re done reading your books, you can return them at any NLB library islandwide .
Snoopy’s Backyard & Lucy’s Booth
Follow a winding road, and you’ll catch the cut-outs of Snoopy, Charlie Brown, Lucy, and Sally Brown posed in an Abbey Road-esque scene as they make their way across a zebra crossing. It’s also where you’ll find Snoopy’s Backyard , a garden-themed zone filled with even more books for young readers to keep themselves entertained.
The set dressing here is immaculate; we’re talking pint-sized, kid-only picnic tables, bush-like shelves stocked with picture books, and even a massive plush of the Snoopy snoozing atop his iconic doghouse. Observant visitors will even spot a Woodstock figure in his nest, perched in the canopy of a book stand.
…
summary: Spend a day reading with the beloved beagle & his pals.

Istana Open House On 1st November 2026
You’ve probably walked past the gates of the Istana countless times while strolling from Orchard Road to Dhoby Ghaut, and wondered what it’s like inside. Well, here’s your chance to stop wondering and actually step in.
The 4th Istana Open House of the year is happening on 1st November 2026 in celebration of Deepavali. There’ll be a full-on programme, complete with an outdoor concert on the Istana grounds, F&B stalls, and activities for all ages.
What is the Istana Open House ?
Image credit: Jason Feuerstein via Google Maps
For those who may not know, the Istana is Singapore’s official presidential residence . While the President doesn’t currently live there , official presidential duties like ceremonies and state visits still happen there. And a fun fact for non-Malay speakers: Istana actually means “palace” in Malay.
The Istana also opens its gates to visitors up to 5 times a year for the Istana Open House, giving visitors rare access to stroll its grounds without needing an invitation. The last time it opened was in July 2026 to celebrate National Day.
What to expect during the Istana Open House
Entering the Istana grounds
Image credit: The Istana
Entry into the Istana grounds starts at 10 am at the Main Gate at Orchard Road. Singaporeans and PRs can enter for free , so head down earlier to chope a spot in the line before the gates open. Last entry is at 6.30pm, so don’t be late!
Standard admission fees apply for other visitors, and are priced as follows:
Category
Standard admission fees
Adults
$20
Children (4-12 years)
$10
Children
Free
These and all other fees will go to the beneficiaries of the President’s Challenge .
When you step onto the grounds, you’ll have to go through security checks ; it is the President’s official office, after all, so expect these checks to add more time to your admission.
To speed through security, be sure not to pack any prohibited items – sharp objects, flammable items, and canned items will all be flagged by the guards. Once you’ve been screened, you’ll be greeted with the large, sprawling garden that is the Istana grounds.
Think of this open house like a stroll in the park – pack light but bring an umbrella and water bottle in case you find yourself far from the tentages or water points in the compound.
However, the Istana Open House will only proceed if the 24-hour Pollutant Standard Index (PSI) is below 200. Do check the Istana website before heading down in case it’s too hazy and the open house is cancelled.
Participate in family-friendly activities
Image credit: President’s Challenge
Head over to the Main Tent and Activity Tent to take part in fun activities like going in bouncy castles, playing card games, and more right within the grounds of the Istana.
If you’re more in tune with your arts side, you can do henna and face painting, make scent pouches, and DIY drip bears to bring home.
The National Library and Archives board will also be bringing MOLLY the mobile library to the Istana as part of ReadSG .
Check out the live performances & narrated Changing of Guards ceremony
Image for illustrative purposes only.
Image credit: @sriwarisan via Instagram
Take a breather from walking, and sit back and enjoy some live performances and an evening concert by students from local schools, such as the official string orchestras from Hwa Chong Institution and Nanyang Girls’ High School, Daydreamer, Heema Izzati, and more.
This edition of the Istana Open House will also have, for the first time, a narrated Changing of Guards ceremony. Visitors will be treated to a performance by the Singapore Armed Forces Ceremonial Band, who will be accompanied by the Silent Precision Drill Squad’s synchronised rifle drills.
These performances and the concert will take place throughout the day, from 11am to 8pm .
Get grub & rehydrate at the food & drink stalls
Image credit: President’s Challenge
If you’re feeling peckish, don’t worry about leaving the Istana grounds. Grab a snack at the food trucks and tents to fill your hungry stomachs, and get your cup of Milo Peng at the Milo Van, available only from 9am-12pm or whilst stocks last. Do note that only cashless payments will be accepted, so you can leave your dollar bills at home.
Collect unique stamps for the Istana Stamp Rally
In collaboration with Singapore Polytechnic, the upcoming Istana Open House will be bringing back the Istana Stamp Rally with new stamps for you to collect. As you and the family explore the Istana compound and participate in the fun activities, you’ll get to collect uniquely designed stamps.
When you’ve completed the stamp book, you can redeem exclusive Istana merch, too!
Tour the Istana Villa
Image credit: Kenny Yao via Google Maps

We’ve got the intel on new bars in Singapore! The bar scene is buzzing with fresh energy, from swanky cocktail bars in Singapore to bold menus that’ll make your taste buds do a happy dance. Some even double as live music bars in Singapore , where you can sip, dine, and groove the night away. We’ve also been busy checking out the new restaurants in Singapore making waves across the city. Ready to drink your way through the crème de la crème with us?
Why trust this guide
When it comes to bars, I’m one of the city’s biggest fans. I’m always on the hunt for the next cool spot that opens up, and I follow it religiously till I can visit for myself to tell you all about it. I’m also very grateful to the bartenders I’ve met along the way who give me the honour of visiting their spaces before they’re open to the public.
Hot new bars in Singapore: November 2026
New bar: Earworm
Photography: Earworm via Instagram
We already know and love Offtrack for its fabulous music choices and even better taste in drinks. So it’s no surprise the group’s second concept is just as musically driven! Aptly named Earworm, this fluid space is a fun mix of bar, restaurant, and live music spot all rolled into one. The music programme champions local artists, and you’ll catch them performing live every Wednesday night. On the weekends, though? You’ll get bass-thumping soundtracks from DJs.
Drinks-wise, the menu is decently extensive with zero-proof picks, beers, wine (red, white, and even orange!), and cocktails. My heart is immediately drawn to the Pimm’s Cup mixed with Another Hendrick’s Gin, and I can never say no to an espresso martini riff, especially if it comes with salted cacao cream like the Caffe Mole!
Must-try drinks: Pimm’s Cup; Caffe Mole; New York Sour; Shakerato
Expect to spend: Cocktails start from $25
Opening hours: Tuesday to Thursday, 6pm to 1am; Friday to Saturday, 6pm to 2am
Address : Earworm , 16 North Canal Road, Singapore 048828
New bar: Sohaus
Photography: Sohaus
From the minds that brought you Nutmeg & Clove, let’s welcome Sohaus, the newest rooftop bar in Singapore . Situated on the roof of the newly opened Moutai House , this new bar in Singapore is a social space made for gathering, unwinding, and soaking in the city vibe. It also boasts one of the most breathtaking views of Singapore’s skyline. According to the team, the bar also gets a fabulous view of the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix ! As if we needed any more incentive to visit this spot.
Naturally, you can expect plenty of Moutai in Sohaus’s cocktails, inspired by cultural moments that have shaped Asia – from what we eat and drink to what we collect, wear, and do. If you’re looking for a seat, you’ll be directed to the alfresco area. But for those who prefer air conditioning, we recommend staying indoors. However, the inside bar area is standing only, and can be a bit of a tight squeeze. We say come in small groups to make the most of the experience.
Must-try drinks: Blind Box Fizz; Coffee Run Martini; Sohaus Highball
Expect to spend: Cocktails start from $28
Opening hours: Tuesday to Saturday, 5pm to 12am
Address : Sohaus , Level 4, Moutai House, 3 Fullerton Road, Singapore 049215
New bar: The Choya Ginza Bar
Photography: The Choya Ginza Bar via Instagram
A century of Choya’s craft and heritage has been distilled into a new establishment: the Choya Ginza Bar. The first-ever bar dedicated to all things Choya, you’ll get to see more than 12 Choya editions and specially curated tasting flights. And this is on top of the Choya serves, classic cocktails, and original concoctions. This is also one of the most affordable cocktail menus I’ve seen in a long time. You won’t find drinks over $22 at this bar, and you can even have a tasting flight of five Choyas for just $20!
Must-try drinks: Anything from the seasonal drinks menu; Choya tasting flights
Expect to spend: Drinks start from $16
Opening hours: Monday to Thursday, 4pm to 11pm; Friday to Saturday, 4pm to 11pm
Address : The Choya Ginza Bar , #02-06, Millenia Walk, 9 Raffles Boulevard, Singapore 039596
Hot new bars in Singapore: October 2026
New bar: Kiap Kiap Chicken Club & Bar
Photography: Sufyan Saad
If you haven’t already caught up with our Kiap Kiap Chicken Club & Bar review , this is your sign to read up, stat. Decked out in red, this new fried chicken spot dishes out nostalgic plates inspired by childhood. Pick between the original or duck fat mala fried chicken to line your stomach. Drinks-wise, we’d recommend the kaya daiquiri ($20) that comes with a little buttermilk waffle garnish. And if you’re going zero-proof, order the virgin smoky yuzu mocktail ($15).
Must-try drinks: Kaya daiquiri; virgin smoky yuzu mocktail
Expect to spend: Drinks start from $20; fried chicken starts from $12
Opening hours: Daily, 5.30pm to 1am (opens till 2am on Fridays & Saturdays)

body:
Zermatt Neo opens OVER restaurant in Tanjong Pagar
Best known for taking on massive amounts of food in one go, competitive eater and content creator Zermatt Neo has started his very first F&B venture: OVER , which just opened along Tras Street .
The new concept brings larger-than-life portions and crazy food challenges, in partnership with The Wolfpack Investment Holdings. They’ve already gotten an overwhelming response for their soft-launch reservations, so we had to visit and see what the commotion is about.
Fans can expect three portion sizes on the menu: Lesser for solo diners, Standard for sharing, and Challenge , featuring the largest servings, typical of Zermatt Neo.
We kick-started our feast with the Rolling Over Wakame in the Lesser portion for $10++ . This featured spring rolls doused in a house-made glaze and topped with wakame salad.
The dish tasted just as interesting as it looked. The spring rolls were crispy and paired well with the briny wakame and subtly sweet glaze, making for a great start to our mukbang-like meal.
Up next we had the Shroyu-Clams! (from $35++) . As a huge lala fan, this starter lived up to all my expectations. Though it came in the smallest size, the clams were anything but. Each one boasted a huge portion of meat, making it worth every penny.
The white clams were simmered and served in a buttery and garlicky shoyu sauce that was finger-licking good. It also came with slices of toasted sourdough to soak up every last drop of the rich sauce.
Moving on to the mains: what really stole the show for us was the Curry Me Over (from $23++) . My colleague and I marvelled at the sheer size of this dish, which Zermatt himself said was originally twice as big.
Atop the bed of rice lies a massive, tender, juicy cut of chicken drowned in nanban sauce that added a pleasant creaminess.
Portions aside, we were impressed with how fragrant the Hainanese-style curry was. Each grain of rice was slathered in the decadent curry zhup, leaving me wanting more after every bite. Despite looking extremely heavy, it was a well-balanced dish that ended up being our favourite of the evening.
On the topic of chicken, we also had the Wing Me Over (from $10++) . Each wing was tender and fried to maximum crunch. While the rub on the skin tasted a tad too salty for me, the teriyaki-like sauce on the side helped cut through the richness.
On top of OVER’s regular menu, the restaurant will also be introducing a rotation of collaborations with various local chefs and businesses. Marking their debut collab with viral local barbecue brand Jett Barbecue, the Over Jett (from $28++) features a burger stacked with Jett BBQ’s signature beef cheeks, crispy onion rings, fried eggs, and a creamy mayo dressing.
Much like how Jett BBQ only makes special appearances now and then, the Over Jett will only be available until 30 November 2026, so grab it while you still can.
Their drinks alone deserve a special shout-out—all of them come in oversized portions. We ordered the Japanese Highball ($13.80++) and Shochu Sour (from $12.80++) , both of which came in extra-tall glasses and were refreshing thirst quenchers.
End your meal on a sweet note with their “secret menu” Mom’s Pie (price TBD) . The pie flavour rotates every month, with this month’s being Apple Pie . The gooey filling within the buttery crust had a woody cinnamon flavour, and the frosting on top was light and airy, marking the perfect end to our meal.
If you’re game, go for the Ultimate Food Challenge (from $239++) , where you take on an entire 8kg platter in one hour. Diners can give it a shot alone or in groups of up to four. Succeed and win a free meal, a spot on the Hall of Fame, a cash prize, as well as bragging rights.
OVER has a bar-like vibe, with high chairs and tables, dim lighting, neon signs, and a curated soundtrack—perfect for a casual night out with pals over some good food and drinks.
The restaurant is located conveniently in the CBD, just a short five-minute walk from Tanjong Pagar MRT Station or Maxwell MRT Station .
In other news, Singapore Coffee Week is back with free entry from 5 to 8 November. If you’re craving a sweet treat in the area, our Messina x Queic feature gives you the latest scoop on their limited-time collab.

Remember the massive waterfront mall we told you about in Penang ? The Waterfront Shoppes is finally opening on 29 Oct 2026 , bringing over 300 retail and dining outlets plus a seafront promenade with views of the Penang Bridge .
Credit – The Light City
Located within The Light City , the sprawling lifestyle destination covers over 1.5 million sq ft across two phases, combining shopping, dining, and entertainment in one coastal precinct. Its waterfront setting also gives shoppers a scenic spot to take a breather between browsing stores and grabbing a bite.
Credit – The Light City
The line-up is set to span everything from familiar local eats and international brands to casual cafes and waterfront dining spots. As more tenants join the mix, there’ll be even more reasons to drop by beyond the usual shopping run, especially if you fancy a meal with a view of the sea.
Credit – Zus, Bakestone, Skechers & XVenture
The confirmed tenant line-up includes Mercato , Parkson , Decathlon , Skechers , Watsons , ZUS Coffee , CU Mart , Loud Speaker , ParaThai , Tai Ho Jiak , Mr. Wu Taiwanese Cuisine , 65c Ondo , Bakestone , and Ningji Lemon Tea . You’ll also find lifestyle and entertainment options such as XVenture , CMC Theatre by Mega Cineplex , and Dreame , alongside fashion, beauty, and tech retailers.
Note that the information provided is accurate at the time of writing and may be subject to change.
Credit – The Light City
The Waterfront Shoppes is part of the wider The Light City integrated development, which will also feature luxury residences, office towers, international hotels , and the upcoming Penang Waterfront Convention Centre (PWCC) . The larger project aims to bring shopping, business, hospitality, and entertainment together in one destination.
The Waterfront Shoppes begins its soft opening on 29 Oct 2026 , so keep it on your radar if you’re planning to visit Penang soon!

summary: The Waterfront Shoppes in Penang opens for a soft launch on 29 October 2026, with over 300 retail and dining outlets across a 1.5 million sq ft lifestyle destination at The Light City. Located near the Penang Bridge and Penang International Airport, it features local eateries, international brands, entertainment options and a seafront promenade, making it a useful stop for shoppers and visitors seeking dining and leisure by the coast.

body:
Diwali eating in Singapore usually means a visit to Little India and a plate of something fried. The Gully Restaurant at Holiday Inn Singapore Little India is taking a different route this year with a mela buffet that puts several festival dishes on one table, plus a four-course set menu running through November.
{‘rendered’: ‘
Gully’s Diwali mela buffet runs for five days from 5 to 9 November. Image: Gully Restaurant & Garden.
\n’}
The mela buffet is S$50++ a person. Dinner runs on 5 and 6 November from 6 to 10pm, and lunch on 7, 8 and 9 November from 12 to 4pm. Those dates sit right around Deepavali itself, which falls on Sunday 8 November, with Monday 9 November a public holiday.
What is on the buffet
The spread is built around the food served at a Diwali mela, the market that springs up before the festival. That means a mix of savoury snacks, curries and sweets rather than a single regional menu, which suits a group where nobody agrees on what Diwali food should be.
{‘rendered’: ‘
The spread at Gully in Holiday Inn Singapore Little India. Image: Gully Restaurant & Garden.
\n’}
{‘rendered’: ‘
The live chaat and pani puri station is part of the mela buffet. Image: Gully Restaurant & Garden.
\n’}
The restaurant seats inside the hotel on Ah Hood Road, a short walk from the Indian Heritage Centre and the Campbell Lane bazaar, so it works as a lunch stop between the lights and the shopping.
The set menu
The A Taste of Diwali set is S$70++ for four courses, or S$60++ for the vegetarian version. It runs from 1 October to 30 November, so it is available now and through the week after the festival.
{‘rendered’: ‘
Gully serves Indian street food as small plates. Image: Gully Restaurant & Garden.
\n’}
Four courses at that price is a reasonable dinner in a hotel restaurant, and the vegetarian option is a proper menu rather than the side dish treatment vegetarian guests usually get at festival promotions.
Booking for the festival week
The buffet dates are the ones to plan around. Deepavali weekend is the busiest in Little India, when the roads around Serangoon Road close for the bazaar and traffic crawls. Book ahead for 5 and 6 November dinner, and expect lunch on 8 and 9 November to be the busiest sittings because both days are holidays.
Ask for a table away from the door if you are bringing children, because the hotel lobby gets busy with festival visitors.
{‘rendered’: ‘
The garden seats beside the pool. Image: Holiday Inn Singapore Little India.
\n’}
The Deepavali light-up runs until 8 November, and the Campbell Lane bazaar is at its best after dark, so an early dinner leaves time for both.
summary: A S$50++ mela buffet runs over Deepavali week, with dinner on 5 and 6 November and lunch from 7 to 9 November, alongside a four-course set menu until 30 November.
title: Gully at Holiday Inn Little India puts a Diwali mela on the buffet

body:
Golden Peony at Conrad Singapore Marina Bay hands its kitchen to Chef Andy Fung for two weeks from 2 November, and the menu he brings reads Cantonese with a Thai accent. Chef Fung runs Liu at Conrad Bangkok, and the residency puts his cooking beside the Cantonese kitchen of executive Chinese chef Ku Keung for 14 days of lunch and dinner. The run is titled Cantonese Craft, with a Thai Accent , and it draws on nearly four decades of Chef Fung’s work in Chinese kitchens in Hong Kong, China, the Philippines and Thailand.
Image: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay
What the guest kitchen cooks
Two dishes anchor the menu. A sea cucumber spring roll arrives with a Thai tom yum sauce, and Boston lobster is served three ways. Both sit in the a la carte list at lunch and dinner, and the kitchen builds four, five and six course menus around them for anyone who wants the full run of the guest chef’s cooking.
The rest of the list leans on the same idea, taking Cantonese technique and moving the seasoning east. The cooking stays in the light, sauced style Golden Peony already works in, and the Thai side shows up in the sauces and the aromatics rather than in a separate Thai section of the menu.
Image: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay
A single four-hands dinner
The two chefs cook together once, on Saturday 14 November at 6.30pm, for a six-course dinner with sake called A Meeting of Masters. It costs S$128++ a person, and S$178++ with the sake pairing. The rest of the fortnight runs as separate services, with Chef Fung’s dishes alongside Golden Peony’s own menu at both lunch and dinner.
Image: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay
Where to find it
Golden Peony is on Level 3 of Conrad Singapore Marina Bay at 2 Temasek Boulevard. The residency runs from 2 to 15 November, and the four-hands dinner is a single sitting on the Saturday in the middle of it. Tables for the fortnight and for the 14 November dinner are booked with the hotel.
The room runs a long menu outside the residency too, so a table booked in the first half of November can sit either with Chef Fung’s dishes or with the restaurant’s own Cantonese cooking, or mix the two across courses. Six courses at the four-hands dinner is the one sitting where both kitchens plate the same meal.
Image: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay
Both chefs keep their own kitchens running through the fortnight, Chef Fung at Liu in Bangkok and Chef Ku Keung at Golden Peony, so the guest dishes appear at the Marina Bay restaurant for 14 days and then leave with him. The run closes on Sunday 15 November.
summary: Chef Andy Fung of Liu at Conrad Bangkok cooks at Golden Peony from 2 to 15 November, with a S$128++ four-hands dinner on 14 November.
title: Golden Peony brings a Bangkok chef and a Thai accent to Cantonese cooking

body:
Unfortunate news for the residents and regular patrons of Telok Blangah Rise Market & Food Centre — it will close for a 2-month Repair and Renovation (R&R) from 1 Nov to 31 Dec 2026 . R&R is periodic maintenance work that is usually carried out every 5 to 7 years, depending on the condition of the hawker centre. It can consist of repainting and redecoration, as well as replacement of plumbing, electrical and sanitary systems. Gas pipes, floor and wall tiles, and roofing may also be replaced.
Credit – Philip Lim via Facebook
Established in 1975, Telok Blangah Rise Market & Food Centre sits slightly below road level, surrounded by lush greenery. It is located near the Southern Ridges and Mount Faber, making it a hotspot for hikers. The hawker centre is smaller and more laid-back than others. This offers a peaceful, serene atmosphere for those who prefer to enjoy their meals away from the crowds.
Some notable stalls include Hai Yan Fried Kway Teow and Vegetarian Delight . The former serves kway teow with excellent wokhei along with a unique addition —- a runny egg. Additionally, their kway teow does not come with cockles. This could be a plus or a minus depending on who you’re asking (a plus for me).
Credit – Philip Lim via Facebook
R&R works keep our hawker centres in good physical condition and ensure a pleasant dining experience for all patrons. They also help to improve business and footfall. The R&R works are all in the public’s interest to protect our health and safety so let’s wait patiently for Telok Blangah Rise Market & Food Centre to reopen! In the meantime, you can visit other hawker centres nearby such as Telok Blangah Crescent Market & Food Centre.
Hai Yan Fried Kway Teow Mee: Telok Blangah hawker sells runny eggs on top of wok hei char kway teow
summary: Telok Blangah Rise Market & Food Centre will close from 1 Nov to 31 Dec 2026 for two months of repair and renovation (R&R) works, which involve cyclical maintenance to keep hawker centres in good condition. Established in 1975, the smaller, quieter hawker centre near the Southern Ridges and Mount Faber is popular with hikers and regular patrons, with stalls such as Hai Yan Fried Kway Teow and Vegetarian Delight. Nearby diners can visit Telok Blangah Crescent Market & Food Centre during the closure.
title: Telok Blangah Rise Market & Food Centre closed from 1 Nov to 31 Dec 2026

body:
Free indoor play area at the Singapore Flyer
With the haze still lingering in Singapore, outdoor playgrounds might not be a parent’s first choice for a day out with the kids. But keeping the kids entertained indoors doesn’t necessarily mean forking out money for pricey indoor playgrounds .
Tucked away at the Singapore Flyer is a lesser-known free indoor padded play area where kiddos can have some fun while parents take a breather. Here’s what to know before bringing your kids down.
What can I expect at this mini indoor play area?
Padded environment & small play equipment
Though small and simple at a glance, the play area features padded walls and flooring , along with mini slides and simple climbing elements for little ones to explore. With soft surfaces placed throughout the space, parents can have some peace of mind as their kiddos crawl, climb, and play.
While the play space is officially designed for children aged 2 to 8 years old , we noticed that the play structures and wall padding are relatively low to the ground, making them better suited for younger tots who are still finding their feet.
Older kids within the recommended age range are welcome too, though they might find the equipment a little too simple for their liking. If you’ve got older kids in tow, we suggest packing a few of their favourite toys to keep them entertained in case they get bored of the simple play equipment.
Bright & clean environment
The playroom itself is bright , clean , and well-maintained , making it an inviting space for little ones to have fun. During our visit, we even spotted a cleaner wrapping up a routine cleaning session, so parents can be assured that the space is regularly maintained.
Rest areas for parents to kill time
There’s also a designated waiting area with a couch for parents to sit back while keeping an eye on their kids, along with shoe racks to keep footwear neatly organised before entering the play area.
Nursing room & changing station
Behind a partition in the playroom, you’ll also find a simple nursing room that doubles as a changing room for parents with babies. While small and basic, it’s equipped with a couch and changing station, enough for those whose babies need a quick fix.
Let your kiddos play for free for 30 minutes
To ensure that the playroom doesn’t get too crowded, only 10 people are allowed inside at any one time, including parents and guardians. Each play session is also limited to 30 minutes , so while your kids might not be able to spend an entire afternoon here, it’s still a convenient spot for a quick play session to help them burn off energy without spending a cent.
Plus, if you are already exploring the Marina Bay area, this is a good pit stop for both parents and kids.
How to get to the free indoor play area at Singapore Flyer
Hop on the train via the Circle Line or Downtown Line to Promenade MRT Station and leave via Exit A . From there, it’s approximately an 8-minute walk to Singapore Flyer.
If you’re driving, there’s also a multi-storey car park on-site, with parking charged at $2.50/hour or part thereof during the day.
Once you’re at the main entrance or drop-off point of the Singapore Flyer, simply walk straight past the open-air cafe and turn left to find the play area, located at #01-05.
Check out this lesser-known indoor play area this weekend
It’s open daily from 10am to 10pm , so besides giving the kids a chance to expend their energy reserves, it’ll also give you some time to relax and beat the heat in an air-conditioned room.
And sure, it might not have the ball pits and obstacle courses of bigger playgrounds, but for young kids that can be entertained by simple mini slides and a short balance beam, it’s a wallet-friendly option that gets the job done.
Admission: Free
Opening hours: 10am-10pm, Daily
Address: #01-05, 30 Raffles Avenue, Singapore 039803

• Baby Shark indoor playground
Photography by Chin Lee Ren.
summary: This lesser-known indoor play area even has a nursing room.

Quby’s Science Explorer Buddies & QUBY WORLD at Science Centre Singapore
There’s a good chance you’ve come across Quby, the adorable white cartoon character that’s been popping up everywhere, from WhatsApp stickers to plushies. Well, the little fella is turning 10 this year, and Science Centre Singapore is joining in on the celebrations.
To celebrate the adorable character’s 10th anniversary , Science Centre Singapore is launching Quby’s Science Explorer Buddies , as well as QUBY WORLD , where you can snap cute photos with Quby-themed installations and explore interactive science exhibits.
Shop 5 new Quby plush keychains inspired by marine life & local treats
Whether you’re a long-time Quby collector or simply someone who can’t resist an adorable plushie, the latest Quby Science Explorer Buddies collection might just have you reaching for your wallet. The collection features 5 special-edition plush keychains , each with a unique design and a connection to science.
Ocean lovers can look forward to Whale Quby , Scallop Quby , and Manta Ray Quby , which take inspiration from their respective marine creatures. It’s a cute way to bring a little bit of the underwater world into your plushie collection.
There’s also Baby Quby , a miniature-inspired take on the beloved character that’s bound to win over anyone with a soft spot for tiny things.
And for a touch of local flavour, there’s Kueh Tutu Quby , inspired by the traditional Singaporean snack. Who knew one of our favourite childhood treats could make such an adorable plushie?
The plush keychains will be available for $29 each at the Curiosity Shop in Science Centre Singapore from 28th October 2026 .
What can I expect at QUBY WORLD?
The Quby celebrations extend beyond the merchandise shelves. Head over to the Everyday Science gallery at Hall D from 28th October 2026 onwards, where QUBY WORLD brings the adorable character into a series of science-themed displays.
Snap photos with Quby-themed installations
Get your cameras ready, because QUBY WORLD has plenty of adorable photo spots to give your camera roll a Quby-themed makeover.
For starters, there’s a giant periodic table that gives the familiar chemistry chart a larger-than-life makeover. It’s a fun photo spot for anyone who wants to channel their inner scientist.
Next, head over to the Quby-themed photobooth to snap some adorable pictures. For just $10 , you’ll get 2 photostrips per session featuring the adorable Quby against a space-themed backdrop, making for a cute little keepsake to remember your visit.
Don’t miss the dome-themed Quby installation either, where you can pose for even more photos with the beloved character.
With all these adorable Quby-themed photo spots, you might want to clear some space in your camera roll before heading down, because 1 picture definitely won’t be enough.
Explore the gallery’s scientific displays for fun learning
While you’re there, don’t forget to explore the gallery’s interactive exhibits, which reveal the surprising science behind things we encounter in our daily lives.
For instance, there’s an exhibit demonstrating the Coanda Effect , where visitors can observe how a stream of water behaves near a solid surface. You’ll get to experiment with a ping pong ball attached to a string, moving it towards a thin stream of water to see the phenomenon in action.
Another exhibit, Bending Water , lets you discover how static electricity can influence the movement of water. Simply rub a rod against a piece of cloth to charge it, then bring it close to a flowing stream of water and watch what happens.
The science behind it? Although water has no overall electrical charge, its molecules have positively and negatively charged sides. When a charged object comes close, the water molecules respond, causing the stream to bend towards it.
These hands-on exhibits let little scientists unleash their curiosity and pick up a thing or two while having a blast.
How much does a ticket to QUBY WORLD cost?
Best of all, access to QUBY WORLD is included with your regular Science Centre Singapore admission ticket , so there’s no separate ticket needed to explore the displays.
Here’s a breakdown of Science Centre Singapore’s ticket prices:

Celebrate Quby’s 10th anniversary at Science Centre Singapore
The Quby x Science Centre Singapore collaboration offers a mix of cute collectibles, photo spots, and hands-on science activities. And if you can’t get enough of Quby, you can also register to vote for your favourite Quby plush keychain and gain access to a Quby sticker pack.
So, round up your fellow Quby enthusiasts and make a trip down to Science Centre Singapore. Just be warned: you might end up leaving with more plushies than you originally planned.

body:
ST Rosyam Mart – 24-hour Supermarket in JB
Singaporeans have been going to JB for their petrol and grocery runs since, well, forever. But because of the Causeway traffic, sometimes it’s hard to justify spending half your precious weekend stuck in a jam to do something you can do in Singapore.
ST Rosyam Mart could fix that. The new halal supermarket at Paragon Market Place just opened on 12th September 2026. And it never closes. So you can cross when the checkpoint is empty, do your whole haul at 2am, and be back in bed before the weekend crowd has started queueing. More reasons to add it to your list of supermarkets in JB to check out.
The current exchange rate is S$1=MYR3.18 as of 28th October 2026.
What’s ST Rosyam Mart?
ST Rosyam Mart is a Malaysian chain that Sri Ternak Group set up in 2018 with local actor Datuk Rosyam Nor. The Tampoi branch is the brand’s 10th outlet and its first in Johor, and also its biggest yet at approximately 70,000sqft.
Where is ST Rosyam Mart located?
Just 20 minutes from the SG-JB Causeway, in Tampoi
Image credit: ST Rosyam Mart Tampoi (Paragon Market Place) via Google Maps
ST Rosyam Mart is at Paragon Market Place along Jalan Tampoi, about a 20-minute drive from the JB Checkpoint . That’s far enough from town to skip the usual tourist-mall crowds, but close enough that you’re not spending your whole night driving.
Image credit: ST Rosyam Mart Tampoi (Paragon Market Place) via Google Maps
The mall is easy to spot: its facade is modelled on a railway station, a nod to the KTM trains that run past it. There are 700 free parking bays, which makes it super convenient to find parking without having to drive in circles.
And if you’re not driving, the Causeway Link runs a direct bus from JB Sentral to the Opp Paragon Market Place stop . The ride takes about 24 minutes and costs RM1-RM3 (~S$0.31–S$0.94), but buses only come once an hour. A Grab is the less stressful option, especially if you’re lugging a week’s worth of groceries home.
Over 40,000 products, including seafood at wholesale prices
Image credit: ST Rosyam Mart Tampoi (Paragon Market Place) via Google Maps
With over 40,000 products on the shelves, this place covers your whole grocery list. But the best part is that you can find fresh produce, daily essentials, household products, celebrity-branded items, and bulk groceries all sold at wholesale prices.
Image credit: ST Rosyam Mart Tampoi (Paragon Market Place) via Google Maps
It’s worth saving your weekly or bi-weekly grocery shopping until you can come here because it’s really worth it. Plus, if you do bulk shopping for non-perishables like soy sauce and canned food, your groceries will last a pretty long time.
Image credit: ST Rosyam Mart Tampoi (Paragon Market Place) via Google Maps
The real draw is the fresh meat and seafood section, where prices are low enough to make you question what you’ve been paying back home. Think ikan bulus , also known as silver whiting , for RM30.90/kg (~S$9.72/kg) and ikan pelaling for RM16.90/kg (~S$5.31/kg) .
Image credit: Prudence Loh via Google Maps
The entire supermarket is halal, which means there’s no pork or lard sold here. Plus, butchers are there to help you even if you go in the wee hours of the morning.
Image credit: Ivan Tan via Google Maps
The store also gives out free ice packs, a small thing that matters a lot here. Your seafood has to survive the drive back and a possible jam at the checkpoint, so you won’t need to bring a cooler bag or rush home with a fish slowly warming in the boot.
Image credit: Prudence Loh via Google Maps
But before you go wild at the meat counter, note that SFA doesn’t allow travellers to bring meat back from Malaysia, while seafood is capped at 5kg per person. So the free ice packs are strictly for your prawns, not your chicken wings. If you are organising a BBQ in JB, though, this is a good place to do your meat shopping.
Also read: Shopping In JB: 10 Things You Cannot Bring Back To SG From Across The Causeway
Shopping In JB: 10 Things You Cannot Bring Back To SG From Across The Causeway
Open 24/7, with more than 20 free services
Image credit: Jimmy via Google Maps
The store also offers more than 20 free customer services on top of the groceries. Besides the ice packs, there’s a free drinks service where you can grab some water, which is handy when you’ve been pushing a fully loaded trolley.
The full list of services for the JB outlet hasn’t been confirmed yet, but ST Rosyam Mart’s other branches offer free trolley use, butcher services and powerbank loans, plus tyre inflators and car jumpers.
Head to ST Rosyam Mart on your next JB trip
For Singaporeans who’ve made the JB run a regular thing, ST Rosyam Mart removes the most annoying part of it: having to go when everyone else does.
If you want to explore more while you’re there, turn the trip into a proper night out with these late-night things to do in JB . And for those staying for the entire weekend, here’s our list of 100 things to do in JB .
…
summary: There are also 700 free parking lots!

Chucky Cat Cafe is a cat cafe at Komtar JBCC
In case you didn’t know, The Smart Local ’s and Eatbook ’s office has two ragdoll cats named Jaymee and Pika, and I personally crowned myself as the former’s favourite. To see if my feline allure extends to other furballs, I headed down to Chucky Cat Cafe in JB.
The cat cafe brand has three outlets spread across JB: Komtar JBCC , Paradigm Mall JB , and Toppen Shopping Centre , with the latter located in Mount Austin . We decided to visit the Komtar JBCC outlet in JB Sentral, a five-minute walk from JB CIQ.
The current exchange rate is RM1 = ~S$0.32 as of 28 October 2026.
25 JB Mount Austin Food Places For $0.60 Mini Bowls, DIY Croffles And More
For just RM24.90 per person , you’ll get an hour’s worth of playtime. Alternatively, if you’re staying for a long time, you can get the Day Pass at RM69 for the whole day, with a complimentary drink thrown in.
The space as a whole was very clean, and there was surprisingly a lack of hairballs despite housing over 15 cats. Before entering, you’ll need to store your bags in a locker and wear shoe covers. The floor is quite slippery though, so do watch your step.
Be warned: you’ll definitely fall in love with these cats. You’ll find them lounging around, either cooped up in their sleeping pods or lazing on the sofas. The cafe did warn us that the cats decked out in gold chains are less friendly than others. However, all of them were equally affectionate when we visited.
The cats’ kryptonite was food, which felt like a very relatable trait. Get their Cat Stick (RM5) to hand-feed them a stick’s worth of cat food, though be prepared to get swarmed. One of the cats even tried wrestling the stick from me, but it gave me the perfect opportunity to sneak in a few pats.
After seeing the cats feast on food, we too felt the need to order some drinks to quench our thirst. We ordered their Rose Latte (RM11.60) , featuring a blend of sweet rose syrup and aromatic coffee. It tasted like a zhnged-up version of bandung, with the floral rose fragrance complementing the earthy coffee notes, though I wished the coffee flavour was slightly stronger. Those who aren’t big on coffee can get the Iced Matcha Latte (RM11.90) or Iced Hazelnut Milk (RM10.90) instead.
To immortalise your memory of the cafe, you can visit the photobooth, which offers a myriad of photo frames, some of which even feature their beloved cats.
If you get bored, you can even play console games on their Nintendo Switch, such as Mario Kart 8 Deluxe and Nintendo Switch Sports, though you might get some curious looks from the cats.
Animal lovers itching for more time with furry friends should check out our guide to the best pet cafes in JB for more places to add to your itinerary. Alternatively, if you’re feeling peckish after an intense cat-petting sesh, our guide to the best cafes near JB customs has you covered.

Chucky Cat Cafe is not halal-certified.

This was an independent visit by Eatbook.sg.

Cheap food places in Orchard for $10 and less
Orchard may be dubbed as the area for the affluent, a place you should avoid at all costs if you are looking to dine on a budget. But we are here to prove you wrong—here is our list of the 15 cheap Orchard food places that will only cost you $10 or less! Whether you’re craving a piping hot bowl of Yong Tau Foo or the comfort of a home-cooked Korean meal, we’ve got you covered.
1. Korat Thai Cafe
The key to finding Orchard Road’s cheap fixes lies in the less fancy, less decorated places. One such spot is Korat Thai Cafe, a nondescript spot serving up affordable Thai cuisine. Plus, their menu is super extensive, with over 50 dishes to choose from!
Options here include Tom Yum Fried Rice ($8.50), Garlic Pepper ($7.50), Sweet and Sour ($7.50), Basil Leaf Pork ($7.50) . Otherwise, dig into a comforting bowl of Tom Yum Noodle Soup ($8.50 ) , which boasts spicy and sour flavours, or a bowl of flavourful Phad Thai ($8.50).
Check out our Korat Thai Cafe review.
Address: 400 Orchard Road, #03-28, Orchard Tower, Singapore 238875
Opening hours: Daily 12pm to 10pm
Website
Korat Thai Cafe is not halal-certified.
Korat Thai Cafe Review: XXL Thai Pork Backbone, Tom Yum Mama And More At Orchard Towers
2. New Station Snack Bar
New Station Snack Bar is located in Far East Plaza. If you’re familiar with their sister joint, New Station Rice Bar in Bugis, you would know just how popular the OG joint is. They sell a range of zi char-style dishes, but the one that put them on the map is their salted egg rice.
This salted egg rice, which is a non-negotiable dish to order when you’re here, is easily one of the best around. We visited their sister outlet not too long ago, so we can attest to this claim. Their delicious Salted Egg Pork Rice ($8) features crispy, deep-fried pieces of pork drenched in a thick, savoury salted egg sauce. But if that doesn’t strike your fancy, go for dishes such as the Marmite Chicken Rice ($9), Sweet and Sour Fish Rice ($8), or Black Pepper Beef Rice ($8) , which are equally as popular!
Check out our New Station Rice Bar review.

Image credit: Ming Rong via Google Maps
Riverside Indonesian BBQ is known for its panggang AKA grilled meats. They have numerous outlets dotted across various Kopitiams on the island, including one in Plaza Singapura and 313 Somerset! Options here include the Ayam Panggang Set ($7.80), Sotong Panggang Set ($8.50), and Ikan Panggang Set ($7.80), among others.
Image credit: Jasmine Adams via Google Maps
Other than meat, each plate comes with rice doused in lemak curry, cabbage, a sunny-side-up, clear soup, and sambal. The grilled chicken is super raved about, known for not only being tender and juicy, but also well-marinated. Each piece is grilled to perfection over charcoal, so you know you’re getting that ultra-smoky flavour!

4. Song Fa Bak Kut Teh
Song Fa Bak Kut Teh needs little to no introduction, with it being arguably Singapore’s most established BKT chain. Not to mention, the stall has also had a consistent spot on the Michelin Bib Gourmand for over seven years!
Though the prices of the BKT here are a leg-up compared to what you would find at more humble hawker stalls, most dishes on the menu here will still set you back less than $10. Must-order items here are the Pork Ribs Soup ($8.80++ ) and the Premium Loin Rib Soup ($9.80++).
The broth boasts a rich, distinctive flavour of pork bones, thanks to the long hours of simmering. It also isn’t overly peppery, which is great as it wouldn’t induce a coughing fit upon first sip. To better soak up more of that fragrant broth, order some Dough Fritters ($2.30++) AKA you tiao to dip on the side.
Check out our Song Fa Bak Kut Teh review .

Song Fa Bak Kut Teh Review: Singapore’s Famous Michelin-Approved Bak Kut Teh, Open Since 1969
5. Fiie’s Cafe
Image credit: Kai via Google Maps
Arguably one of the most well-known food joints in Lucky Plaza is Fiie’s Cafe , or you might better know the stall as the famous Mister Grumpy’s fried chicken. body:
Best omakase restaurants in Singapore
Omakase, synonymous with fancy Japanese fare, actually means: I leave it up to you. The “you” here refers to the chef, who would present a series of dishes centred around the season’s best produce. Fancy it may be, it doesn’t always mean that you have to spend a bomb and then some—with that, here’s a list of the best omakase restaurants in Singapore for all budgets, with prices from less than $40++ a person.
1. Tentsuru
Image credit: @tentsurusg
At most omakase experiences, tempura might be but one of many courses. At Tentsuru , however, tempura takes centre stage on their chef’s choice menus—a decision founded on Master Chef Daiki Kawaguchi ’s love for the deep-fried Japanese dish.
There are four omakase menus at Tentsuru, each with progressively more courses. These are Tsuzumi ($188++), Uguisu ($280++) , and Tsuru ($380++) . Whatever your choice, be certain that a fine-dining tempura and omakase experience awaits, built upon fresh ingredients air-flown from the Toyosu Fish Market and various parts of Japan. Typically, the experience involves an appetiser, a seafood and vegetable tempura medley, a tendon or a tencha, and a dessert. All courses are enjoyed on a Japanese bar counter, with front-row seats to Chef Kawaguchi in action.
Image credit: @tentsurusg
If you’re in the mood for a splurge, order the Tsuru. The meal starts with a seasonal appetiser and dish of the day, before segueing into eight different tempura offerings. Of the lot are two Tentsuru signatures: the Sea Urchin Tempura , where uni roe is served raw on a deep-fried shiso leaf, with a dollop of caviar. Also of note is the Miyazaki A5 Wagyu Beef tempura, topped with earthy black truffle shavings and a house-made komi sauce. During the winter season, diners can also expect Hokkaido wild king crab to make an appearance on their plates.
A selection of premium sake—including an exclusive Tentsuru Kura No Hana Junmai Daiginjo (from $55++) —along with a curated range of fine wines, is also available for pairing.
Address: 29 Tanglin Road, Level 2, The St. Regis Singapore, Singapore 247911
Opening hours: Tue-Sun 12pm to 2:30pm, 6pm to 10:30pm
Tel: 8113 3612
Website
Tentsuru is not halal-certified.
2. Sushi Masa by Ki-setsu
Image credit: Sushi Masa by Ki-setsu
Cuppage Plaza is known for being a haven for authentic Japanese restaurants. Among them is Sushi Masa by Ki-setsu , often regarded as one of the best omakase spots in the area . Tucked away on the plaza’s sixth floor, it is an intimate reservations-only eight-seater omakase restaurant run by Chef Masa. Diners get a front-row seat as the chef prepares his dishes of the day, spanning appetisers to sushi and sashimi, as well as cooked dishes.
The pace of the meal is leisurely, thanks to the fact that Sushi Masa has only one seating each night. Expect to spend two to three hours feasting on Chef Masa’s creations, all made with seasonal ingredients air-flown daily from Tokyo’s Toyosu Market.
Image credit: Sushi Masa by Ki-setsu
Currently on the menu are highlights like the Grilled Ankimo with Deep-Fried Sweet Onion , where monkfish liver is grilled in a manner similar to foie gras, and topped with a sweet onion garnish for added texture. There’s the Monaka , Sushi Masa’s spin on the negitoro sushi, comprising chopped fatty tuna and uni served on a crisp Japanese wafer, with a zingy housemade shiso pesto and sansho pepper sauce.
For sushi, the Flame-Grilled Otoro Nigiri with Leek is a memorable reinterpretation of an aburi course. Fatty tuna grilled directly over an open flame to develop a lightly charred crust that enhances the fish’s butteriness, finished with leek for freshness.
Prices start at $230+ for their 16-course Syuugetsu Dinner menu—a more reasonable price than omakase experiences of a similar calibre, thanks to the fact that Sushi Masa isn’t housed in a hotel or an expensive shophouse.
Reservations open 60 days in advance, and can be made via their website .
Address: 5 Koek Road, #06-03, Singapore 228796
Opening hours: Tue-Sat 7:15pm to 10pm, Sun for private bookings only
Tel: 9752 5851
Website
Sushi Masa by Ki-setsu is not halal-certified.
3. AN Omakase
Image credit: @anomakase.sg
Located near Maxwell MRT Station is AN Omakase , a casual Japanese dining restaurant serving up both lunch and dinner omakase.
Image credit: @anomakase.sg
Prices start at $13 8++ for the Himitsu menu, which comes with five courses—an appetiser, a steamed dish , nigiri sushi , soup , and dessert . Vegan-friendly options are available too.
summary: Check out this list of best omakase restaurants in Singapore for all budgets: from under $40++ to splurge-worthy, Michelin-starred spots!
title: 25 Omakase Restaurants In Singapore For Special Occasions, Including Those By Michelin-Starred Chefs

body:
Best traditional desserts in Singapore
The craziest reinvented traditional dessert I’ve had is probably the Mr Bean cocktail from local bar Jekyll & Hyde. While I was impressed by how the cocktail, made with Lao Ban beancurd, vodka, kaya, and Frangelico, tasted, it’s not something I’d crave all the time, unlike a good old bowl of red bean soup or cheng tng. For these old-school treats, here are the stalls where you can get the best traditional desserts in Singapore .
1. Siyuan Desserts
Tucked inside a cheongsam shop in Lavender, Siyuan Desserts is a hidden gem serving traditional Chinese desserts. Expect old-school favourites such as freshly made sesame paste, yam paste and more.
If you’re not sure what to get, try the 3 Mini Bowls ($6.50) to sample the cafe’s specialties: almond, sesame, and walnut paste. Other recommendations include the classic Orh Nee ($5.80) and Cheng Teng with Peach Gum ($5.50).
Read our Siyuan Desserts review .
Address: 111D King George’s Avenue, Singapore 208559
Opening hours: Tue-Wed, Sat-Sun 1pm to 9:30pm, Fri 1pm to 10pm
Tel: 8922 9094
Website
Siyuan Desserts is not halal-certified.
Siyuan Desserts: Fresh Sesame Paste, Old-School Orh Nee And More In Lavender
2. Yuen Yeung
TikTok-viral Yuen Yeung formed snaking queues in the first few months of their opening, mainly because of their modern interpretations of traditional desserts. Take the Pistachio Paste ($8.60+) for example; this was a hot pick among diners as it’s a three-in-one of nutty, creamy, and sweet, made even better thanks to the salted pistachio bits. Another dessert in a similar shade of green—but one that tastes very different—is the Matcha Mochi Peaks ($6.40+) , starring a creamy white paste topped with matcha ice cream and lots of chewy brown sugar pearls.
Read our Yuen Yeung review .
Maxwell outlet

Opening hours: Tue-Sun 11:30am to 10:30pm
Buona Vista outlet
Address: 1 Vista Exchange Grn, #01-47A/48 The Star Vista, Singapore 138617

Website
Yuen Yeung is not halal-certified.
Yuen Yeung: This TikTok-Viral Chinese Dessert Cafe Has 1H Queues—Is It Worth The Wait?
3. 75 Ah Balling Peanut Soup
For old-school handmade tang yuan packed to the brim, check out 75 Ah Balling Peanut Soup at Golden Mile Food Centre . Since they started their business in 1947, they have been famous for their glutinous rice balls in Peanut Soup ($2) . While peanut soup is their signature, other soup options include Longan Red Date , Ginger , and Almond Milk , all priced at $2.10 .
Each bowl typically comes with four pieces of glutinous rice balls for $2.80 . It’s priced at $3.20 for five Ah Balling and $3.50 for six Ah Balling. They’re filled with peanut, sesame, and red bean. The more adventurous folks can try their yam and matcha ones!
Read our 75 Ah Balling review.

4. 115 Tang Shui
The next time you’re in Chinatown, pop your head into 115 Tang Shui ’s stall and you will see a big stone grinder sitting at the side. In an effort to keep all preparation methods traditional, the stall uses this 42-year-old machine to make their desserts. Serving mainly Cantonese desserts, you can find traditional bowls such as Sesame Paste ($2.30) , Almond Paste ($2.30) , and Pumpkin Corn ($2.30) here. One of their best-selling items, Bobo Chacha ($2.30) , follows a traditional recipe passed down in the family.
Read our 115 Tang Shui review .

Website
115 Tang Shui is not halal-certified.
5. Jin Yu Man Tang Dessert Shop
Jin Yu Man Tang Dessert Shop allows you to have traditional Chinese desserts in a comfortable, modern setting. If you’ve missed Hong Kong’s famous milk puddings, get them here. Their Signature Ginger Milk Pudding ($5.30+) is a silky, creamy concoction, while the Shun De Double Layer Milk Pudding ($4.40+) will whisk you right back to Australia Dairy Company. You can also get peach gum desserts, Sago with Mango ($5.20+) , and savoury bites here too.

Thong Sum Hot & Cold Desserts is a stall started by a young hawkerpreneur, serving traditional Chinese desserts.
