body:
Mendung Kafe in Bandar Bukit Mahkota came onto my radar thanks to a dear friend who was deep in a serious nasi lemak craving spiral and determined to find a new spot worth obsessing over.
One quick look at its social presence and I was already intrigued. The branding was clean, neat, and thoughtfully put together, which admittedly matters more than ever in an age where first impressions are made by a scroll and a double tap.
Stepping into Mendung Kafe sealed the deal. The space was unexpectedly cosy, filled with natural light streaming through wide glass windows without feeling glaring or overwhelming.
The service was warm, the decor leaned into a tasteful blend of traditional touches and modern sensibilities, and there was an easy breeziness to the whole place that made you want to linger a little longer (while fighting the drowsiness taking over after a full meal).
What to order at Mendung Kafe
Since Mendung Kafe operates only until 12pm , it naturally leans into breakfast fare . That said, the menu is far from limited. You’ll find familiar Malay breakfast staples alongside a small Western selection , so there’s room to play it safe or switch things up. If you’re visiting on a weekday, their pasta options are also worth a look, though mornings here clearly belong to comfort food.
What genuinely surprised me, however, was the drink menu. It’s impressively varied, covering everything from coffee to non-coffee options like teas and mocktails. To kick off the morning, I went with their Latte (RM11.90) , served hot.
From the first sip, it was clear this was a well-executed cup. The foam was smooth and creamy, holding up beautifully all the way to the end. The coffee itself was bold and robust, with flavour notes that leaned more towards fruity than nutty. If that’s your thing, this will hit the spot. Personally, I lean towards nuttier profiles, but there’s no denying the quality here.
I didn’t wait long before moving on to the main event: the Nasi Lemak Ayam Makdee (RM11.90) . While the menu doesn’t label it as a McDonald’s-inspired version, the resemblance is there. For the price, the portion was generous without feeling excessive.
The rice stood out immediately. Fluffy and fragrant, it carried strong santan notes and, most importantly, was properly seasoned. While some places shy away from adding salt to their coconut rice entirely, this one didn’t hold back, making every bite far more layered.
The sambal was a knockout. Spicy, with a subtle sour edge and just a hint of sweetness, it struck a well-balanced profile that kept me going back for more. Easily one of the better sambals I’ve had, though I wouldn’t complain if it leaned even more towards sour. The ikan bilis and roasted peanuts were crispy and well-prepared, adding texture without stealing the spotlight.
Five Sisters Nasi Lemak: Taking on Forbes’ World’s Spiciest Nasi Lemak — Carolina Reaper & Ghost Pepper sambal so hot you’ll need to sign a form
Visually, the fried chicken could pass for something you’d expect from a fast-food favourite . That deep red colour and crispy skin were instantly inviting. Flavour-wise, it leaned closer to Texas Chicken than McDonald’s, with a smoky-forward profile and straightforward seasoning. The chicken was cooked just right, juicy on the inside with a satisfying crunch on the outside.
Another standout was the Nasi Lemak Ayam Salted Egg (RM16.90) . The battered fried chicken was generously coated in sauce, making every bite indulgent.
While the sauce leaned more curry-forward than distinctly salted egg, it was undeniably delicious. Savoury, aromatic, and packed with spice — it was dangerously addictive.
To round things off, we ordered the Lontong Kuah (RM9.90) for a bit of variety. Once again, the portion size exceeded expectations.
The plate was brimming with tempeh , tofu , green beans, nasi impit , and more. Halfway through and we were already comfortably full. The broth was flavourful yet light, and rich without being overwhelming.
Who Mendung Kafe is best for?
Mendung Kafe isn’t restrictive in any way. You can come alone, with friends, or with whoever you feel like bringing along. That said, it really shines as a spot for a slow, relaxed breakfast, especially with family .
It’s a place that suits an unhurried morning. Wake up early, take your time getting ready, throw on something comfortable, and arrive with empty stomachs and no rush to leave. The calm atmosphere, generous portions, and familiar flavours make it ideal for lingering conversations over breakfast, where the goal isn’t to eat quickly, but to enjoy the start of the day together.
How to get there?
Mendung Kafe isn’t directly accessible by public transportation , so driving is your best bet. Coming from Cheras, the journey took us close to an hour, depending on traffic.
…
summary: Mendung Kafe in Bandar Bukit Mahkota is a breakfast-focused cafe known for its cosy setting, Malay comfort food and relaxed morning pace, operating only until noon. The menu centres on nasi lemak variations, lontong and coffee, with generous portions, moderate prices and flavours that lean traditional rather than experimental. It suits diners who enjoy slow breakfasts with family or friends, paired with calm, unhurried atmosphere.
title: Mendung Kafe: Cosy breakfast spot serving tasty nasi lemak Makdee & perfectly crafted coffee

We all know the feeling of a brand new work week. You just had a great weekend, but now it’s time to get back to the Monday-to-Friday grind.
But there’s encouraging news for those of you working in the CBD area: another reason to look forward to going to the office on weekdays. 11Westside , a California-Mexican restaurant, recently launched 3 weekly promotions on Mondays , Tuesdays , and Wednesdays .
Credit: 11Westside
11Westside is located in Asia Square Tower 1 , so those of you who pass by frequently might find it familiar. The restaurant prides itself on delivering bold West Coast flavours and artisanal cocktails in a relaxed atmosphere, perfect for after-work dinners or drinks .
Credit: 11Westside
Kicking things off on Mondays is Margarita Mondays , featuring free-flow handcrafted margaritas and bar snacks you can pair with your Mexican-inspired orders . This deal is available from 5.30pm–8pm , while stocks last. I guess it’s a nice way to beat the Monday blues for those of you who work nearby.
Taco Tuesdays then take over on the second day of the week, offering 50% off all tacos from 6pm onwards . Menu highlights include Baja Fish (S$8) , Mango Shrimp (S$8) , and Wagyu Beef Cheek Birria (S$18 for 2pcs) . Planning a Tuesday post-work hangout with colleagues and friends doesn’t seem like such a bad idea!
Credit: 11Westside
Ladies, there’s also something for you to look forward to when dreaded mid-week comes. Ladies’ Night Wednesdays at 11Westside invites you to a free-flow suckling pig taco live station , and house pours for just S$9.90 .
This deal is only available between 5.30pm and 8pm , so it’s great for those of you who can leave the office early and don’t want to end your night too late.
Credit: 11Westside
For those of you who would rather have a lunchtime catch-up, 11Westside also offers a 3-course Executive Set Lunch at S$48++ on weekdays . Choose a starter , a main , and a daily dessert for a complete meal.
Beyond these new deals, 11Westside also recently revamped its regular menu , so it might really be time to check out this weekday CBD spot. Explore the full menu on the restaurant’s website .

Straight from its homecoming in Taiwan comes Bao Fast Foods, the newest concept from London’s cult favourite, Bao. Happening at New Bahru , the part fast food joint, part Asian convenience store also serves as the brand’s experimental testbed as the team gathers new ideas ahead of its first permanent outlet for Bao Fast Foods – fingers crossed that it’ll be in Singapore!
Bao Fast Foods’ Singapore pop-up: Details at a glance
When: 11 November to 28 December 2026
Price: Fried chicken starts from $6.50; rice box starts from $7.95; noodles start from $6.50
Opening hours: Daily, 11am to 10pm; closed on Tuesdays
Where: Bao Fast Foods’ Singapore pop-up , New Bahru, 46 Kim Yam Road, Singapore 239351
An introduction to Bao
Photography: Bao London via Instagram
Founded by Shing Tat Chung, Erchen Chang, and Wai Ting Chung, Bao started as a humble street food stall at East London’s Netil Market. Now, the brand boasts several locations across the city, including Soho, Borough, and King’s Cross. Beyond the deliciously affordable food, collaborations with brands such as Carhartt, WIP, and Dover Street Market proved Bao had more personality than just fluffy buns.
Unlike fast food in the West, convenience in the East is defined by care, thinking ahead, and service. Think about the joy of visiting a Lawson or Family Mart in Japan! With the creation of Bao Fast Foods, the group is on a mission to take Taiwanese culture worldwide in an accessible, quick-service format.
The BFF experience
What went down at Bao Fast Foods’ pop-up in Taiwan! Photography: Bao Fast Foods
The Bao Fast Foods pop-up at New Bahru comes with two concepts: the fast food joint and the convenience store.
At its core, the pop-up has a dedicated focus on food. Specifically, Taiwanese comfort food reworked with Bao’s signature meticulous detail and playful attitude. Psst: read on for more details (including prices) of the menu.
Surrounding it is the classic Asian convenience store facade. Reminiscent of bodegas with a touch of that local mama shop vibe, BFF’s shelves will be stocked with goodies like Taiwanese snacks and even Bao’s own branded merchandise and collaborations. There’ll also be grab-and-go sections and self-serve stations.
What to expect on the menu
Photography: Bao Fast Foods
On to the meat and potatoes (or rice, if you will) of the pop-up: the food.
The must-try is the chicken chopper ($6.50), BFF’s take on Taiwanese fried chicken – more than 140 versions in the making. Yes, the team takes their fried chicken game very seriously here. The brand has spent their time mastering the craft of creating the perfect crust and its seasoning powders, like how they do on Taiwanese streets.
For heartier dishes, opt for the rice box ($7.95) or have it with dan dan noodles ($6.50), or even beef cup noodles ($12.50). And to wash it all down, get one of the Taiwanese craft teas developed with Taiwan-based S.C Labs, in nitro or carbonated options.
Here’s a list of everything the brand has to offer so far:
• Chicken Chopper, available in Original Crispy, Flame Glazed, and Master Scalded flavours ($6.50)
• Rice box ($7.95)
• Dan dan noodles ($6.50)
• Beef cup noodles ($12.50)
• Fluffy Natural Alishan Wintermelon ($5.95)
• Orange Guava Beauty Tea ($6.50)
• The Original Peanut Oatside M*lk ($6)
• Egg sandos
• Marinated eggs
• “Fried Rice” quinoa
• BFF Broth
• Golden Kimchi
• Soy puddings
We’ll be back with a review of Bao Fast Foods’ pop-up at New Bahru soon, so watch this space!
Looking for other cool pop-ups and happenings in Singapore? Right this way…
• Age.3 is bringing Japanese sandos to Ion Orchard
• Sogurt is coming back with self-serve froyo and 10 rotating flavours!
• MilkyShop’s viral Butter Sand cookies are at New Bahru
Frequently Asked Questions
What is Bao Fast Foods (BFF)?
It's a Taiwanese-inspired fast food and convenience store concept, created by the founders of Bao, a London-based restaurant.
Is BFF the same as Bao?
BFF is a new concept created by the team at Bao. While it's not exactly the same as Bao, you can expect some signature dishes to make an appearance.
Is BFF permanent?
For now, BFF will be a pop-up at New Bahru. The team is looking to open its first permanent store in early 2027.
Do I need to make a reservation?
BFF's pop-up is a fast food style concept, so you don't have to make a reservation.
What should I order?
The chicken chopper is a must-try, and we'd get them in every flavour (if your calories allow you!).
summary: Straight from its homecoming in Taiwan comes Bao Fast Foods, the newest concept from London’s cult favourite, Bao. Happening at New Bahru, the part fast food joint, part Asian convenience store also serves as the brand’s experimental testbed as the team gathers new ideas ahead of its first permanent outlet for Bao Fast Foods –
title: Bao Fast Foods is coming to Singapore: Expect Taiwanese fried chicken, snacks, convenience store goodies, and BFF merch

Our top Christmas gift ideas in Singapore, incoming! It’s that time of the year when our work involves (window) shopping for the best Christmas gifts for everyone on your list – and we aren’t complaining. After all, the holiday season is here, and our shopping carts must follow suit. Once you’re done sprucing up your abode with one of the best Christmas trees in Singapore , it’s time to shop for festive gifts to lay out under the glittering firs. (And if you need more festive inspiration, check out our ultimate guide to Christmas in Singapore .)
Why trust this guide
We spend the festive season keeping tabs on new launches, gift sets and limited-edition drops, trying what we can and digging into the rest. Some picks make the cut because they’re practical or beautifully made; others, admittedly, are just things we’d be very happy to find under our own Christmas tree. Either way, we check the details, prices and availability before they land on this list, and keep updating it as new finds come in.
Fab Christmas gift ideas in Singapore for 2026
1. Colourful everyday gifts from Bynd Artisan
If you’re shopping for someone who appreciates a good-looking everyday essential, have a peek at Bynd Artisan’s Where Hearts Meet festive collection. This year’s edit mixes new launches with familiar favourites in fresh colours, with gifts for work, travel and home – handy when your Christmas list includes everyone from your desk buddy to the friend who’s impossible to buy for.
One of our picks is the silk twilly ($38), printed on both sides with artwork by The Letter J Supply. Tie it around a bag, wear it in your hair or loop it around your neck when an outfit needs a little something extra. There are plenty of small gifts around the same price point too, including printed leather tags ($38), a fruit coaster set ($45) and AirTag keyrings ($48) – useful little treats that won’t immediately get shoved to the back of a cupboard once Christmas is over.
Price: From $38 for the picks above
Where to buy: Shop online at Bynd Artisan, or visit Bynd Artisan at #03-24, Raffles City, 252 North Bridge Road, Singapore 179103
2. A one-of-a-kind coloured gemstone from Madly
Photography: Madly
For the person who’d rather receive something no one else has, skip the off-the-shelf jewellery and let them have a hand in creating their own. Singapore jewellery design house Madly specialises in coloured gemstones, from sapphires, rubies and emeralds to less expected finds like spinel, tsavorite and Paraiba tourmaline. Each bespoke piece is designed from scratch around the chosen stone, making it a truly unique Christmas gift idea for your loved one.
Christmas makes the proposition a little sweeter. Each week leading up to the big day, Madly will release a new Christmas Gem Edit from its vault. Secure one of the featured stones during its respective promotional week and you’ll receive $500 design credit towards turning that same gem into a bespoke piece. Don’t deliberate for too long – once the weekly edit ends, so does the credit. And plan ahead: bespoke pieces typically take around nine to 12 weeks to craft once the design is confirmed.
Price: Bespoke pieces generally from $3,500; $500 design credit with qualifying Christmas Gem Edit purchases
Where to buy: Madly , 13 Ann Siang Road, Singapore 069693
3. A classy wine preservation system from Coravin
Photography: Coravin
For the vino lover in your life, Coravin’s 2026 Limited-Edition Timeless Six+ in the brand-new rich blue finish is the gift to beat. This sleek, ultra-chic wine preservation gadget lets you pour from even your most precious bottles without popping the cork – meaning the rest of the wine stays fresh and fabulous for months (or even years!) to come.
So, how does it work? A precision needle slips through the cork to draw out the wine, while argon gas fills the space to keep oxygen at bay. Pull out the needle, and the cork naturally reseals like nothing ever happened. Now, that’s smart sipping. Cheers to that!
Price: $665
Where to buy: Shop online at Coravin
4. Aromatherapy treats from Hysses
Photography: Hysses
Shopping for someone who takes their wind-down routine seriously? Hysses’ Christmas collection has plenty to sniff through, without locking you into one giant hamper. For the homebody, the room scent gift set ($92.90) comes with four different fragrances to spritz around the house, while the handcrafted clay diffuser sets ($119.90) double as cute little decor pieces – no flame or electricity needed.
We’re also eyeing the Luxe Cloud shower steamers ($39.90 each) for an easy stocking filler. Pop one into the shower and let the warm steam release scents like lavender chamomile, palmarosa jasmine or bergamot geranium. And for the person whose fragrance preferences you’d rather not guess, Hysses’ mix-and-match range lets you pair two travel-sized body care essentials and choose the pouch or gift box they come in. Practical, personal, and much harder to get wrong.
Price: From $39.90

body:
Beautiful cafes in Singapore
With the countless #foodporn and #whatsonmytable flatlays on Instagram, social media has now gone way beyond simple snaps of food. New cafes sprouting all over Singapore have caught on to the Insta- and TikTok-action, and are now tempting us with their chic and aesthetic vibe on top of fancy food . Here’s a list of 21 beautiful cafes in Singapor e to check out when you want to up your cafe-hopping game.
1. Five Oars Coffee Roasters
Image credit: @stannertan
Weekend brunch at Five Oars Coffee Roasters is a must. Nothing revives an Instafeed like luscious green plants, wood accents, and cement floors. If you have never been here, expect a sort of Melbourne cafe scene meets Scandinavian vibe. The centrepiece of this cafe is a huge table filled with plants in the middle; make sure to come early for a seat on the most coveted table.
Five Oars Coffee Roasters offers that extra dose of fancy with their dishes plated beautifully. The prices here might be on the higher side, but you will not be disappointed in the taste department. Dishes to try from their brunch menu include Pork Ham Benedict ($24++) , featuring house-made sourdough, poached eggs, shredded Iberican pork, apple slaw, hollandaise sauce, caramelised onions. Else, get their Sticky Date Pancake ($12++) if you’re looking for something sweet.

2. Twenty Eight Cafe
Image credit: @daphn3poon
It is notoriously difficult to find a nice cafe with good natural lighting, but in the case of Twenty Eight Cafe , you need not worry. Unpretentious to a T, the cafe in Singapore is also minimally decorated with an industrial-chic interior design. The colours are a chic mix of greys and neutrals like black and white. This space also makes for a good place to do work or study, as it has charging ports and free Wi-Fi.
Image credit: @twentyeightcafe
Those who love breakfast but never seem to be able to wake up in time for it will be glad to know that Twenty Eight Cafe serves breakfast all day. Get your fill with the Common Breakfast ($30+) served with sausage, eggs, sourdough toast, bacon, beans, grilled tomato, mushroom, and hash brown, or their Avocado Smash ($20+) , one of their signatures. If you’re trying to eat cleaner, get their Salmon and Kale ($28++) , with pan-seared salmon, kale, hazelnut, pomegranate, onsen egg, and goma dressing.

3. Jin Yu Man Tang Dessert Shop
Located in East Coast is Jin Yu Man Tang Dessert Shop , which specialises in Chinese desserts. Within the cafe’s white walls, you’ll find wooden tables alongside leather chairs, as well as a hanging chair in the corner for that #metime moment. The space is also blessed with natural lighting and gorgeous potted plants that bring the outdoors in.
Their desserts are as much a treat for your palate as they are for your Instagram feed. Get your camera ready as a staff member pours warm milk into your bowl of Signature Ginger Milk Pudding ($5.80) . When executed correctly, the pudding is super smooth and melt-in-the-mouth. If you’re into traditional Cantonese desserts, try their Mango Pomelo Sago ($6.70) , featuring a mix of mango puree and milk topped with pomelo slivers, or the Peach Gum + Milk ($5.30) , which is fruity and creamy.

body:
Tan Ser Seng Herbal Soup , the Geylang shop that has sold turtle soup since 1946, has opened its first mall outlet at Great World this month, in the year the family business turns 80.
The new restaurant sits at #B1-106/107, 1 Kim Seng Promenade. It opens daily from 11am to 10pm, with last order at 9.30pm, and closes only for Chinese New Year. Great World MRT on the Thomson-East Coast Line (TE15) is the easy way in: Exit 6 leads into the mall at Basement 2, and the restaurant is one floor up.
Claypot Turtle Soup, the house signature since 1986. Photo: Tan Ser Seng Herbal Soup
From a shoulder pole to Lorong Bachok
The family traces its roots to Fengtang Xiang in Chao’an. Tan Ah Sai arrived in Singapore in 1927, aged 11, and after the war cooked herbal turtle soup for workers rebuilding the city, selling it bowl by bowl from a shoulder-pole pushcart before saving for a tricycle. He founded the business in 1946.
His son Tan Khar Seng took over the fire in 1973, at 20, while supporting eight siblings, and his wife Tay Ah Lek cooked through the night. In 1986 the shop moved to individual claypots, which the family bills as Singapore’s first claypot turtle soup. It settled at 29 Lorong Bachok in 1992, and the third generation, Vivian and Allan, joined in the 2000s.
The Tan family, photographed in a Singapore studio in the 1960s. Photo: Tan Ser Seng Herbal Soup
What a bowl costs
The family publishes dine-in prices for the Geylang shop and has not posted a separate Great World menu, so treat these as the reference point rather than a promise for Kim Seng Promenade.
• Claypot Turtle Soup: S$28 small, S$50 medium, S$78 large
• Double Boiled Turtle Soup: S$16 small, S$21 medium
• Premier Fish Maw and Abalone Soup: S$30
• Ginseng Black Chicken Soup and Cordyceps Chicken Soup: S$15 each
• Sugarcane, Water Chestnut and Imperatae Root Soup: S$9.90
The double-boiled small bowl is the cheapest way into the turtle soups. Sides run from S$6 for cucumber in vinaigrette to S$16.90 for steamed seabass with Teochew olive vegetable, and a bowl of Fragrant Yam Rice is S$2.50. The menu does not state whether service charge or GST applies. Prices on GrabFood, foodpanda and Oddle run higher than in the shop.
Double Boiled Turtle Soup, from S$16 at the Geylang shop. Photo: Tan Ser Seng Herbal Soup
Cordyceps Chicken Soup, S$15 at the Geylang shop. Photo: Tan Ser Seng Herbal Soup
Before you go
There are no table reservations at either branch. Seating is walk-in, first come, first served. The Great World outlet takes WhatsApp messages only, on 8997 0368. Pick-up orders and food reservations go through a separate WhatsApp line, 8737 2929, and food is set aside once paid.
Tan Ser Seng is not halal-certified. It serves pork dishes, and some soups carry a splash of house herbal wine. The family describes its soups in traditional terms and is clear that the descriptions are not medical advice.
The original shop at 29 Lorong Bachok keeps shorter hours, 11am to 8.30pm daily with last order at 8pm, a five-minute walk from Aljunied MRT.
The Lorong Bachok shop in Geylang, home to the family since 1992. Photo: Tan Ser Seng Herbal Soup
summary: Geylang's 1946 turtle soup house opens at Great World in its 80th year: hours, MRT access, menu prices and what to know before you go.
title: Tan Ser Seng turns 80 and opens its first mall outlet at Great World

When the F&B business gets tough, we often see restaurant owners reducing operating hours or cutting down on manpower. Not Jacky Tan , though, the owner of Cheeky Don at Millenia Walk . He actually created a video game that celebrates Singapore’s rich hawker culture — Hawker Fantasy .
Hawker Fantasy is a free retro role-playing game (RPG) which showcases our beloved hawker culture and food through food-themed battles. You can also look forward to local references and iconic dishes being in the game. Hawker Fantasy is free to play and can be accessed through a phone browser without downloading an app. Which is great for people like me whose phone storage space is exploding. You can try it out here .
I tried the game out and here’s what you can expect. Players will take control of 3 heroes with familiar and hilarious names: Ah Beng , Ah Huat and Ah Lian . What’s scarier than bland, tasteless food? That’s why you’ll follow them as they travel across Singapore to stop the evil Bland Emperor from turning all our beloved local food tasteless.
Along the way, I encountered bosses inspired by familiar hawker fare, with every stage set at a real hawker centre or food street. The food-inspired villains include Rojak Bromance, a youtiao donning chic sunglasses accompanied by a pineapple wearing a cap. There is also the Sambal Stingray Baron from our famous Chomp Chomp Food Centre.
Once you defeat the bosses, you’ll unlock a “ food gem “: the dish, its history, and what to order when you visit. Additionally, through the game’s Hawker Dex , you’ll discover the stories of 88 dishes along with the background of the communities who created them. Beyond in-game fun, Hawker Fantasy also encourages its players to visit real-life hawker centres.
With the game’s Makan Passport , players can visit hawker centres around Singapore and stamp down their own food photos. Sounds fun? That’s not even all — I won’t spoil all the fun for you, but trust me when I say there are so many more features to this game, even secret stages! Try it out for yourself, and you might find yourself addicted.
10 best video game stores in Singapore that are ahead of the game
summary: Hawker Fantasy is a free, retro-style role-playing game created by Jacky Tan, owner of Cheeky Don at Millenia Walk, to celebrate Singapore’s hawker culture. Players control 3 heroes, battle food-inspired bosses at real hawker centres, unlock the histories of local dishes and explore 88 entries in the Hawker Dex. Accessible through a phone browser without an app download, it suits local food enthusiasts interested in interactive ways to discover hawker heritage.
title: Hawker Fantasy – hawker themed video game created by donburi restaurant owner

A short ferry ride, a change of scenery, and perhaps a long lunch by the water ? Batam is welcoming a new waterfront destination this December , as Opus Bay begins its phased opening with the promise of leisurely island stays, waterfront dining, and a little retail therapy along the way.
Credit – Opus Bay
Just 45 minutes by ferry from Singapore , the integrated resort will make its debut with Marina Bay Ferry Cove , its own ferry terminal, and Residence on Opus Bay , home to the 493-room Balmoral Tower hotel . The best part: the hotel is only a 3-minute walk from the terminal — so less walking, more vacationing!
Credit – Opus Bay
Getting there is as easy as a breeze. The upgraded Marina Bay Ferry Cove will offer direct access to the resort, with ferry connections from Singapore’s HarbourFront and Singapore Cruise Centre . Guests can also look forward to a VIP lounge, dedicated priority lanes, and buggy services to assist with luggage.
Credit – Opus Bay
Beyond checking into your room, there will be more to explore as the resort develops. Bay Boulevard Marina Promenade , opening in a later phase, is planned to bring together waterfront restaurants, a food hall serving local favourites, specialty boutiques, and a supermarket.
Expect a leisurely mix of shopping and dining, with Indonesian designers, locally crafted souvenirs, and resortwear adding a distinctly island-inspired touch.
Credit – Opus Bay
For something to get your blood pumping between meals, Opus Bay will also feature 3 padel courts — including one built to competition standards — alongside 4 pickleball courts . Hotel guests will enjoy complimentary access, so you can work up an appetite before settling in for another meal.
Credit – Opus Bay
While the full line-up of facilities will arrive in stages, Opus Bay is already shaping up to be an appealing addition to Batam’s growing leisure scene . Think an easy island escape without the fuss of a long-haul journey, with the prospect of sea views, unhurried afternoons, and plenty to discover as the resort takes shape.
Planning a year-end getaway? Keep Opus Bay Batam on your radar, and check which facilities are open before making your reservation.
What to expect from Penang’s 1st waterfront mall with 300+ outlets & sea views, opening 29 Oct
summary: Opus Bay in Batam begins its phased opening in December, with a 493-room hotel at Residence on Opus Bay just a 3-minute walk from its dedicated ferry terminal, around 45 minutes from Singapore. Planned facilities include waterfront dining, retail outlets, padel and pickleball courts, with hotel guests enjoying complimentary court access. It is suited to travellers seeking a convenient island getaway, though facilities will open in stages.
title: Batam’s new waterfront resort Opus Bay opens this December, just 45 minutes from Singapore

ActiveSG Punggol Sport Centre in Punggol
It really feels like they’re playing favourites when it comes to new openings in the heartlands. Of course, we’re talking about the North-East; from Punggol Coast Mall to autonomous self-driving shuttles , those residing at the tail-end of the purple line have been getting a steady stream of shiny new amenities to call their own as of late.
And now, they’ve got one more to lay claim to: the new ActiveSG Punggol Sport Centre . Initially slated for a 2023 opening, it’s finally in its soft launch phase, which means it’s open to the public as we speak. So, we popped by to check it out; here’s everything the sporty amongst us can get excited about that warrants an early visit.
How to get to ActiveSG Punggol Sport Centre?
The ActiveSG Punggol Sport Centre is pretty accessible, especially if you’re already residing in the North-East. Located a stone’s throw from One Punggol and SAFRA Punggol, hop on a train from the Punggol LRT station and alight at the very next station on the West Loop , Sam Kee LRT station . Take a 3-minute walk , and you’ll arrive at the sports centre in a jiffy.
Image adapted from: Google Maps
Alternatively, you can take bus no. 84W , 117 , 117M , 382 , or 382G and alight at the Opp One Punggol bus stop (stop ID: 65481) , which will put you right in front of the ActiveSG Punggol Sport Centre. Plenty of parking is available at the facility too; even if it gets full during peak hours, you can opt to park your vehicle at the nearby One Punggol car park.
Although the walk over to the ActiveSG Punggol Sport Centre from Punggol MRT station is just 10 minutes , there’s heavy construction work taking place along Punggol Place Road as of writing. As such, we recommend getting there via public transport for now to avoid additional detours.
What is the ActiveSG Punggol Sport Centre?
Initially scheduled for completion in 2023, the ActiveSG Punggol Sport Centre is a part of Singapore’s Sports Facilities Master Plan, which was a key initiative of Vision 2030 – our national sports blueprint that seeks to foster a healthier, more inclusive society through sports while developing high-performance athletes.
Image adapted from: ActiveSG
Delays were spurred on by the pandemic, but fast-forward a couple of years, and the facility is currently in its soft launch phase, with its official opening happening on 22nd November 2026 . Almost all of the sports centre’s facilities are open to the public, and you’ll be able to book them via the ActiveSG website . Simply log in with your Singpass account, and you can book them or buy swim or gym passes for your visit.
Be sure to check if you’ve got remaining ActiveSG credits , as you can use them to pay for your bookings and passes. Do note that ActiveSG Punggol Sport Centre’s swimming complex, futsal courts, and football stadium are currently not open to the public ; they’ll be opening sometime in November 2026.
What to expect at the ActiveSG Punggol Sport Centre?
With 6 floors of sporty facilities to take in, there’s much to do at the new ActiveSG Punggol Sport Centre. We’ve broken down all of their offerings; here’s what you can expect at each one, starting from the ground up.
Level 1: Football Stadium & Swimming Complex
One of the more impressive inclusions at the ActiveSG Punggol Sport Centre is their massive football stadium . It’s not any plain ol’ pitch; this stadium can fit up to 5,000 spectators in its grandstands, comparable to the one over at Our Tampines Hub.
It even comes equipped with powerful floodlights that are designed to meet international football standards – perhaps a sign that it’ll potentially play host to major competitions like the Singapore Premier League in the future. However, you can’t personally lace up for your own games on the artificial pitch just yet, as bookings are not currently available.
Also located on Level 1 is the swimming complex , another standout feature of the facility. It has 4 different swimming pools , catering to folks who want to take their swimming seriously, recreational swimmers, and waddling tots at the same time.
There’s a sheltered, 8-lane swimming pool to swim laps around, along with a similar outdoor pool for swimmers to soak in the sun as they work on their strokes. Nearby, there’s a shallow water play area complete with tunnels and slides that’s bound to be a hotspot for kids.
But stealing the spotlight is the swimming complex’s 50m-long infinity pool . The views here are stellar too; while the world-famous one at MBS unlocks aerial views of the Singapore skyline, this one overlooks the verdant green of Punggol Waterway Park . But your swimming sessions here will have to wait for now, as the swimming complex will only be open next month.
Level 2: Gym & Gym activity rooms

summary: Punggol just got more exciting.

Deepavali in Singapore is happening soon, in case you haven’t noticed the lights along Serangoon Road. The Festival of Lights falls on the 15th day of Kartika, which is the holiest month in the Hindu calendar. This year, it’s celebrated on 8 November 2026. On the lookout for gorgeous lights, beautiful rangoli decorations to bring good luck, mouth-watering Indian cuisine, and fun events? We’ve put together a list of Deepavali events for the festive season. If you want to look your best, here’s where to find traditional and modern Indian clothes in Singapore .
Events to celebrate Deepavali in Singapore
1. Indian Heritage Centre’s Deepavali Open House
Photography: Indian Heritage Centre
The best way to celebrate Deepavali in Singapore? At the Indian Heritage Centre’s Deepavali Open House, with loads of celebrations from now till 8 November 2026. On weekends, you can join free museum tours, watch special performances, redeem free money packets, and browse the weekend bazaar. If you’re hungry, snack on traditional treats like murukku and masala chai while you get your free henna done.

How much: Tickets start from $32.50
Where: Shiv Kamdar’s Diwali , Zouk Singapore, 3C River Valley Road, Singapore 179022

Photography: Indian Heritage Centre
Every year, Little India turns it on for Deepavali with its eye-popping light-up. Just when you think the street lights can’t get any more dazzling, out come massive peacocks, lotus flowers and oil lamps beautifying Serangoon Road and Race Course Road. You seriously can’t miss it – time to plan an evening stroll!
When: Daily until 28 November 2026
Where: Along Serangoon Road and Race Course Road

Inside Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple. Photography: Choo Yut Shing

Cheesecakes in Singapore can be found just about anywhere, but they’re not quite the same as the silky delights from Tokyo’s Mr. Cheesecake. With over a million cheesecakes sold in Japan, these masterfully crafted desserts come from chef Koji Tamura. Through the art of Japanese precision, the humble cheesecake has been given a massive upgrade. But what makes Mr. Cheesecake’s desserts so worth the wait? Here’s the 411.
Mr. Cheesecake’s pop-up in Singapore: Details at a glance
When: 11 November to 30 December 2026
Price: TBC
Opening hours: TBC
Where: Mr. Cheesecake’s pop-up , Ion Orchard, opposite Hermes, Level 3, 2 Orchard Turn, Singapore 238801
What makes Mr. Cheesecake special
Photography: Mr. Cheesecake
From classic cheesecakes and burnt Basque cheesecakes to other dessert options like roll cakes, tiramisu, and financiers, Mr. Cheesecake’s offerings are nothing out of the ordinary. So what is it about these cakes that made this brand go insanely viral in Tokyo?
Part of Mr. Cheesecake’s uniqueness is in the method of serving. Its signature cheesecake has three different taste profiles, depending on the temperature you serve it. You can enjoy it frozen, where it’s extra tart and tastes like ice cream cake. Wait a little while for it to warm up and you get a contrast of textures with a smooth outer layer and frozen centre. Or have it fully thawed for a mouthfeel akin to creme brulee – the best way to enjoy the sweetness and aroma.
Mr. Cheesecake’s key flavours also read like a perfume list in the best way possible. Made with vanilla, white chocolate, tonka bean, and lemon, it’s skillfully balanced to create a rich but light cake.
And as Mr. Cheesecake says: it may not be the best in the world, but it might just be the best you’ll ever have in your life.
What to expect at the Singapore pop-up
Photography: Mr. Cheesecake
Very few details have been released about the brand’s upcoming Singapore pop-up. Given that it is the brand’s first-ever pop-up in Southeast Asia, we’re expecting minimalist displays that shine the spotlight on the main star – the cheesecakes.
We’re told to expect a curated line-up of five creations, brought together for the first time just for the Singapore debut. Flavours you can look forward to include the matcha and caramel Earl Grey cheesecakes and the rich tiramisu.
We’ll be back with more updates as more information rolls out, so stay tuned!
Frequently Asked Questions
What is Mr. Cheesecake?
It's a brand founded in 2018 by chef Koji Tamura. Mr. Cheesecake is best known for its (you guessed it) cheesecakes with rich and creamy flavour.
Why is it so popular?
Thanks to its distinct texture and layered flavours, Mr. Cheesecake is exceptionally popular in Japan. You can enjoy the cake at three different temperatures, and each has its unique texture and flavour.
Where is the Mr. Cheesecake pop-up?
It'll be located within Ion Orchard.
Is this Mr. Cheesecake's first pop-up?
Yes, this is the brand's inaugural pop-up in Southeast Asia.
Will this be permanent?
As far as we've heard, Mr. Cheesecake has no plans on opening a permanent store in Singapore.
summary: Cheesecakes in Singapore can be found just about anywhere, but they’re not quite the same as the silky delights from Tokyo’s Mr. Cheesecake. With over a million cheesecakes sold in Japan, these masterfully crafted desserts come from chef Koji Tamura. Through the art of Japanese precision, the humble cheesecake has been given a massive upgrade.
title: Tokyo’s cult-favourite Mr. Cheesecake makes its Singapore debut at Ion Orchard

Rollercoasters, marine encounters, retail therapy and destination dining may be among the best-known draws at Resorts World Sentosa . But look beyond the headliners and you’ll find another side of the resort hiding in plain sight: sustainability is woven into many of the places you explore, from attractions and dining experiences to hotel stays. We’ve rounded up seven sustainability initiatives to explore Resorts World Sentosa’s greener side across your next few visits!
1. Stay cool as a cucumber
Photography: Resorts World Sentosa
Between dining, shopping and exploring the wider resort, Singapore’s heat and humidity can quickly make their presence known. So, what can you do about it?
Enter: Weave . This lifestyle and dining hub uses ETFE roofs and large fans to keep the space cool. The roof blocks up to 80% of solar heat while still letting natural light in, and the ventilation systems help keep the air moving. The result is a brighter, breezier place to pause between stops, whether you are dining at Moutarde by celebrated French chef Paul Pairet or cooling down with a soft serve from Sundae Royale .
2. In oceans deep
Photography: Resorts World Sentosa
Singapore Oceanarium is a popular attraction with marine life and immersive habitats that’ll wow you. But while they’re bound to steal the show, there’s plenty to discover beyond the habitats, too.
The oceanarium runs programmes such as Ocean Advocates and Citizen Science, where the public can sign up for activities ranging from coastal and marine clean-ups to biodiversity monitoring.
Got little ones in tow? They’ll be in awe of animal care specialists diving to feed animals like moray eels, rays, sharks and more, happening every day at the Open Ocean Habitat at 4pm (except Monday and Friday).
For a closer look at marine life, try PADI Discover Snorkelling, a 90-minute beginner-friendly experience that lets you spot manta rays, sharks and schools of fish from the surface of the oceanarium’s Open Ocean Habitat. Open to guests aged 10 and above, it requires no prior swimming or snorkelling experience.
3. A (green) walk to remember
Photography: Resorts World Sentosa
Did you know there’s a ginormous coastal forest in Sentosa? Just beside Equarius Hotel is a 2.9-hectare wild pocket of greenery that’s home to 93 plant species, 17 avian species and 21 butterfly species. Fun fact: Resorts World Sentosa regularly monitors the area’s ecological health, making this more than just a “green space”.
Keep an eye out for the Heritage Trees while exploring. Recognised under the National Parks Board’s Heritage Tree Scheme, these protected trees offer a glimpse into the island’s natural landscape – way before the resort arrived. It’s a quieter side of Sentosa worth taking the time to discover, whether as a visit in its own right or as part of a longer stay.
4. Soaking up the sun
Photography: Resorts World Sentosa
Besides the adrenaline-pumping rides, interactive shows and Illumination’s Minions, there’s something else to look out for at Universal Studios Singapore . Look up! We’re talking about more than 1,500 solar panels sitting across the theme park’s rooftops. These green features harness Singapore’s sunshine to power the attractions below.
Also, the theme park’s latest attraction, Illumination’s Minion Land, has attained the BCA Green Mark Platinum Zero Energy Building status, thanks to energy-efficient features and solar installations incorporated into its design.
5. It’s a garden-to-table affair
Photography: Resorts World Sentosa
On another visit, make food the focus at the Laurus Table with a twist. As part of The Laurus Kitchen Sessions, you’ll start with a guided tour of its herb garden before heading into the kitchen to prepare your meal using seasonal ingredients. And yes, that includes the herbs you’ve just seen growing outside.
The garden is just one part of Resorts World Sentosa’s wider initiative on food sustainability, with the resort supporting local suppliers and responsibly sourcing more than half of its seafood.
6. Enjoy a sip from the garden
Photography: Resorts World Sentosa
When the occasion calls for a slower evening, wind down at The Collector’s Bar at The Laurus, where the “garden to the glass” concept brings ingredients from the garden straight into the drinks menu.
Try the Zest of Eden, made with vodka, fresh ginger, lime, lemongrass cordial and ginger beer. Or go for the Spiced Solstice if you’re skipping the booze. Either way, it is an experience to savour without rushing to the next stop.
7. Small details, greener stays
Photography: Resorts World Sentosa
If you are extending one of your visits with a stay, look closely and you will find sustainability built into the Hotel Ora experience. Here, you’ll find refillable water carafes and bulk bathroom amenities in the rooms. These help to reduce single-use plastics and unnecessary packaging.
…
summary: Rollercoasters, marine encounters, retail therapy and destination dining may be among the best-known draws at Resorts World Sentosa. But look beyond the headliners and you’ll find another side of the resort hiding in plain sight: sustainability is woven into many of the places you explore, from attractions and dining experiences to hotel stays. title: 7 sustainability initiatives you can actually see at Resorts World Sentosa

We all know and love Orchard Road as an iconic shopping destination in Singapore. But when the hunger pangs call, finding the perfect dining spot can leave us stumped – especially if you’re searching for a quiet restaurant away from the crowds that delivers on its ambience, food and drinks. Enter Slainte at Paragon, Orchard, a newly revamped sanctuary that hits all the marks. Made for intimate date nights and convivial group hangouts alike, Slainte might be that day-to-night spot you need on your radar.
Slainte at Orchard: Details at a glance
Best for: An inviting day-to-night spot with charcoal-grilled dishes and rare whiskies
Must-try dishes: Snow aging yukimuro full blood wagyu; miso-glazed Patagonian toothfish; salt-roasted carabinero; Iberico pluma
Price: Starters from $9; mains from $19; desserts from $19; drinks from $5
Opening hours: Daily, 11am to 10pm
Address: #04-09, Paragon Shopping Centre, 290 Orchard Road, Singapore 238859
Cosy up in a chic and inviting setting
Photography: Slainte
Step inside Slainte, and you’ll be instantly enveloped in a warm and welcoming ambience. From the cave-like stone walls to wooden furnishing and warm glow, every inch of the restaurant is designed to make you linger.
With a perfect balance of intimacy and luxury, it is a space that makes for easy and effortless conversations. Coupled with its quieter location away from the main shopping strip, Slainte is where you can finally take a breather from the hustle and bustle.
A smoky menu takes centre stage
Bold, smoky flavours and charcoal grilling anchor the menu at Slainte. The restaurant’s state-of-the-art Kopa oven is where all the grilling magic happens. Fired by charcoal and applewood, this showstopper reaches a blistering 600 degrees Celsius.
The results? An irresistible menu kissed by smoke, serving up unbeatable juiciness and deeply charred flavours that can’t be replicated at home.
Photography: Slainte
The flame-grilled selection beckons with signatures like black Angus porterhouse ($78), char siew Iberico pork jowl ($17) with a sweet-savoury glaze, Jack’s Creek wagyu hanger steak ($58), miso-glazed Patagonian toothfish ($38), and an 18-hour-marinated ayam bakar ($24).
And don’t miss the Iberico pork ($42) cooked to medium-well – we hear it’s one of the best in town. Enjoy these succulent meats and seafood with moreish sides ($9 each) like French onion mac and cheese, smashed crispy potatoes and charred asparagus.
Beyond these charcoal-grilled creations, we’re also eyeing starters like the scallop and prawn tartlets ($25) for a savoury pastry with fresh seafood, and hearty plates such as the signature yuzu kosho pasta ($29). With an extensive selection of pasta, vibrant salads and hearty mains, you’ll be left happily spoilt for choice from day through night.
Sip auctioned-sourced whiskies by the dram
Photography: Slainte
Curious about the world of whisky? Take a seat at Slainte to get started. The restaurant offers a collection of auction-sourced rare whisky that you can sip by the dram from just $15. Take it as your licence to try lesser seen whisky labels, each with its unique taste, history and craftsmanship.
Wines, champagne and creative cocktails are also available. We recommend trying the specially concocted cocktails, including the signature Slainte. An ode to the restaurant’s Irish roots, it is a blend of smoky Islay Scotch, sweet vermouth, Aperol and cinnamon.
Hello Slainte, our new go-to spot in Orchard
In an area known for glitz and sky-high prices, Slainte is where you can treat yourself to a well-crafted dining experience without the hefty price tags. On your next shopping spree in Orchard, swing by the restaurant to indulge in charcoal-grilled delicacies and sip fine whiskies and cocktails.

China-famous Yee3 is opening in Singapore this November
Image credit: Yee3
ION Orchard has been popping off lately, with the newly revamped Food Opera and a plethora of new international F&B brands. Now, it’s about to get even more exciting: China’s viral coconut drink brand Yee3 is set to make its debut in the mall in mid-November 2026 , giving competitors a run for their money.
Image credit: Yee3
For the uninitiated, Yee3 is a Shanghai-born brand, best known for its unique spin on coconut drinks. It’s since expanded to more than 500 outlets globally, drawing long queues in Kuala Lumpur and even in Sydney.
The brand prides itself on creating lighter and healthier drinks, using fresh Thai coconut water and no excessive sweeteners in all its products.
Image credit: Yee3
Look forward to an extensive menu of interesting coconut-based flavours and concoctions. The must-order here would be the Pistachio Cloud Coconut Water (price TBD) , with over five million cups sold worldwide. Other drinks in the Cloud Coconut Water Series (price TBD) include Salt Cheese Cloud Coconut (price TBD) and Oreo Storm Coconut (price TBD) .
Image credit: Yee3
Another highlight would be Yee3’s Coconut Frost Shake Series (price TBD) , marking Singapore’s first “frost fried” coconut drink. Made fresh to order daily, every cup comprises flash-iced coconut for a frosty texture and finish, churned with a gelato machine for maximum creaminess.
Choose from a variety of flavours, including Original , Matcha , and fruity options such as Grape , Watermelon , and Mango .
Image credit: Yee3
For mint fans, the Mint Coconut Water (price TBD) is an ultra-refreshing and cooling pick. On top of that, Yee3 also has a Coconut Sticky Rice Series (price TBD) in its line-up, with flavours such as Mango , Pistachio , and Taro .
While we don’t have prices for the upcoming SG outlet, the drinks usually cost between ¥13 and ¥28 in China, which works out to roughly $2.50 to $5.40 at current exchange rates. Do note that prices here may differ.
Although an official launch date has yet to be announced, we’ll keep this article updated with more information once we have it.
In more food news, Singaporean competitive eater Zermatt Neo has just opened Restaurant OVER in Tanjong Pagar. If you’re looking for more Japanese food spots, read our guide to the best new Japanese F&B openings in 2026 .
Address: 2 Orchard Turn, #B4-70, ION Orchard, Singapore 238001
Opening hours: TBD
Website
Yee3 is not halal-certified.
Feature image adapted from Yee3.

body:
Chaleur Atelier Patisserie in JB sells hyper-realistic cakes
Cake lovers heading across the Causeway, here’s one for your JB itinerary . Just a 15-minute drive from JB CIQ , Chaleur Atelier Patisserie makes hyper-realistic, fruit-shaped cakes that look almost too cute to be eat.
2-Day JB Itinerary: Affordable Desserts, Famous Zi Char, Thrifting And More
The current exchange rate is RM1 = ~S$0.32 as of 30 October 2026.
Chaleur is a modern French cake shop on the ground floor of Zennith Suites Service Apartments .
The whole menu is free of pork, lard, and alcohol. We tried three of its fruit cakes.
First up is the Mango Serai (RM29.80) . Its chocolate coating encases vanilla mousse, vanilla sponge, and a mango serai compote. For those who don’t know, serai is the Malay word for lemongrass, though we couldn’t discern a distinct lemongrass flavour.
Mango lovers will be happy to know there are real mango chunks inside. It’s a little on the sweet side, though, especially with the chocolate shell, so it’s a good one to share.
Next up, the Yuzu Pear (RM29.80) , shaped to look like a green pear.
This cake comprises vanilla pear parfait and a yuzu pear compote on a vanilla genoise, all wrapped in chocolate.
It was the most refreshing of the three, and less sweet than we expected. The yuzu was a nice touch, though we’d have liked it to come through stronger.
Our favourite was the Coconut Gula Melaka (RM29.80) .
Under the chocolate coating are coconut mousse, a Hawaiian pandan coconut layer, and gula melaka pain de Gênes, a French almond sponge. The best part was the real young coconut shreds in the middle. The sponge was a little dry, but the moist, creamy coconut mousse made up for it.
The shop itself is simple, with only a few seats, but it’s clean and works well for a quick dessert stop.
Overall, Chaleur is worth the detour for something unique in JB. Each cake comes to about S$9.20, which is reasonable for this level of workmanship. The shop isn’t far from the checkpoint, so you can dabao a box back to your hotel or even home to SG. Just get them into a fridge as soon as you can, because ours started melting quite fast.
For more cross-border sweet treats, check out our comprehensive JB cafe guide . If you’d rather stay on this side of the Causeway, read our master guide to the best bakeries in Singapore .

Tel: +60 14-665 0928

body:
The rise of protein coffee and tea in Singapore
As a zillennial, I adopt a fair number of Gen Z trends, from matcha lattes and thrifting to self-photo booths, but the trend that really stuck with me was fitnessmaxxing, AKA going all in on your workouts.
You may have seen reports that Gen Z is hitting the gym more thanks to social media and peer influence. I can vouch for the latter. With a social circle full of 2000s babies who have swapped nights out drinking for Pilates and CrossFit classes, it was only a matter of time before I got influenced too.
Within weeks of joining the gym, my fellow gym junkies were already bombarding me with questions: “Have you hit your macros?” “Do you drink protein shakes ?” As a coffee drinker who eats out often, my meals tend to be heavy on rice and noodles and light on protein, so I started buying ready-to-drink coffees with added protein, such as Rokeby and Meiji, to make up the difference. Very soon, protein coffee, or “proffee”—as it’s known online—became part of my training routine.
Turns out I’m not the only one—beverage chains have caught on too, with Starbucks Singapore launching their Protein Cold Foam on 7 October, PlayMade rolling out a protein smoothie series two days later, and Tim Hortons offering their own protein drinks. So, I picked up two drinks from each brand to answer one question: is protein coffee worth the hype, or is it just another food fad?
How did protein coffee become a thing?
Protein coffee started gaining traction on social media around late 2021, when people began mixing protein powder into iced coffee. The trend has since racked up over 20.2 million related posts on TikTok . But TikTok isn’t the only driver. Other reports, including this article by The Straits Times , have also linked the rise of protein-focused eating to GLP-1 weight-loss drugs (such as Ozempic), which suppress appetite and make prioritising protein more important for maintaining muscle.
Protein coffee is also part of a bigger movement called “proteinmaxxing”, the internet term for getting as much protein as possible into your day. What started in gym circles has since gone mainstream, with protein now added to everything from cereal and Pop-Tarts to, as you’ll see later in this article, bubble tea.
Sure, protein coffee could well be a cash grab. But if that added protein actually does something for us, is it really so bad if everyone comes out ahead?
Is protein coffee just a fad?
Personally, I don’t think protein coffee is completely a fad, but it could be a phase, much like collagen coffee before it. The functional coffee market, which covers everything from added protein to adaptogens, is projected to grow about 70% between 2026 and 2031 . Then again, it could fizzle out once something shinier comes along. Fibre looks like the next contender, with forecaster Datassential naming it the top health trend to follow protein in 2026.
But before deciding whether protein coffee is worth the hype, there’s the more basic question of whether you need the extra protein at all. You could also be paying a premium for a “healthy” label, since the word “protein” alone doesn’t guarantee a big nutritional benefit. Singapore’s Health Promotion Board recommends about 0.8g of protein per kg of body weight a day, or roughly 50g to 60g for adults aged 18 to 49.
At 46kg, that baseline works out to just 37g a day for me. A typical protein coffee with 20g to 30g of protein covers about half to 80% of it, and since I train every day and often miss even that on days when my meals have no protein, I’m probably exactly who proffee is meant for.
That said, I’m no dietitian, so do check with one before changing your diet, especially if you have underlying health conditions.
Is protein coffee actually good for you?
Starting with the pros: it’s an easy way to hit your daily protein target, which supports muscle maintenance and repair, and protein can keep hunger in check. For me, convenience is the biggest draw, since it’s readily available at most gyms and convenience stores.
Image adapted from [u/No_Tell_6675] via Reddit
Proffee might also be gentler on the nerves, since dietitians say protein can help buffer the effects of caffeine. One Redditor says the Rokeby Double Espresso doesn’t give them the jitters that regular coffee does, and I can vouch for that, since too much caffeine gives me heart palpitations. Plus, powders can be whey, plant-based or collagen, making it suitable for vegan and other diets.
On the flip side, some protein drinks are loaded with sugar or artificial ingredients that can undo the benefit, and certain sugar substitutes can cause bloating or stomach discomfort. Then there’s the taste, which matters more than you’d think, because for a lot of coffee drinkers, the coffee itself is the whole point.
Image adapted from [u/adtechheck] via Reddit
…
summary: Protein coffee in everywhere in Singapore now. We tried six protein drinks in Singapore to see if they're actually worth the hype.

Best Raffles Place food places
The hustle and bustle of the CBD mostly happens during weekday lunch hours. Every weekday, streams of office ladies and gentlemen raid the area looking for grub to fuel them for the day ahead. From the quick and cheap to the payday splurge, here are the best Raffles Place food places that will cater to any budget.
1. OGOG
If you love Korean food but you’re on a budget, OGOG is the place for you. This casual eatery at CIMB Plaza offers Korean cai png from just $9.90 , where you can choose from different bases and side dishes.
The most affordable option is the 3-Dish Ban sang (from $9.90) , which gives you a base—such as rice—alongside three Korean dishes, and a choice between kimchi or a sauce. We recommend the Soy Garlic Oven Baked Chicken and Gochujang Pork (+$1) or Gochujang Soy Mackarel for mains, as well as the mini-sized Kimchi Pancake or Shrimp Pancake for something bite-sized and easier to eat.
Read our OGOG feature .
Address: 30 Raffles Place, #B1-30, CIMB Plaza, Singapore 048622
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 11am to 3pm, 5:30pm to 8pm
Website
OGOG is not halal-certified.
Build Your Own Korean Cai Png From $9.90 At This Raffles Place Kiosk
2. Nakoko
For a refreshing treat to beat the heat, get an acai bowl at Nakoko , conveniently located at Lau Pa Sat . The acai soft serve here is dairy-free, and you can choose from over 15 different toppings to customise your bowl to your liking.
A medium cup costs $6.20 while a large costs $7.70 . We’d say the classic acai base is the best when paired with fresh fruits and some Baked Cashews , finished with the creamy Almond Nut Butter drizzle. The acai spot is only a five-minute walk from Raffles Place MRT Station , and you don’t have to worry about seats, as you can enjoy it straight at the hawker centre.

If it’s your first time here, we recommend getting the crowd-favourite Stir-Fried Pork with Abalone and Chilli ($28.80++) . body:
Best coffee cafes in Singapore sorted by neighbourhood
My friends often joke that my blood is made up of iced coffee. It’s true, I am a self-proclaimed coffee fanatic. If you are like me and subsist on a diet of caffeine, check out our list of the best coffee cafes in Singapore for a good brew . Some of them serve food too, if you want bites to go along with your favourite coffee. Many of them also roast their own beans, so you can take home a bag or two to make your own coffee at home.
Best coffee cafes in Singapore, in a nutshell:
• Best coffee cafe in town: Cafe Manna – Orchard cafe hidden inside a former chapel with coffee and matcha
• Best coffee in the CBD: Hellu Coffee – Long queue cafe in Telok Ayer with cream-topped lattes and croffles
• Best home-based cafe for coffee: Brew With Grace – Studio Ghibli-themed home cafe with a resident cat
• Best coffee chain: Luckin Coffee – China’s most famous coffee chain with 99-cent coffee
• Famous coffee shop in Singapore: Apartment Coffee – Rated the best coffee in Asia
Orchard coffee cafes
1. Rise Bakehouse – Popular cafe with locally inspired lattes
Muslim-friendly brunch cafe with unique drinks
What is Rise Bakehouse? Rise Bakehouse is a Muslim-friendly brunch cafe at TripleOne Somerset with two other outlets across Singapore. Here, you can expect all-day brunch, pasta dishes, gelato with waffles and more. For coffee, the Milo Mocha Gao ($9++) is the one to order. The kopi is strong enough to balance the chocolatey Milo, and a roasted coffee note lingers after each sip. It comes with a cream biscuit for dipping. Another unique drink is the Pandan Matcha Cloud Latte ($9++) , which is creamy, earthy, and sweet.
Read our Rise Bakehouse Chinatown review .
Expect to pay: $20–$30++ per person
What to order: Milo Mocha Gao ($9++), Pandan Matcha Cloud Latte ($9++)
Address: 111 Somerset Road, #01-05, TripleOne Somerset, Singapore 238164

Tel: 8928 9111

2. Bacha Coffee – Luxury international coffee brand at ION Orchard
100% Arabica specialty coffee from 35 countries
Image credit: @bachacoffeeofficial
What is Bacha Coffee? Dining at Bacha Coffee will make you feel like royalty. You sip your coffee in a Moroccan-style coffee room, overlooking a display of beautifully packaged coffee beans, with attentive waiters at your service. The coffee menu is the star here. They serve over 200 types of Arabica coffee beans from around the world, sorted into single origin, flavoured, blended, and decaf. Each coffee comes with a strength rating of one to five beans, from mild to bold, so you can pick one to suit your taste.
Expect to pay: $20–$70++ per person
What to order: Black Pearl Coffee ($9++), Copacabana Coffee ($14.50++)

3. Blue Bottle Coffee – Famous coffee brand from California
World-famous NOLA iced coffee and Liege waffles at Raffles City and Paragon
What is Blue Bottle Coffee? The cult-favourite American brand that started in a San Francisco garage finally has its Singapore home, with two outlets at Raffles City and Paragon . Their must-try NOLA New Orleans-Style Iced Coffee ($8) is a crowd-pleaser—cold-brew beans steeped with roasted chicory and sweetened with cane sugar, delivering chocolatey and fruity notes in every sip. For something more classic, the Cold Brew ($7.50) is intensely flavoured with very mild astringency, while the full-bodied Latte ($8.50) pairs velvety steamed milk with a robust espresso. Non-coffee drinkers will appreciate the smooth, subtly earthy Matcha Latte ($9.50) .
For bites, their Liege Waffles ($8.50) are made fresh to order with a crisp caramelised edge and a fluffy centre. In partnership with local bakery Bakery Brera, they also offer Singapore-exclusive pastries such as the Coconut Kouign-Amann ($8) and the fragrant Pandan Canele with Kaya ($6) .
Read our Blue Bottle Coffee feature .
Expect to pay: $10–$20 per person

body:
Verandah Rooftop Rotisserie at Momentus Hotel Alexandra is running a Spanish Christmas buffet from 30 November, with lunch at S$48++ per adult and dinner at S$98++ per adult. The two menus differ by more than price: the evening sitting adds a sangria at the table, a tapas spread, king crab legs, a 21-day dry-aged wagyu rump cap and a whole suckling pig on two nights.
The restaurant sits on the hotel’s Level 7 Level 7 of the hotel at 323 Alexandra Road, with indoor seating, al fresco tables and a poolside area.
Lunch from 30 November at S$48++
The Christmas lunch buffet runs daily from 30 November 2026 to 1 January 2027, 12pm to 3pm. Adults pay S$48++ and children aged 6 to 11 pay S$24++, with children aged 5 and below eating free.
It opens with a seafood on ice counter of poached prawns, pearl conch and white clams, with cured salmon crudo, dressed with salsa rosa, nahm jim and lemon. The carving board carries a truffle and chestnut stuffed dry-aged poulet with creamy spinach and chicken gravy, and a grain mustard glazed honey baked ham with grilled pineapple and cranberry sauce. A live pasta station does linguine carbonara. The hot section covers wood-fired margherita pizza, slow-braised beef cheek, a baked whole salmon fillet, live mussels with chorizo and smoked paprika, and garlic prawns with chilli.
The Christmas lunch buffet runs 12pm to 3pm from 30 November at S$48++ per adult. Photo: Momentus Hotel Alexandra
Dessert at lunch is Spanish crema catalana, red velvet yule log and butterscotch sticky dates pudding.
Dinner from 4 December at S$98++
Dinner runs 6pm to 10pm daily from 4 December 2026 to 2 January 2027, at S$98++ per adult and S$49++ per child aged 6 to 11. Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve cost S$118++ per adult and S$59++ per child.
Every guest is welcomed at the table with a glass of Sangria de Bienvenida. The tapas spread, listed for dinner, is gambas al ajillo, blistered padron peppers, beef albondigas in romesco, tortilla espanola and a charcuterie board of jamon serrano, salchichon and chorizo. The seafood counter adds king crab legs and half shell scallops to the prawns, conch and clams.
The tapas section is dinner only: gambas al ajillo, albondigas, padron peppers and tortilla espanola. Photo: Momentus Hotel Alexandra
The carving lineup is longer. A 21-day dry-aged wagyu rump cap is seared on the hibachi grill, alongside US prime short ribs, a whole lamb leg slow-roasted at 75 degrees Celsius, citrus-brined rotisserie chicken stuffed with chorizo and herbs, crackling pork belly with anchovy butter and gammon ham glazed with honey and grain mustard. Cochinillo, the Spanish suckling pig roasted whole over charcoal and carved in front of the room, comes out only on Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve.
Cochinillo, carved whole at the table, is served only on Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve. Photo: Momentus Hotel Alexandra
Hot dishes run to a Valencian seafood paella, Galician-style turbot with garlic confit, chargrilled octopus on brussels sprouts, overnight braised wagyu beef cheeks and two wood-fired pizzas. Dinner adds snowman pavlova with wild berry compote, poached pear parfait, mini Basque cheesecakes, an artisan cheese platter, and a pink chocolate fondue fountain with churros and waffles.
Other Christmas menus near this price
Two other Christmas tables are close enough in price to compare. Tablescape at Grand Park City Hall charges S$98++ for its four-course Christmas dinner from 2 December, a seated meal rather than a buffet. Four Points by Sheraton Singapore, Riverview charges S$32.80++ per adult for its weekend Christmas brunch from 21 November, served Saturdays and Sundays only.
The Verandah lunch at S$48++ is the cheaper way onto the rooftop and keeps the ham, the salmon, the beef cheek and the dessert table. The crab legs, the wagyu, the tapas and the sangria are dinner only.
Bookings made by 30 November take 20 per cent off the food bill.
Christmas roasts to take home
The restaurant also sells a Christmas Feast at Home. Roasts are a 72-hour dry-aged rotisserie chicken stuffed with chorizo and herbs, a grain mustard glazed ham and a crackling Duroc pork porchetta, each serving five to six, and a dry-aged Angus picanha for two to three. Sides such as roast duck fat potatoes, pancetta brussels sprouts and truffle mash are S$12+ each. Orders go in at least three working days ahead, with full payment within two days of confirmation, and collection is at the restaurant between 12pm and 9pm.
Verandah Rooftop Rotisserie sits on Level 7 at 323 Alexandra Road. Photo: Momentus Hotel Alexandra
• Address: Level 7, Momentus Hotel Alexandra, 323 Alexandra Road, Singapore 159972
• Christmas lunch: 12pm to 3pm, 30 November 2026 to 1 January 2027
• Christmas dinner: 6pm to 10pm, 4 December 2026 to 2 January 2027
• Booking: Verandah Rooftop Rotisserie
summary: Verandah Rooftop Rotisserie runs a Spanish Christmas lunch at S$48++ from 30 November and dinner at S$98++ from 4 December, with cochinillo on two nights.
title: Verandah serves a Spanish Christmas buffet from 30 November

Hi friends, I’ve returned once again to share 5 brand-new eating places across Singapore that have opened recently. If you’ve been following this series (my sincere thanks), you know that I try my utmost best to include 5 vastly different destinations with differing price points to suit various budgets and occasions. And with that, I present to you my list of the 5 new hawker stalls , rosti spots and restaurants that opened in Singapore in Oct 2026 .
Warmhouse Nasi Lemak
Nestled in the blue zone of Chinatown Complex , Warmhouse Nasi Lemak is opened by Singaporean Kenneth and his Taiwanese wife, Cindy, whose dreams were to experience being hawkers in Singapore. This photographer and make-up artist couple decided to combine the food cultures of Taiwan and Singapore onto their plates of coconut rice.
I’m still salivating over the Set B Taiwanese Salt & Pepper Popcorn Chicken Nasi Lemak (S$5.50) . The mini orbs of salt and pepper chicken were plump and juicy, garnished with fried basil leaves. The fluffy coconut rice possesses a strong but not overpowering coconut flavour. The unique, flowy ramen egg won me over. I couldn’t help but wonder why nobody had thought of this pairing sooner because it was soooooo GOOD! I also adored the house-made dried shrimp-laden sambal that wasn’t so sweet and had texture. You can also try the Set A Warmhouse Nasi Lemak (S$5) that comes with chicken wing and luncheon meat.
335 Smith Street, Chinatown Complex, #02-223, Singapore 050335
Petra
Petra is the newest Mediterranean spot at Dempsey by Executive Chef Anas Shami that delivers a fresh perspective of Eastern Mediterranean dining to our shores, paying homage to the region’s culinary traditions, exuberant flavours, and the culture of gathering together to enjoy a meal. The space is romantic and even comes with a pet-friendly outdoor terrace.
Some dishes that remain etched in our memory are the house-baked Barbari w/ Sesame Seeds (S$12) paired with the Mezze Dip Trio (S$32) — hummus , marbukham and taramasalata . The Crispy Falafel (S$18) with ponzu edamame and the thin, crispy Eggplant & Zucchini Chips (S$22) served with tzatziki , saffron honey, and dukkah nuts were great. Seafood lovers will love the Chargrilled Japanese mackerel (S$56) with fennel drizzled in sumac vinaigrette , while the Chicken Shawarma Skewer (S$32) is marinated with hawaij spices and slathered with capsicum sauce.
40C Harding Road, Dempsey Road, Level 1, Singapore 249548
Hippopotato
Thank goodness for Hippopotato , a new addition to the lacklustre food scene at Punggol’s Northshore Plaza . If I’m being brutally honest, there’s hardly anything left to entice me to swing by, especially since Sixth Floor Oyster Cake and Little Caesar have vacated the mall. Hippopotato is run by a pair of brothers, who were previously making rosti as a home-based business at Tampines with raving reviews on Google . Oh, and one of them used to be an ex-chef at Marche dishing out rosti .
There are a total of 9 varieties to choose from starting with the Golden Classic Rosti (S$8) that’s served with just sour cream. The O konomirosti (S$10.50) is perfect for Japanese fans who love a touch of umami with bonito flakes, zingy okonomiyaki sauce, and Japanese mayo crowning the rosti . There’s also other decadent options like Salted Egg Chicken Schnitzel Rosti (S$12.50) and Smokin’ Salmon Rosti (S$13.50) .
407 Northshore Drive, Northshore Plaza I, #02-41 , Singapore 820407
Matsuya
60-year-old Japanese beef bowl chain, Matsuya , has stepped into Singapore’s food scene with its first Singapore outlet landing at the basement of Suntec City . The menu offerings are exactly the same as the ones in Japan, featuring a range of Rice Bowls , Unagi , Japanese curry , as well as Hamburg .
If you’re clueless on what to order, the classic Gyumeshi Beef Bowl (S$5.50 for small) is a good introduction. Enjoy tasty beef slices coupled with sweet onions over fluffy Japanese rice — it doesn’t get more comforting than that. Those with larger appetites can check out their other sizes — from Medium (S$5.90) to Double (S$10.90) . My personal recommendation would be the Gyumeshi topped w/ Green Onion & Mentaiko Mayonnaise (S$8.50 for small) . The combination of spring onions, creamy mentaiko , beef slices, and seaweed had multi layers of flavour that danced in my mouth. Remember to add a Soft-Boiled Egg (+S$1.50) to hit that sweet spot!
3 Temasek Boulevard, Suntec City Mall, #B1-149/149A, Singapore 038983
OVER
…
summary: Singapore’s October 2026 food openings span five new eateries, from Taiwanese-inspired nasi lemak at Chinatown Complex and Mediterranean dining in Dempsey to rosti at Northshore Plaza, Japanese beef bowls at Suntec City and oversized Asian fusion dishes at Tras Street. With options ranging from S$5 hawker meals to restaurant dining and group-sized food challenges, the selection suits different budgets and occasions.
title: October 2026: 5 new hawker stalls, rosti takeaway spots & restaurants in Singapore
