Sentosa’s autonomous vehicle shuttle service
Judging by how some drivers behave on the road and the countless complaints on the Roads.sg Facebook page, you might think that letting a bus drive itself would be an accident waiting to happen. But autonomous vehicles are already plying the roads in Punggol , and they might soon become a regular sight on our roads.
In fact, you won’t have to wait long to see another one in action. Sentosa is set to welcome a driverless shuttle service that ferries passengers between hotels, beaches, and attractions across the island.
Ahead of the service’s public pilot in early 2027 , we got a sneak peek at the shuttle in action to see what it’s like to have a bus take the “wheel”, quite literally.
What are autonomous vehicles?
An autonomous vehicle is a driverless , electric shuttle equipped with 360° sensors and self-driving technology . These allow it to detect its surroundings and navigate roads independently, without the need for a human driver.
Autonomous vehicles are becoming an increasingly important part of Singapore’s long-term public transport strategy. In September 2025, Punggol introduced autonomous shuttles as part of its public transport network, with feedback collected showing most riders felt safe onboard and would recommend the service to others.
Now, the driverless bus service is rolling into sunny Sentosa. Developed by Guangzhou-based autonomous technology company WeRide in partnership with Sentosa Development Corporation (SDC) and TADA, the shuttle has received the green light to begin pilot rides following extensive testing and safety assessments.
What route does Sentosa’s autonomous vehicles take?
The 1st pilot phase, when the service launches in early 2027, will cover western Sentosa, including Siloso Beach and Palawan Beach , with 21 Planned Pick-up & Drop-off (PUDO) points . The on-demand service allows the shuttle to skip certain PUDO points along its predetermined routes based on passenger needs.
The 2nd phase will extend the service to eastern Sentosa, connecting Tanjong Beach to Sentosa Cove and bringing the total number of PUDO points to 27 . Details on this will be announced at a later date, subject to regulatory approval from the Land Transport Authority (LTA).
Here is the full list of PUDO points for the Western phase:
1. Beach Station (In front of The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf)
2. Palawan Kidz City
3. Equarius Hotel
4. Hotel Ora
5. Hotel Michael / Crockfords Tower
6. The Laurus Singapore
7. Village Hotel Sentosa / The Barracks Hotel Sentosa
8. Oasia Resort Sentosa
9. Capella Singapore
10. Palawan Beach (In front of FOC by the Beach)
11. In front of the Southernmost Point of Continental Asia
12. The Palawan @ Sentosa
13. Siloso Point (Beachfront)
14. Mega Adventure Park
15. Siloso Beach Resort
16. Ola Beach Club
17. Coastes / Skyline Luge Singapore
18. Amara Sanctuary Sentosa
19. Shangri-La Rasa Sentosa (Planned for mid-2027)
20. Siloso Point (Planned for mid-2027)
21. Imbiah Lookout (Planned for mid-2027)
How do I book a ride on the Sentosa autonomous vehicles?
Booking a ride on the shuttle can be done through the TADA app ( App Store | Google Play ), though the feature isn’t available just yet. However, we did get a sneak peek at how the booking process works.
Once you’re at a pick-up point, look out for the PUDO signboard. Simply open the TADA app, select your pick-up and drop-off points, then follow the on-screen steps to book your ride.
During the pilot phase, only 2 vehicles will be in operation, running daily from 1pm to 7pm . The good news is that all rides will be free during the pilot, with payment options for the future still under consideration.
What’s the entire Sentosa autonomous shuttle experience like?
Boarding the autonomous shuttle
Our ride started at Beach Station, serving as a convenient alternative for getting to Sentosa’s beaches without the long walk or wait for the tram.
Before boarding, check that the shuttle ID matches the one shown on your TADA app .
Once onboard, scan the QR code to confirm your ride, buckle up, and stay seated throughout the journey. Eating and drinking aren’t allowed, so save your beachside snacks for later!
It can seat around 8 passengers , but the vehicle felt surprisingly spacious for its size, with enough room to stretch our legs without feeling cramped.
Safety features of the autonomous vehicle
One of the first things we noticed was the array of sensors and 360° cameras fitted around the shuttle. Like everyone else, you were wondering whether it’s safe, but riding onboard gave us a firsthand look at how the bus navigates its surroundings.
An onboard screen offers a closer look at this process, visualising what the vehicle detects along the way. Nearby vehicles, pedestrians, and buildings are mapped out on the display, giving passengers a glimpse of how the bus reads its surroundings as it makes its way around Sentosa.
…
summary: Bookings can be made via the TADA app.
title: We Got To Ride Sentosa’s Self-Driving Shuttle Service Before It Launches In 2027 & Here’s What It’s Like

body:
SAFRA Punggol’s River of Life kayak tour
When we think of kayaking in Singapore , the first place that comes to mind is usually The Kallang’s Water Sports Centre. But what if I told you there’s a more unconventional spot where you can explore a longer stretch of water while getting closer to nature?
That’s where SAFRA Punggol’s River of Life kayak tour comes in. Spanning 5km to 6km along Punggol Waterway , the tour takes you past heartland architecture and lush greenery, with plenty of opportunities to spot wildlife along the way.
It’s a fun way to spend the weekend with the family or switch up the usual date with a little outdoor adventure, so here’s everything you need to know about the kayaking tour.
What is the River of Life kayak tour?
Image credit: Fever.sg via Facebook
Organised in collaboration with Fever Kayak Adventures, the River of Life experience lets you explore Punggol’s waterways and scenic sights at a leisurely pace.
You’ll be using a Hobie Mirage Drive kayak , which uses underwater fins powered by foot pedals to propel you forward, much like riding a bicycle. This takes the strain off your arms and leaves them free to snap photos of the scenery.
Image credit: Fever.sg via Facebook
The tour is beginner-friendly, so you don’t need any prior kayaking experience to join. You can choose between a single-seater kayak or a double-seater , with life jackets provided for all participants.
Certified instructors will also kayak alongside the group throughout the tour to guide you along the way. Each participant also gets a VHF walkie-talkie radio to hear live commentary on Punggol’s history and local wildlife.
Keep your eyes peeled as you pedal, as your guides will point out interesting sights and critters along the route.
What can I see on the tour?
Your kayaking adventure begins at SAFRA Punggol . Make your way to the floating pier and spot Fever’s bright yellow and orange kayaks waiting by the water. The guides will provide your safety equipment and run through a safety briefing before you hit the water.
Iconic architectural landmarks in Punggol
Image credit: L via Google Maps
One of the first landmarks you’ll spot along the route is the Adventure Bridge , a pedestrian suspension bridge in Punggol Waterway Park designed with wood-inspired steel frames. From water level, you’ll get a closer look at its rustic, timber-like understructure as you glide beneath it.
Image credit: Fever.sg via Facebook
Keep your cameras ready as Waterway Point comes into view, with the mall’s modern architecture forming a scenic backdrop along the waterway. Take the opportunity to snap some group photos with the mall in the background before pedalling on to the next stretch.
Image credit: @safrapunggol via Instagram
Another landmark to look out for midway through the journey is Jewel Bridge , which stands out with its distinctive dome-shaped structure. Its unique design makes it another great spot to snap a few photos as you pedal past.
Image credit: Fever.sg via Facebook
We won’t spoil all the sights just yet, but expect to pass plenty of scenic bridges, waterfront views, and familiar landmarks along the way. The loop route lets you explore a good stretch of Punggol’s waterways before pedalling back to SAFRA Punggol.
Spot plants & wildlife, including resident otters
Image credit: Fever.sg via Facebook
Beyond the buildings, look out for wildlife such as butterflies , dragonflies , and the occasional monitor lizard hiding among the greenery. The waterway is also home to over 100 bird species , including local and migratory varieties, making it a great spot for wildlife enthusiasts.
Along the way, your guides will share fun facts about native plants and herbs commonly used in local cuisine. Keep an eye out for wild pandan and lemongrass , which are used in local favourites such as pandan chiffon cake and nasi lemak.
Image credit: Kam-Yung Soh via Facebook
One of the tour’s highlights is spotting Punggol’s resident otter family as you pedal along the waterways. These playful smooth-coated otters call the area home, so you might spot them swimming by or splashing around in the water.
What do I need to bring for the tour?
Image credit: @safrapunggol via Instagram
While the kayaks are suitable for seniors and families, participants must be at least 5 years old . Children aged 5 to 12 must share a tandem kayak with an accompanying adult.
Make sure to wear covered water shoes or strapped sandals for the trip. Don’t forget your sun and bug protection, including sunscreen , sunglasses , a hat , and insect repellent . Bring along a water bottle too to stay hydrated throughout.
How can I book a River of Life tour?
Prices start from $49.90 per kayaker, and bookings are available through Fever’s website or platforms like Klook and GetYourGuide . Each session lasts about 2 hours , with 2 morning slots available each day: 7.30am to 9.30am and 10am to 12pm .
Explore Punggol’s waterways with the River of Life experience
…
summary: Rather than using paddles, you’ll use foot pedals on their kayaks to propel yourself forward.
title: You Can Kayak Through Punggol On A Guided Tour To Explore The Waterways & Spot Wildlife

body:
Tarot reading vending machine at Sunshine Plaza
We’re no strangers to unique vending machines scattered around Singapore, dispensing everything from fully cooked meals to EZ-Link charms . Among these quirky finds is a tarot reading vending machine located at Sunshine Plaza , offered by fortune-telling consultancy Destiny Wealth Crafter.
If you’re curious about what the cards have in store for you, this is a pretty unconventional way to seek some spiritual guidance without booking a face-to-face session with a tarot reader. We tried it out ourselves to see how it works and if its readings resonated with us.
What to know about the tarot reading vending machine
Those familiar with Singapore’s tarot scene might have come across Destiny Wealth Crafter , known online for its well-reviewed tarot and numerology services , as well as workshops for aspiring fortune tellers . To make tarot readings more accessible, the consultancy introduced a tarot vending machine that lets passers-by get a reading while on the go.
Located a 3-minute walk from Bencoolen MRT Station , the vending machine is just around the corner from Destiny Wealth Crafter’s Sunshine Plaza outlet. It operates 24/7 and is entirely self-service , with each reading priced at $4.99 and taking less than 5 minutes to complete.
How do I use the tarot reading vending machine?
1. Choose a topic you need guidance on
Before your reading begins, choose a topic for the cards to focus on. Pick between love , career , wealth , and health depending on which area you’d like some insight into.
2. Type in the burning question you want answered
Next, enter a question related to your chosen topic , with a limit of 120 words , to help guide your reading. If nothing comes to mind, you can also select 1 of the suggested questions given to you by the virtual tarot reader.
P.S. Keep it to 1 question per reading , as multiple questions may result in less accurate readings according to the machine.
3. Shuffle the deck & pick out 3 cards
Tap on the screen to shuffle the deck, then pick out 3 tarot cards to get your reading. Once they’re laid out, tap on each card to reveal what’s hidden beneath.
BTW, you’ll need to make your payment before revealing what’s under the 3rd card. The vending machine only accepts cashless payments , so make sure to have your card or e-wallet ready.
4. Collect your tarot reading
After revealing the 3 tarot cards, the machine will generate its interpretation of what each card means and what you should do moving forward. It’ll print out your reading for you to bring home, with the choice of having a copy sent to your email for easy reference as well.
Are the readings accurate?
So, how accurate are the readings from this tarot vending machine? To put it simply, don’t expect it to predict your future . When we asked about health and how to better support our current wellbeing, the reading came back fairly generic.
It advised us to spend more time outdoors, accept more acts of support from others, and let go of unnecessary stress. Though it did surface some sensible points for self-reflection, the advice felt more like general wellness tips rather than anything particularly personal.
The machine is a fun novelty to try out given its low price ; it’s not every day you get your fortune told by a metal box, after all. Just remember to take the reading with a grain of salt, as it’s ultimately open to your own interpretation. If the experience did pique your interest in cartomancy, you can consider heading over to the Destiny Wealth Crafter outlet nearby to find out more.
What else does the vending machine dispense?
Beyond the readings, it also doubles as a blind box vending machine. Before your reading is printed out, you can opt to buy a Crystal Energy Blind Box that corresponds with your chosen topic, containing a trinket or crystal that’ll amplify the energy behind your reading.
Each blind box is priced at $29.90 , but you can get 1 for $19.90 when purchasing it with a tarot reading.
Gain a new perspective with the tarot reading vending machine
It may not tell you your future, but this tarot vending machine is a decent excuse to slow down and reflect on what’s actually on your mind. If you’re around Sunshine Plaza, give this unusual vending machine a go; you might even walk away with a fresh idea on what to manifest next.
For more unique experiences around Singapore:
• Scentphony: perfume vending machine
• DIY pocket watch workshop
• BUZZATTACK: interactive gameshow experience
Photography by Wong Kai Bin.
summary: We tried this tarot reading vending machine to see if the results are accurate.
title: We Tried A $4.99 Tarot Reading Vending Machine In SG To See If The Results Are Accurate

body:
Yo-Chi, Messina & Mixue vouchers at blood banks in Singapore
2026 is flying by, and if your New Year’s resolutions are still sitting on your Notes app untouched, there’s still time to tick something off the list. For those who have no idea where to begin, why not start by donating blood? It’s a simple way to do some good and help save lives.
Plus, you can score vouchers from Yo-Chi , Messina , and Mixue when you donate blood at participating blood banks in Singapore as part of the Not All Pints Are Equal campaign. Here’s how.
Donate blood at 1 of the 5 blood banks in Singapore
Image credit: Michael Chia via Google Maps
From 2nd November to 6th December 2026 , you’ll earn a voucher for a sweet treat when you donate blood at any of the 5 participating blood banks in Singapore.
Here are the 5 locations:
• Bloodbank@HSA
• Bloodbank@Dhoby Ghaut
• Bloodbank@Westgate Tower
• Bloodbank@One Punggol
• Bloodbank@Woodlands
Book your appointment according to the sweet treat you want
Image credit: Eatbook
Remember to book an appointment online before heading down. But something to take note of is that the vouchers are available during different periods , so you’ll want to time your blood donation according to the treat you’re eyeing.
Image credit: Messina via Google Maps
Here’s when you can snag each voucher:
Date
Voucher
2nd-15th Nov 2026
$5 Mixue discount voucher
16th-26th Nov 2026
Voucher for a free extra scoop of ice cream at Messina
27th Nov-6th Dec 2026
$5 Yo-Chi discount voucher
Remember to flash the campaign page or campaign-related visuals to be eligible
View this post on Instagram
Don’t forget to show the Not All Pints Are Equal campaign page or the campaign’s Instagram post to the staff at the registration counter when you arrive for your appointment.
This is an important step if you want to walk away with your voucher, as staff won’t prompt you about the promotion. You’ll have to flash the campaign visuals before your blood donation procedure begins to qualify.
Celebrate doing a good deed with a silent disco
Image credit: Singapore Red Cross Society
There’s more to look forward to after rolling up your sleeves. Pints & Beats is a 1-day silent disco specially organised for blood donors, happening at Another Bar on 6th December 2026 , from 2pm to 6pm .
It’s essentially a daytime party for donors to celebrate doing a good deed, with fun activities lined up. To be eligible, you’ll need to have successfully donated blood between 1st July and 30th November 2026 .
There are 2 ways to register your interest:
• Those who donated before 2nd November will receive an email by 9th November inviting you to register your interest. Take note that this is only for sign-ups and isn’t your event access confirmation.
• Those who just donated can look out for the QR code on the tent cards at any refreshment area in the blood banks and scan it to register your interest.
Successful applicants will receive a separate confirmation email by 4th December 2026 , with access details for themselves and a plus-one.
Image for illustrative purposes only.
Image credit: @mixuesyd via Instagram
As for what’s in store, expect free Mixue drinks, photo spots, a custom T-shirt station, and hourly sure-win lucky draws. There’s also a grand draw featuring 3 prizes, including a staycation!
Book your blood donation appointment soon
Image credit: @xt_lee via Instagram
If it’s your first time donating blood and you’re feeling anxious, check out our guide to donating blood in Singapore for everything you need to know before heading down.
Also, we can’t stress this enough: book your appointment early and remember to flash the campaign visuals at the registration counter before donating, or you might just miss out on your sweet treat voucher!
Find out more about the Not All Pints Are Equal campaign

If trimming the guest list is one of the first things on your wedding agenda, you’re in luck. Some of the best small wedding venues in Singapore prove that fewer guests doesn’t have to mean fewer bells and whistles. In fact, swapping a cavernous ballroom for a private dining room, rooftop or garden can make it much easier to actually spend time with everyone you invited.
We’ve done the venue scouting for you, with options for proper micro weddings of 25 or 30 guests, celebrations around the 50-person mark and slightly larger receptions that still feel personal. So if you’re hunting for small wedding venues for 50 to 100 guests in Singapore, consider this your shortlist. Or, peep our list of larger wedding venues in Singapore for more full-on celebrations.
1. Four Seasons Hotel Singapore
Photography: Four Seasons Hotel Singapore
For a five-star hotel wedding minus the sprawling ballroom, head straight for the top floor of Four Seasons Hotel Singapore. Windows East and Windows West sit on level 20, two elegant and intimate wedding venues with floor-to-ceiling windows boasting sweeping city views. Both also come with a private outdoor patio – a nice little change of scene for pre-dinner drinks and photos.
Each 101-square metre (1,087-square foot) venue accommodates up to 100 guests, with banquet seating for 60, and receptions for 80. Curate an individually plated six-course lunch or seven-course dinner from Michelin-selected Jiang-Nan Chun, including its signature mesquite wood-roasted Peking duck. Floral arrangements, wedding favours, and a one-night stay are included in the package, too.
For those who prefer their celebrations more convivial, Nobu, Jiang Nan-Chun and One-Ninety Restaurant also offer buy-out options for small weddings and solemnisation ceremonies in Singapore.
Best for: An intimate five-star hotel wedding with city views
Capacity: Up to 100 pax at Windows East and Windows West (60 pax for banquet, 80 pax for receptions). Up to 130 pax at Nobu; up to 120 pax at Jiang Nan-Chun; up to 80 pax at One-Ninety Restaurant
Price: From $238++ per pax for Windows East and Windows West, from $7000 for restaurant buy-outs
Address: Four Seasons Hotel Singapore , 190 Orchard Boulevard, Singapore 248646
2. Flutes
Photography: Flutes
If your idea of a wedding reception looks more like an elegant dinner party than a traditional banquet, bookmark Flutes. The longstanding fine-dining restaurant has moved into Midtown House on Beach Road, where its current home pairs heritage architecture with polished dining rooms and private spaces. Weddings can take the form of a solemnisation, lunch or dinner, with this small wedding venue in Singapore accommodating up to 90 guests.
The beauty here is that you don’t necessarily have to take over the entire restaurant. Flutes specifically offers smaller private-room and designated-area configurations for more intimate receptions, making it suitable for couples who would rather spend the evening over good food and wine than build an elaborate wedding programme around a ballroom stage.
Best for: An elegant restaurant wedding centred around food and wine
Capacity: Up to 90 pax
Price: From $236.10 per pax
Address: Flutes , 120 Beach Road, #01-02 Midtown House, Singapore 189769
3. The Summerhouse
Photography: The Summerhouse
Ballroom carpets and chandeliers not up your street? Take the party outside. The Summerhouse in Seletar is built around a heritage house and leafy grounds, giving couples a mix of indoor and outdoor spaces. We’d consider this for a late-afternoon ceremony, especially if greenery features heavily on your Pinterest board.
For a verdant small wedding venue in Singapore, the garden solemnisation is set up for 50 guests, while the courtyard accommodates up to 80. You can then move indoors for the meal, and useful wedding-day basics such as a bridal room, sound system, projector and microphones are available too.
Best for: A romantic and lush garden wedding
Capacity: Up to 50 pax for a garden solemnisation; up to 80 pax in the courtyard
Price: Enquire for a quote
Address: The Summerhouse , 3 Park Lane, Singapore 798387
4. Vineyard at Hortpark
Photography: Vineyard at Hortpark
Garden wedding dreams, Singapore humidity concerns – we hear you. Vineyard at HortPark gives you several ways to stage the perfect small wedding in Singapore. The outdoor patio works for vows and pre-dinner drinks, while the verandah keeps the greenery within your photo ops but adds air-conditioning. The latter seats up to 60 guests, while the indoor dining hall accommodates 86.

Things to do at Jewel Changi Airport
Jewel Changi Airport needs no introduction. Locals and visitors flock over in droves for that million-dollar shot with the famous Rain Vortex in the background. And not to mention, the mall is chock-full of delish grub, tempting stores, lush greenery, and of course, attractions that can keep you entertained for hours.
Trust us when we say – there’s a lot to cover. So here’s a comprehensive guide to all you can do at Jewel Changi Airport .
– Indoor garden spaces –
We don’t flaunt our Garden City status for nothing, and it only makes sense that one of the first few places tourists set foot in upon reaching Singapore reflects that reputation. Like all terminals in the airport, Jewel Changi is full of green spaces for that extra calming aura.
1. Rain Vortex
Be mesmerised by the tallest indoor waterfall in the world
Your Skytrain might cruise through this area, depending on which terminal you’re headed to.
Perhaps the most prominent green feature of Jewel Changi is its Forest Valley , which is stacked with trellis upon trellis of different trees and shrubs. And right at the centre of it all is the massive Rain Vortex , the tallest indoor waterfall in the world. The falls rain down 40m from Level 5 all the way to B1, and despite being artificial, it’s a sight to behold nonetheless.
Image credit: @blackminusgreen via Instagram
Come night, and you’ll be treated to a magical light-and-sound show, with rainbow-coloured animations projected on the wall of water itself. The Rain Vortex light show happens at 8pm and 9pm from Monday to Thursday, and at 8pm, 9pm, and 10pm from Friday to Sunday and on public holidays.
Occasionally, there’ll also be special, themed light shows based on big events happening on the Little Red Dot. A Disney Cruise one recently played here earlier this year, and December will see a BTS-themed takeover of the man-made marvel.
Note: The floor surrounding the Rain Vortex is usually wet due to the mist, so be careful not to slip and fall.
2. Forest Valley
Indoor “forest” decorated with over 900 trees & 60,000 shrubs
For a better view of the gorgeous Rain Vortex, you can climb up the Forest Valley stairs to reach an ideal vantage point. As you ascend surrounded by shrubbery and smaller water features, you’ll feel as though you’re taking a hike outdoors – minus the humid weather. Yup, you don’t have to worry about breaking a sweat here as temperatures are a comfortable 23°C.
To best enjoy the walking trails, it is advisable to wear comfortable flat shoes instead of heels as there are numerous steps to climb.
The entire Forest Valley is full of lush, leafy backdrops. Look out for the mini bamboo grove on the lowest floor of the Valley, where you can snap pics to bluff your friends that you’re in Japan .
– Canopy Park –
The top floor of Jewel Changi is where you’ll find the Canopy Park , which is less of a park and more of a giant playground that both kids and adults will find thrilling. Think bouncy nets to play on, flower gardens to walk through, and even mazes to get lost in.
Do note that general admission into the Canopy Park is from $6/pax for Singapore Residents and $8 for everyone else, and covers only the Discovery Slides, Foggy Bowls, Petal Garden, and Topiary Walk. The rest of the attractions have a separate charge, which includes admission to Canopy Park as well.

body:
Bukit Panjang finally has its own Sushiro. The Japanese conveyor-belt chain’s newest outlet sits on the second floor of Bukit Panjang Plaza, and it comes with two weeks of 1-for-1 sushi and S$6++ drinks to pull in the neighbourhood. If you live in the north-west and have been taking the bus to Lot One in Choa Chu Kang or Causeway Point in Woodlands for your salmon plates, this one is for you.
The grand opening deals run from 30 October to 12 November. Image: Sushiro Singapore
What the grand opening deals cover
The opening promotion runs from 30 October to 12 November. Sushi goes 1-for-1, and the second portion arrives on the same plate rather than as a separate plate on the belt, so one plate carries double the sushi. Ask the staff which plates are in the deal on the day you go.
Three drinks drop to S$6++ each for the same two weeks:
• Lemon sour, usually S$8++
• Suntory The Premium Malt’s draught beer, usually S$10.50++
• Kaku highball, usually S$9++
The sure-win gachapon for diners spending S$50 or more was an opening-day special on 30 October only, so that one has come and gone.
The second part of Sushiro’s October limited menu runs until 3 November. Image: Sushiro Singapore
The limited menu running alongside
Bukit Panjang opens in the middle of the second part of Sushiro’s October limited menu, which runs at every outlet until 3 November while stocks last. The headline plates are the Miyako salmon trout taste and compare from Japan’s Sanriku Rias coast at S$2.90++ and a fatty swordfish at S$2.90++.
The rest of the line-up leans on soy sauce koji, a fermented seasoning of soy sauce and koji, across four fish:
• Soy sauce koji fresh salmon, S$2.90++
• Soy sauce koji engawa, S$2.30++
• Soy sauce koji yellowtail, S$3.90++
• Soy sauce koji red snapper, S$4.90++
Pufferfish fans get two fugu plates at S$4.90++ each, and the bancha braised octopus uses Hokkaido mizudako at S$3.90++. Prices differ at the Digiro outlet in Mandai Wildlife Reserve.

body:
A barista at a plant milk booth during the 2025 edition of Singapore Coffee Week. Photo: Singapore Coffee Week
Singapore Coffee Week returns for its third edition from 5 to 8 November, filling Hall C on Level 1 of Sands Expo and Convention Centre from 10am to 8pm daily. Entry is free and you can simply walk in. Before the doors open, public voting for the Singapore People’s Choice Café Award of the Year 2026 starts tomorrow, 1 November, at 10am.
The event is run by the Singapore Coffee Association, the trade body for the local coffee industry. Its members span coffee traders, roasters, café owners, equipment suppliers and baristas.
How the café vote works
Café entries closed on 20 October, and approved cafés sit on the Singapore Café Map and the official voting platform. Each person gets one ballot tied to a verified Singapore mobile number and can pick up to three different café brands, with each pick counting as one equal vote.
• Online voting runs from 1 November, 10am, to 8 November, 6pm.
• Onsite voting at Sands Expo runs from 10am to 8pm on 5 to 7 November, and from 10am to 6pm on 8 November.
• Cafés are not allowed to offer payments, gifts or discounts in exchange for votes.
The café with the highest verified total is named the Singapore People’s Choice Café Winner of the Year 2026 and gets a trophy, a certificate, a digital badge and a free individual booth at the 2027 edition. The rest of the top ten receive a trophy or certificate and a counter in a shared café pavilion next year.
The interactive coffee map traces coffee’s journey around the world and into Singapore. Photo: Singapore Coffee Week
What you can do in Hall C
The Bean Discovery Bar gathers beans from different roasters in one spot, so it suits anyone hunting for a new bag to brew at home. An interactive coffee map traces how coffee spread around the world and how Singapore built its own coffee habits, with trivia along the way.
Sip and Stamp is a coffee discovery trail, and finishing selected activities earns a turn at Spin and Win for coffee goodies and merchandise. There is also a Golden Bean Hunt for 24K golden beans worth S$10,000 in total. Collect any eight stickers on the pre-event Café Hopping Adventure and you receive a location hint for the hunt.
An oat milk exhibitor booth at Singapore Coffee Week 2025. Photo: Singapore Coffee Week
Exhibitors include A.muse Tea and Co, Addison Institute, Asia Supply Trading, Balance Coffee, Baristart Coffee and Bettr.
Competitions on the floor
Teams in the Singapore Coffee Roasting Team Championship 2026 compete through roasting, cup tasting and voting for a chance to represent Singapore at the ASEAN Coffee Roasting Championship 2027. The Singapore Home Roasting Championship also runs during the four days.
Roasting teams compete through roasting, cup tasting and voting for a place at the ASEAN Coffee Roasting Championship 2027. Photo: Singapore Coffee Week
The Singapore Fashion Drinks Competition takes place on 5 and 6 November, and its top three go on to the 2027 World Fashion Drinks Competition at HOTELEX Shanghai. People’s Choice winners are named on the association’s and the event’s social media channels on 8 November, once the votes are verified.
summary: Singapore Coffee Week takes over Sands Expo Hall C from 5 to 8 November with free entry, and People's Choice café voting opens on 1 November at 10am.
title: Singapore Coffee Week returns to Sands Expo from 5 to 8 November, with café voting open from 1 November

body:
McDonald’s and Pokémon fans, here’s something to look forward to: the Pokémon Happy Meal collaboration is heading to Singapore and Malaysia in December 2026 , following its US launch on 10 Nov .
Credit – @HuinGuillaume via X (formerly Twitter)
The collection is said to feature 15 collectible mini box toys and 15 Pokémon trading cards . Each mini box is designed around a different Pokémon , including familiar favourites such as Pikachu, Eevee, Charmander, Bulbasaur, Umbreon and Piplup, alongside other recognisable characters.
Credit – @ModernNotoriety & @HuinGuillaume via X (formerly Twitter)
The mini boxes are arguably one of the more interesting parts of the collection. They can reportedly be turned into little charms that you can clip onto your keys, bags or even your trousers.
I don’t know about you, but the idea of having a tiny Pokémon companion from a Happy Meal tagging along on everyday errands, rather than leaving the collectibles at home is actually quite genius!
Credit – @pokehuntdotfun via X (formerly Twitter)
As for the trading cards , leaked photos suggest that the collection could include 15 designs , 7 of which feature a holofoil finish . The alleged line-up includes Jirachi, Tyranitar, Absol, Decidueye, Hawlucha, Pikachu, Palafin, Lucario, Snorlax, Eevee, Metagross, Mimikyu, Chandelure and Wooloo.
However, some reports have listed only 14 stamped cards , so the final selection remains unclear .
Each Happy Meal is also reportedly expected to include 2 Pokémon trading cards , though this detail has yet to be confirmed for Singapore and Malaysia.
The meals may come in special Pokémon-themed packaging , too, with 3 reported box designs featuring Pikachu, Umbreon and Torchic. The exact selection of toys and cards, as well as how they will be distributed, could vary by market.
The McDonald’s x Pokémon collaboration is expected to reach Singapore and Malaysia in Dec 2026, though local prices, exact launch dates and the final selection of toys and cards have yet to be confirmed.
For now, I’m curious to see which Pokémon make it into the local collection, especially if the mini box charms turn out to be as adorable as they sound (and practical, of course)!
Batam’s new waterfront resort Opus Bay opens this December, just 45 minutes from Singapore
summary: McDonald’s Pokémon Happy Meal collaboration is expected to arrive in Singapore and Malaysia in December 2026, featuring 15 collectible mini box toys and a reported selection of 15 trading cards. Pokémon fans can look forward to clip-on box charms and possible holofoil cards, although local prices, launch dates, final designs and distribution details remain unconfirmed.
title: McDonald’s x Pokémon Happy Meal with mini box charms & trading cards coming to Singapore & Malaysia

It’s finally Nov, with just 2 more months left before the year comes to an end. As the festive season draws closer, there’s plenty to explore around Singapore . From fitness competitions to a relaxed evening with orchestral music, the possibilities are endless.
If you’re wondering how to have a fun time in Nov 2026, here are 11 of the best things to do in Singapore during this month.
How I chose these best things to do in Nov 2026
These are the 3 main criteria I used to decide which activities to recommend:
• Variety : The activities on this list cater to a range of interests, from sports to arts & culture.
• Wide price range : From paid events to free events, there’s something for every budget.
• Accessibility : I included events located in different parts of Singapore so you can pick the one most convenient for you.
I have also grouped them into 3 different categories, so you can find what suits you best.
• Activities & Wellness
• Food & Beverages
• Arts & Culture
This isn’t a ranked best-to-worst things-to-do list, but a collection of the most enjoyable activities overall, in no particular order. Get ready to head out to have fun before the year inevitably ends!

1. AIA HYROX Singapore 2026 (26 – 29 Nov 2026)
Credit – HYROX Singapore via Facebook
Ready to put your strength and stamina to the test before the year ends? AIA HYROX Singapore 2026 returns from 26 to 29 Nov 2026 , bringing 4 days of high-energy fitness competition to our red dot. You can expect an accessible and inclusive fitness movement that remains challenging at HYROX. If you’re 16 years or older and prepared, you can take on HYROX as a challenge. Fun fact: their oldest contestant to date is 73 years old — wow!
There are 2 divisions in HYROX: Pro (for seasoned athletes seeking maximum intensity) and Open (for those wanting something a little more accessible). Each participant takes on an 8km run , broken up by 8 workout stations that include exercises such as sled pulls, sled push, burpee broad jumps and more.
If the thought of tackling the course solo in HYROX Open/Pro sounds intimidating, sign up for HYROX Doubles/Doubles Pro with a friend. Alternatively, you can find 3 friends and take on HYROX Relay , with each member completing part of the course. Younger fitness enthusiasts aged 8 to 15 years old can also look out for HYROX Youngstars , happening on 28 and 29 Nov 2026 .

Fans of marine life are in luck: Resorts World Sentosa has introduced PADI Discover Snorkelling at Singapore Oceanarium . Guests aged 10 years and abov e can now take part in Singapore’s only snorkelling experience and see a range of marine animals up close. This experience costs S$109 per person and includes a 1-day admission ticket to the Singapore Oceanarium, so you can have plenty more fun exploring after the snorkelling session ends.
You can expect to see manta rays , sharks and thousands of other animals from the surface of the iconic Open Ocean habitat. The experience will last 90 minutes and is designed with beginners in mind — no prior swimming, snorkelling or diving experience is required before you sign up.

Ask anyone from the Hou- gang (please tell me you get it) for the best porridge place and they’ll probably exclaim Sin Heng Kee Porridge in a heartbeat. The corner stall along Hougang Street 61 is renowned for its thick and hearty porridge bowls, and warmed tummies and souls since childhood days.
I thought I’d find out for myself what the hype was all about and rocked up to the bustlin’ store at 7am, just as they opened. Of course, there was no issue getting a seat but I was pleasantly surprised at the snaking queue to place dine-in and takeaway orders. Mind you, this was minutes after they just opened for the day!
What I tried at Sin Heng Kee Porridge
My ultimate favourite combination that I order everywhere I go is Century Egg and Meatball Porridge (S$6) . Given it was my first meal of the day, I thought I’d add an Egg (additional S$0.50) and You Tiao (+S$1.20) for that extra protein and energy.
Plus, I love how the colours come together so beautifully. Had to snap one for the ‘gram before I dug in.
As talk of the town, I’ll admit that I had high expectations for Sin Heng Kee. As I dived into my first spoonful with a little bit of everything, it surprised me that the flavours didn’t quite take me on a gastronomical ride.
The sharpness of the century egg and ginger didn’t quite cut through as I’d hoped for it to. Sin Heng Kee’s handmade meatballs were small and pretty much hidden in the huge bowl but just like its appearance, it was so-so.
Ye Lai Xiang Teochew Porridge: Your taxi uncle’s fave Teochew Mui, open till 4am
Of course, fried dough sticks are an absolute must. A great complement that gave the dish another dimension with its crisp texture. However, the thick gruel lacked a savouriness that perhaps could be alleviated with more soy sauce.
I also gave the seafood series a go with the Cuttlefish & Peanut Porridge (S$6) . If there’s one thing to count on at Sin Heng Kee Porridge, it’s their wide variety of porridge. I’m talking over 15 combinations!
While the large slices of ginger was a promising sign to me, the cuttlefish slices paired together with the peanuts as stars of the show, fell short of delivering a powerful combination. Rather, it was a tad too fishy for my liking. Altogether, not the biggest fan of the series but this might just appeal to lovers of seafood porridge.
Final thoughts
Overall, decent bowls that looked better than they tasted. Perhaps I should’ve given the Signature Porridge (S$7.50) a try, given that it’s loaded with century egg, sliced pork, meatballs, liver, intestines, cuttlefish, sliced fish, and minced chicken. Personally, Chai Chee Pork Porridge sets the bar when it comes to hearty, savoury porridge and handmade meatballs.
If you’ve yet to visit Sin Heng Kee before, I’d highly recommend visiting once to play judge to Hougang’s pride and joy.

summary: Sin Heng Kee Porridge along Hougang Street 61 serves over 15 porridge combinations, including century egg and meatball, and cuttlefish with peanut. The thick, generous portions and affordability may appeal to Hougang residents and comfort-food seekers, though the flavours vary in depth, making some bowls more satisfying than others.
title: Sin Heng Kee Porridge: Generous and value-for-money, but looks better than it tastes
